treks.title: Everest Base Camp Wellness Trek – 14 Days
treks.description:
The Everest Base Camp Wellness Trek – 14 Days combines one of the world's most iconic trekking adventures with a carefully designed wellness experience. This unique journey allows you to explore the breathtaking landscapes of the Khumbu region while nurturing your physical and mental well-being through daily yoga, guided meditation, breathing techniques, and mindful trekking practices.

Starting with a scenic mountain flight to Lukla, you'll trek through picturesque Sherpa villages, ancient Buddhist monasteries, suspension bridges, alpine forests, and glacier valleys before reaching the legendary Everest Base Camp (5,364m). Along the way, wellness sessions are thoughtfully integrated into the itinerary to help improve flexibility, support acclimatization, relieve muscle fatigue, and promote relaxation after each day's hike.

Witness spectacular views of Mount Everest (8,848.86m), Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, Thamserku, and many other Himalayan giants while experiencing the warm hospitality and rich culture of the Sherpa people. Whether you are an experienced trekker or looking to combine adventure with mindfulness, this wellness trek offers a balanced and unforgettable Himalayan experience.

Wellness Experience:
Throughout the journey, professional wellness practices are incorporated to enhance your trekking experience.
- Morning Wellness: Gentle Yoga, Sunrise Stretching, Pranayama (Breathing Exercises), Mindfulness Practice
- Evening Wellness: Restorative Yoga, Guided Meditation, Muscle Recovery Stretching, Relaxation & Mindfulness Sessions
These activities are suitable for both beginners and experienced practitioners and are designed to complement the trekking schedule without adding physical strain.

Why Choose This Trek?
Unlike a traditional Everest Base Camp trek, the Wellness Trek focuses not only on reaching your destination but also on how you feel throughout the journey. By combining mindful movement, breathing techniques, and meditation with one of the world's greatest trekking routes, you'll return home with unforgettable memories, renewed energy, and a deeper connection to the Himalayas.
highlights: Reach the iconic Everest Base Camp (5,364m)
Hike to Kala Patthar (5,545m) for breathtaking sunrise views of Mount Everest

Cross thrilling suspension bridges over the Dudh Koshi River
Enjoy panoramic views of Everest, Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, Pumori, and Thamserku
Experience authentic Sherpa culture and Himalayan hospitality
Optional luxury lodge accommodation on selected sections of the trek

treks.title: Annapurna Base Camp Yoga Trek 11 Days
treks.description:
The 11-Day Annapurna Base Camp Yoga Trek is a unique wellness adventure that combines Himalayan trekking with daily yoga, meditation, and mindfulness practices. Set within the breathtaking Annapurna Conservation Area, this journey takes you through picturesque Gurung villages, lush rhododendron forests, cascading waterfalls, and alpine landscapes before reaching Annapurna Base Camp at an elevation of 4,130 meters.

Each day begins with guided sunrise yoga and pranayama to energize your body and prepare you for the trek ahead. After reaching your destination each afternoon, gentle stretching, restorative yoga, and meditation sessions help relieve muscle fatigue and promote relaxation.

Throughout the journey, you'll enjoy panoramic views of Annapurna I (8,091m), Machhapuchhre (6,993m), Hiunchuli, Gangapurna, and other Himalayan peaks while experiencing Nepal's rich mountain culture and peaceful natural surroundings.

Whether you are an experienced yogi or trying yoga for the first time, this trek offers the perfect balance of adventure, wellness, and cultural immersion.
highlights: Daily sunrise yoga overlooking the Himalayas
Evening meditation and restorative yoga sessions
Reach Annapurna Base Camp (4,130m)
Walk through beautiful Gurung villages
Explore rhododendron forests and alpine landscapes
Relax in the natural hot springs at Jhinu Danda
Practice breathing techniques for better acclimatization
Spectacular views of Annapurna I, Machhapuchhre, Hiunchuli, and Gangapurna
Experience authentic Nepali mountain hospitality

treks.title: Lobuche East Peak Climbing With EBC Trek-18 Days
treks.description: The Lobuche East Peak Climbing paired with the Everest Base Camp Trek is an extraordinary 18-day odyssey into the heart of the Khumbu region. Standing proud at 6,119 meters, Lobuche East offers an exhilarating mountaineering challenge tailored for adventurers seeking to conquer a Himalayan giant. You'll traverse diverse landscapes covering approximately 205 km, acclimatizing along the legendary route to Everest Base Camp. Your journey begins with a thrilling flight to Lukla, followed by a gradual ascent through vibrant Sherpa villages like Namche Bazaar and Dingboche. Highlights include witnessing the dawn break over Everest from Kala Patthar (5,545m), exploring ancient Tibetan Buddhist monasteries, and finally ascending the technical snow and ice slopes of Lobuche East via the South East Ridge. With breathtaking panoramas of Lhotse, Nuptse, Ama Dablam, and Everest itself, this expedition promises a sublime fusion of high-altitude trekking and technical alpine climbing.
highlights: Conquer the 6,119m summit of Lobuche East Peak for unparalleled panoramic views of Mount Everest, Lhotse, and Nuptse.
Trek to the iconic Everest Base Camp (5,364m) and marvel at the formidable Khumbu Icefall.
Ascend Kala Patthar at dawn to witness a spectacular golden sunrise illuminating the Himalayas.
Immerse yourself in Sherpa culture by exploring the ancient Tengboche and Pangboche Monasteries.
Cross the challenging Kong Ma La Pass at an altitude of 5,550 meters.
Discover Khumjung village, home to the legendary Yeti scalp and the historic school founded by Sir Edmund Hillary.
Experience a thrilling scenic flight between Kathmandu and the mountain airstrip of Lukla.

treks.additionalInfo: For a successful ascent of Lobuche East (6,119m), timing is critical. The premier climbing windows are during the vibrant Spring (March to May) and the crystal-clear Autumn (September to November). Spring welcomes you with blooming rhododendrons and progressively warmer days, though nights remain crisp. Autumn offers the most stable weather patterns and arguably the clearest skies, revealing the rugged beauty of the Khumbu region in sharp detail. Daytime temperatures can reach a comfortable 15°C (59°F), while nighttime temperatures at higher camps will drop significantly to around -10°C (14°F). Proper acclimatization and physical endurance are essential to prevent altitude sickness and fully enjoy this demanding yet deeply rewarding Himalayan expedition.

treks.title: Upper Mustang Mountain Biking Tour- 16 Days
treks.description: The Upper Mustang Mountain Biking Tour is the ultimate 16-day two-wheeled expedition into the heart of the Himalayas. Known as the 'Forbidden Kingdom of Lo,' this pristine, restricted region offers mountain bikers an otherworldly journey across trans-Himalayan deserts, ancient trade routes, and high-altitude mountain passes. Starting with a flight to Jomsom, you will pedal through the world's deepest gorge—the Kali Gandaki—navigating thrilling descents, rugged dirt trails, and river crossings. Along the way, you'll uncover centuries of history, from the 108 sacred water spouts of Muktinath to the mysterious sky caves of Chhoser and the walled medieval capital of Lo Manthang. Surrounded by the towering peaks of Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, and Nilgiri, this adventure perfectly blends adrenaline-pumping off-road cycling with deep cultural immersion into Tibetan Vajrayana Buddhism.
highlights: Conquer thrilling off-road trails through the stark, beautiful trans-Himalayan deserts of the forbidden kingdom.
Ride through the world's deepest gorge, the mighty Kali Gandaki, flanked by 8,000-meter giants.
Explore the ancient, walled medieval capital of Lo Manthang and the grand Royal Palace.
Seek blessings at the sacred Muktinath Temple, revered by both Hindus and Buddhists.
Discover the mysterious, man-made sky caves of Chhoser and the ancient Ghar Gompa.
Soak your tired muscles in the natural thermal hot springs of Tatopani.
Immerse yourself in authentic Tibetan-influenced culture, exploring remote villages like Kagbeni and Marpha.
Enjoy sweeping panoramic views of the Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, and Nilgiri mountain ranges.

itinerary.details: Our airport representative will greet you upon arrival and transfer you to your hotel. Enjoy a warm welcome dinner in the evening.

treks.additionalInfo: Upper Mustang is a highly restricted zone in Nepal. To legally mountain bike here, you must obtain a special Restricted Area Permit (RAP), which costs USD 500 for the first 10 days, alongside the standard Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP) and Trekkers' Information Management System (TIMS) card. While ACAP and TIMS have no time limit, the RAP strictly governs the duration of your stay in the forbidden kingdom. These permits must be processed through a registered trekking agency to ensure your safety and legality while exploring this pristine trans-Himalayan region.

faqs.question: Why must you pack lightly instead of bringing everything?
faqs.answer: The key to a successful mountain biking trip in the high Himalayas is mobility and efficiency. Keeping your backpack light promotes better balance, comfort, and sustainability. Essential gear includes moisture-wicking base layers, insulating mid-layers, windproof jackets, padded cycling shorts, a good-quality helmet, cycling shoes with grips, and protective gear like knee/elbow pads and sunglasses.

faqs.question: How can I remain fit and healthy for this demanding tour?
faqs.answer: A balanced diet, ample hydration, and physical fitness are crucial for this once-in-a-lifetime adventure. We recommend engaging in regular cardiovascular exercises (cycling, swimming, running) to build stamina, and strength training (squats, lunges) for your core and legs. Practicing yoga or Pilates can also enhance your flexibility and balance. Most importantly, allow your body time to adapt to the low oxygen levels at high altitudes.

faqs.question: When is the absolute best time to go for the Upper Mustang Biking Tour?
faqs.answer: Since Upper Mustang lies in the rain shadow of the Himalayas, it receives very little rainfall, making it a rare destination that is excellent to visit even during the summer monsoon (mid-June to mid-August). However, the premier seasons remain Spring (March to May) and Autumn (September to November), offering stable weather, clear trails, and spectacular visibility. Winter is possible but requires heavy-duty gear to combat severe cold and wind.

treks.title: Beijing To Kathmandu Via Lhasa And Everest
treks.description: Embark on the ultimate trans-continental pilgrimage spanning 4,000 kilometers from the imperial grandeur of China to the spiritual heights of the Tibetan Plateau, and finally down into the lush valleys of Nepal. This exclusive 12-day fixed-departure expedition promises unparalleled cultural immersion and logistical excellence. Your journey begins at the iconic Great Wall and the Forbidden City in Beijing before boarding the engineering marvel of the Qinghai-Tibet Railway, ascending through sweeping grasslands into the 'Roof of the World.' In Lhasa, you'll uncover the secrets of the Potala Palace and witness the energetic monk debates at Sera Monastery. The climax of the journey brings you face-to-face with the majestic North Face of Mount Everest, spending a night under the stars at Base Camp, before a dramatic overland descent across the Friendship Bridge into the vibrant city of Kathmandu.
highlights: Walk the ancient, uncrowded stones of the Mutianyu section of the Great Wall of China.
Explore the immense courtyards and imperial architecture of the Forbidden City in Beijing.
Ride the legendary Sky Train on the Qinghai-Tibet Railway, crossing spectacular 5,000m high-altitude passes.
Delve into spiritual Tibet with visits to the towering Potala Palace and the sacred Jokhang Temple.
Witness the lively and dynamic tradition of monk debating at the historic Sera Monastery.
Sleep in a traditional tent at Everest Base Camp and watch a golden sunrise over the North Face.
Experience a dramatic overland crossing from the arid Tibetan plateau into the lush, green landscapes of Nepal.

itinerary.details: Welcome to China! Upon arrival at Beijing Capital International Airport, you will be met by our representative, transferred to your hotel, and briefed on the adventure ahead.

itinerary.title: Imperial Beijing
itinerary.details: Dive into history at Tiananmen Square and the Forbidden City, exploring vast courtyards. In the afternoon, visit the masterpiece Summer Palace.

itinerary.title: The Great Wall of China
itinerary.details: Tick off a major bucket-list item by walking the peaceful, less-crowded Mutianyu section of the Great Wall, known for its stunning ridgeline views.

itinerary.title: High-Speed Train to Xining (2,270m)
itinerary.details: Take a 10-hour high-speed train to Xining, the gateway to the Tibetan plateau, and spend the evening acclimatizing to the elevation shift.

itinerary.title: The Sky Train to Lhasa
itinerary.details: Board the world-famous Qinghai-Tibet Train for a 24-hour journey in a soft-sleeper cabin, passing grazing yaks and snow-capped peaks.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Lhasa (3,650m)
itinerary.details: Arrive at Lhasa Railway Station in the 'City of Sunshine'. The rest of the day is strictly reserved for rest and hydration to adjust to the altitude.

itinerary.title: Drepung & Sera Monasteries
itinerary.details: Explore the massive Drepung Monastery, and in the afternoon, witness the dynamic monk debating sessions at Sera Monastery.

itinerary.title: The Potala Palace & Jokhang Temple
itinerary.details: Climb the steps of the iconic Potala Palace. Later, visit Jokhang Temple, the spiritual heart of Tibet, and walk the Barkhor Circuit with pilgrims.

itinerary.title: The Road to Shigatse (3,905m)
itinerary.details: Drive across the Kambala Pass to see the turquoise Yamdrok Lake and the massive Karola Glacier before arriving in Tibet's second-largest city.

itinerary.title: To the Roof of the World: EBC (5,200m)
itinerary.details: Drive through Qomolangma National Nature Reserve to Everest Base Camp. Visit Rongbuk Monastery and sleep in a traditional tent under the stars.

itinerary.title: Everest Sunrise & Drive to Gyirong (2,600m)
itinerary.details: Wake up for a spectacular sunrise hitting the North Face of Everest. Afterward, descend dramatically towards the Nepal border town of Gyirong.

itinerary.title: Border Crossing & Drive to Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Cross the Friendship Bridge into Nepal, where the landscape transforms instantly into lush greenery, and drive to Kathmandu to conclude the tour.

Accommodation: 3-Star hotels in cities (twin share) and a traditional tent/guesthouse at EBC.
Meals: Daily breakfast at all hotels.
Entrance Fees: All tickets for monuments listed (Great Wall, Potala Palace, etc.).
Safety: Emergency oxygen supplies carried in the vehicle for the Tibet portion.
costExcludes: International airfare arriving in Beijing and departing out of Kathmandu.
Chinese Visa Fee (must be arranged in your home country prior to arrival).
Lunch and Dinner meals (allow approximately $15-20 per day).
Mandatory travel and emergency medical insurance.
Gratuities and tips for local guides and drivers.
treks.additionalInfo: This cross-border expedition requires careful logistical preparation. You must arrange your Chinese Visa in your home country before departure. All Tibet-specific permits (Tibet Travel Permit and Alien Travel Permit) are handled by our team and included in the cost. Due to the extreme altitude variations—reaching up to 5,200m at Everest Base Camp—our itinerary is meticulously designed for gradual acclimatization, utilizing the Qinghai-Tibet railway to help your body adjust. Emergency oxygen is always carried in our vehicles in Tibet for your peace of mind.

treks.title: Fam & Media Expedition 2026- 13Days Nepal Bhutan & India
treks.description: The Himalayan Trinity Expedition is an exclusive 13-day 'Golden Thread' journey seamlessly connecting Nepal, Bhutan, and India (Darjeeling). Led by founder Nabraj Ghimire, this meticulously crafted itinerary is designed as a premier familiarization and product inspection tour for travel agents and content creators. Highlighting the extraordinary advantages of the 'Green Season' in August, you'll witness emerald rice paddies, dramatic cloud forests, and crowd-free iconic sites. From Kathmandu's vibrant cultural heritage to Bhutan's exclusive Gross National Happiness philosophy and Darjeeling's colonial nostalgia, this expedition offers unparalleled logistical feats—including a rare overland border crossing into India. It’s not just a tour; it’s a masterclass in packaging the ultimate high-value Himalayan Grand Tour.
highlights: Discover Kathmandu's ancient spiritual heart, including the Monkey Temple, Boudhanath, and UNESCO royal squares showcasing Newari architecture.
Hike to Bhutan's iconic cliffside Tiger's Nest Monastery (Paro Taktsang) and marvel at the massive Buddha Dordenma statue.
Experience the 'Green Season' advantage with crowd-free access to emerald landscapes and dramatic cloud forests.
Execute a rare, logistical overland border crossing from Phuntsholing, Bhutan directly into Jaigaon, India.
Explore the stunning Phobjikha Valley and grand fortress-monasteries (Dzongs) like Punakha Dzong.
Enjoy a nostalgic ride on the UNESCO-listed Darjeeling Himalayan Railway 'Toy Train'.
Savor the 'Champagne of Teas' with an exclusive tasting and estate tour in Darjeeling.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Transfer from the airport to your hotel. In the evening, enjoy a walking tour of Thamel and an authentic Nepalese welcome dinner.

itinerary.title: The UNESCO Loop
itinerary.details: Morning visit to Swayambhunath and Patan Durbar Square. Enjoy a Newari culinary inspection for lunch, and rooftop drinks at Boudhanath in the evening.

itinerary.title: Ancient Cities & Leisure
itinerary.details: Explore the incredible ancient architecture of Bhaktapur Durbar Square and the 4th-century Changu Narayan temple.

itinerary.title: The Flight of a Lifetime to Paro (2,200m)
itinerary.details: Take a breathtaking flight to Bhutan (with left-side seats for Everest views). Explore Rinpung Dzong and Ta Dzong Museum.

itinerary.title: The Icon – Tiger’s Nest
itinerary.details: A thrilling hike to the iconic Taktsang Monastery perched on a cliff. Conclude the day with a traditional Bhutanese Hot Stone Bath.

itinerary.title: The 'Haa Loop' to Thimphu (2,400m)
itinerary.details: Drive via the stunning Chele La Pass (3,988m) and enjoy a picnic lunch in the exclusive, off-the-beaten-path Haa Valley.

itinerary.title: Thimphu City Inspection
itinerary.details: Visit the giant Buddha Dordenma statue and the Painting School, followed by luxury and boutique hotel site inspections.

itinerary.title: Into the Glacial Valley (3,100m)
itinerary.details: Drive over Dochu La Pass to the pristine Phobjikha Valley, staying in the conservation area of the endangered Black-Necked Cranes.

itinerary.title: Nature & Descent to Punakha (1,200m)
itinerary.details: Walk the scenic Gangtey Nature Trail before descending to the sub-tropical Punakha Valley to visit the famed Fertility Temple.

itinerary.title: The Road to the Border (300m)
itinerary.details: Embark on a scenic 7-8 hour drive descending from Punakha down to the Bhutanese border town of Phuentsholing.

itinerary.title: Border Crossing to Darjeeling (2,042m)
itinerary.details: Walk through the border arch into Jaigaon, India. Switch to Indian vehicles, ascend to Darjeeling, and enjoy a colonial dinner at Glenary's.

itinerary.title: The Champagne of Teas
itinerary.details: Enjoy a joy ride on the UNESCO Toy Train, visit the active Happy Valley Tea Estate, and spend the afternoon shopping along Mall Road.

itinerary.title: Departure
itinerary.details: Drive to Bagdogra Airport (IXB) for your flight home, or opt to fly to Delhi for a Golden Triangle extension.

costIncludes: Twin-share accommodations in 3-star and premium hotels across Kathmandu, Bhutan, and Darjeeling.
Full board meals in Bhutan; 8 breakfasts, 7 lunches, and 7 dinners throughout the trip, plus a Welcome Dinner in Nepal.
All private transfers and dedicated sightseeing vehicles in all three countries.
Regional flights: Kathmandu to Paro, and Bagdogra to Delhi.
Top-tier English-speaking expert guides.
Bhutan Visa processing, fees, and the mandatory Bhutanese Royalties (Sustainable Development Fee).
costExcludes: International flights arriving in Kathmandu and departing from Delhi/Home.
Visa fees for Nepal and India (e-visas are readily available and must be procured prior).
Mandatory personal travel and emergency insurance.
Tips, gratuities, and personal expenses.
treks.additionalInfo: This exclusive Fam & Media Expedition is a fixed departure for August 2026, strategically chosen to highlight the 'Green Season'. Participants will enjoy heavily subsidized FAM rates, including a significant waiver on Bhutanese Royalties (SDF), available exclusively to our delegation. As this tour involves complex, multi-country logistics and land border crossings, travelers must ensure their passports have at least 6 months validity and secure their Indian e-visa prior to arrival. Pack lightly and be prepared for diverse climates, ranging from the humid plains of India to the crisp alpine air of Bhutan.

treks.title: 4x4 Road Trip To Upper Mustang Express Tour-6 Days
treks.description: Embark on the ultimate 4x4 overland expedition into Upper Mustang, one of the last forbidden kingdoms and a hidden jewel of the Himalayas. This exclusive 6-day off-road tour effortlessly blends raw adventure with luxurious comfort, taking you deep into Tibetan culture, ancient monasteries, and surreal desert landscapes that few visitors ever witness. From the comfort and safety of a powerful Toyota Landcruiser or Hilux, you will traverse rugged mountain trails, the towering Kali Gandaki river gorge, and windswept plateaus. Every day of this overland journey unveils a new layer of history and natural beauty, culminating at the mystical walled city of Lo Manthang. Whether you are a thrill-seeker or a cultural explorer, this express 4x4 overland trip promises the perfect balance of adventure and scenic luxury.
highlights: Travel off-the-beaten-path in the unparalleled comfort and style of a powerful 4x4 Toyota Landcruiser or Hilux.
Discover the hidden capital of Lo Manthang, a medieval walled city rich with royal history and whitewashed homes.
Experience an authentic and untouched blend of ancient Tibetan and Himalayan cultures.
Visit centuries-old monasteries and witness rituals that have remained pristine for generations.
Marvel at trans-Himalayan landscapes, from the deep Kali Gandaki Gorge to the wind-eroded cliffs of Chhoser.
Drive along the historic salt trade route, marked by ancient caves, vibrant chortens, and intricate Mani walls.
Reward yourself with a deeply relaxing soak in the natural thermal hot springs at Tatopani.
Explore the mysterious, multi-story sky caves of Chhoser, carved directly into towering cliff faces.

itinerary.title: Drive from Pokhara to Lete (2,480m)
itinerary.details: A scenic 6-7 hour drive along the Kali Gandaki River, stopping at Kusma (for bungee views) and the spectacular Rupse Waterfall.

itinerary.title: Lete to Kagbeni via Muktinath (3,800m)
itinerary.details: Ascend to the sacred pilgrimage site of Muktinath with its 108 water spouts, then descend to the ancient gateway village of Kagbeni.

itinerary.title: Kagbeni to Lo Manthang (3,840m)
itinerary.details: Complete permit formalities and drive deep into the restricted zone, passing dramatic canyons and visiting the ancient Ghar Gompa.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang Excursion Day
itinerary.details: Explore three major monasteries (Jampa Lhakhang, Thubchen Gompa, Chode Gompa), the sky caves of Jhong, and one of the world's highest golf courses.

itinerary.title: Lo Manthang to Marpha (2,670m)
itinerary.details: Retrace your route south, leaving the barren highlands for the lush apple orchards of Marpha, famous for its apple brandy.

itinerary.title: Marpha to Pokhara (822m)
itinerary.details: A final scenic drive down through the world's deepest gorge, stopping for a thermal soak at Tatopani before arriving back in Pokhara.

costIncludes: Best available guesthouse and lodge accommodations throughout the Mustang journey.
Government-licensed, top-tier English-speaking guide for the entire trip.
Full board meals (Breakfast, Lunch, Dinner) during the Upper Mustang tour.
Round trip transportation in a private 4WD luxury vehicle (max 3-4 passengers per vehicle).
Complete insurance, food, accommodation, and wages for all support staff.
All government road taxes and vehicle fees throughout the trip.
costExcludes: International flight tickets to/from Nepal and applicable taxes.
Lunches and dinners during any stay in Kathmandu and Pokhara.
Entrance fees for temples, monuments, and monasteries.
Mandatory travel insurance covering emergency evacuation and medical assistance.
Personal expenses (bar bills, laundry, phone calls, etc.).
Extra accommodations required due to natural calamities or political strikes.
Gratuities for the guide, driver, and support staff.
treks.additionalInfo: Upper Mustang is a highly restricted, high-altitude region in Nepal that was closed to outsiders until 1992. Located in the rain shadow of the Himalayas, its dry, desert-like environment is perfect for overland exploration even during the monsoon season. Foreign travelers require a special Restricted Area Permit (costing approximately US$50 per day) along with the Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP). Despite the rugged terrain, our luxury 4x4 vehicles ensure a comfortable and safe journey through this culturally preserved, former independent Kingdom of Lo.

faqs.question: Is previous off-roading experience required for this trip?
faqs.answer: Not at all! You will be chauffeured in a powerful, luxury 4WD vehicle by our highly experienced, government-licensed drivers who are experts at navigating the rugged Trans-Himalayan terrain. You simply get to sit back, relax in comfort, and enjoy the breathtaking scenery.

faqs.question: What is the risk of altitude sickness on an overland express tour?
faqs.answer: While we do reach elevations up to 4,730m, the itinerary is designed to ascend gradually. However, because we drive rather than walk, the ascent is faster. We strongly recommend drinking plenty of water and avoiding alcohol during the ascent. Our guides are trained in wilderness first aid and closely monitor your health throughout the journey.

faqs.question: How rough are the roads and what kind of comfort can I expect?
faqs.answer: The road to Upper Mustang is an unpaved, rugged dirt track carved into mountain cliffs and riverbeds, meaning sections will be bumpy. However, our use of premium 4x4 luxury vehicles significantly dampens the ride. We ensure a maximum of 3 to 4 passengers per vehicle so everyone has a window seat and ample legroom.

faqs.question: Will I be able to charge my batteries and access the internet?
faqs.answer: Yes! Most guesthouses and lodges in Upper Mustang now have electricity (often solar-powered) where you can charge your devices, usually for a small extra fee. Wi-Fi and cellular data are available in many villages, though speeds can be slow and unpredictable due to the remote nature of the region.

treks.title: The Grand Trans-Himalayan Traverse 2026-17 Days
treks.activity: Day Or Multiple Day Hike And Tours
treks.description: The Grand Trans-Himalayan Traverse is an epic 17-day overland odyssey curated for June 2026. This rare and highly sought-after journey connects the ancient wonders of China with the spiritual heartland of Tibet and the lush valleys of Nepal. Starting at the iconic Great Wall and Forbidden City in Beijing, you will board the world-famous high-speed 'Sky Train' to the Tibetan Plateau. Witness the awe-inspiring Potala Palace in Lhasa, catch a golden sunrise illuminating the North Face of Mount Everest, and embark on a sacred 3-day Kora trek around Mount Kailash. Finally, descend dramatically from the barren roof of the world into the vibrant streets of Kathmandu. Led by our expert founder Raj, this fixed-departure tour is strictly limited and reserved on a first-come, first-served basis.
highlights: Walk the ancient steps of the Mutianyu Great Wall and explore the majestic Forbidden City in Beijing.
Experience an engineering marvel aboard the Qinghai-Tibet Railway, the 'Sky Train', ascending to the roof of the world.
Immerse yourself in Lhasa's spirituality at the Potala Palace, Jokhang Temple, and witness energetic Monk Debates at Sera Monastery.
Catch a breathtaking, golden sunrise illuminating the North Face of Mount Everest from the Rongbuk base camp.
Embark on a sacred 3-day circumambulation (Kora) trek around the holy Mount Kailash, crossing the formidable Dolma La Pass (5,630m).
Reflect in peace at the pristine and holy Lake Manasarovar before beginning your Kailash trek.
Execute a dramatic overland descent from the barren Tibetan plateau down into the lush forests and waterfalls of the Gyirong Valley and into Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Beijing (60m)
itinerary.details: Welcome to China! Transfer to your hotel and recover from jet lag or explore the vibrant streets.

itinerary.title: Imperial City Tour
itinerary.details: Walk through Tiananmen Square, explore the Forbidden City, and visit the masterpiece Summer Palace.

itinerary.title: The Great Wall
itinerary.details: Travel to the lush Mutianyu section of the Great Wall. Enjoy a cable car ride up and a fun toboggan ride down.

itinerary.title: High-Speed Journey to the Plateau (2,240m)
itinerary.details: Board the high-speed bullet train to Xining, capital of Qinghai Province, an essential stop for acclimatization.

itinerary.title: The Sky Train
itinerary.details: Enjoy a free day in Xining. In the evening, board the world-famous Qinghai-Tibet Railway.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Lhasa (3,650m)
itinerary.details: Enjoy high-altitude scenery from your train window before arriving at Lhasa Railway Station. Rest is vital today.

itinerary.title: Lhasa Spiritual Tour
itinerary.details: Visit the Jokhang Temple, walk the Barkhor Circuit with pilgrims, and witness the Monk Debates at Sera Monastery.

itinerary.title: Treasures of the Dalai Lama
itinerary.details: Climb the iconic Potala Palace and later explore the Norbulingka summer palace or Drepung Monastery.

itinerary.title: Lhasa to Shigatse (3,840m)
itinerary.details: Drive over the Gampala Pass to see turquoise Yamdrok Lake and the Karola Glacier before arriving in Shigatse.

itinerary.title: The Face of Everest (5,200m)
itinerary.details: Cross Gyawu La Pass for panoramic Himalayan views, visit Rongbuk Monastery, and settle in near Everest Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Everest to Saga (4,500m)
itinerary.details: Wake up to a golden sunrise over Everest, then drive west past Peiku Tso Lake with views of Shishapangma.

itinerary.title: Saga to Darchen (4,575m)
itinerary.details: Drive to the holy Lake Manasarovar for spiritual reflection before heading to Darchen, the gateway to Mt. Kailash.

itinerary.title: Kora Day 1 – Valley of the God (5,080m)
itinerary.details: Begin the sacred 20km trek, leading to Dirapuk Monastery with up-close views of Kailash's North Face.

itinerary.title: Kora Day 2 – The High Pass (4,820m)
itinerary.details: The toughest day. Climb over the Dolma La Pass (5,630m), descend past Gauri Kund, and stay at Zutulpuk Monastery (18km).

itinerary.title: Kora Day 3 & Return to Saga (4,500m)
itinerary.details: Complete the final 14km leg back to Darchen, then meet our vehicle for the drive across the plateau to Saga.

itinerary.title: Saga to Gyirong (2,600m)
itinerary.details: Drive south toward the Nepal border, dropping dramatically in altitude into lush forests and waterfalls.

itinerary.title: Gyirong to Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Cross the bridge into Nepal and drive the rugged roads to Kathmandu for a final celebration and rest.

costIncludes: Accommodation: 3-star hotels in major cities; simple authentic guest houses/lodges during the Kailash and Everest segments.
Transport: Private Van throughout Tibet, and a dedicated Jeep transfer from the border to Kathmandu.
Trains: High-Speed Train (Beijing to Xining) & Soft Sleeper class on the Sky Train (Xining to Lhasa).
Staff: Highly experienced, English-speaking local Tibetan Guide.
Permits: All necessary Tibet Travel and Trekking permits.
Meals: Daily breakfast included (B/B Basis).
Fees: All sightseeing and entrance fees as outlined in the itinerary.
costExcludes: International flights (Home to Beijing / Kathmandu to Home).
Lunch and Dinner throughout the trip.
Mandatory Travel Insurance with high-altitude coverage.
Rescue and Evacuation Services.
Personal expenses (tips, beverages, laundry).
Horse or Porter hiring for the Kailash Kora (optional).
Costs arising from unforeseen circumstances like landslides or weather delays.
treks.additionalInfo: This epic Trans-Himalayan traverse is physically demanding, taking you to extreme altitudes exceeding 5,000m at Everest Base Camp and Mount Kailash. Proper physical and mental preparation is crucial to handle the thin air, cold temperatures, and remote, basic facilities during the Kailash Kora. We recommend traveling in Spring (March-May) or Autumn (September-November) for the best visibility and weather. While we provide bottled water, we encourage bringing a reusable bottle and purification tablets. Be aware that internet access is heavily restricted in China; a VPN must be downloaded prior to arrival if you wish to access western social media, and connectivity will be scarce during the high-altitude remote segments.

faqs.question: Is the 3-day Kailash Kora trek mandatory?
faqs.answer: While the 3-day Kora is a spiritual highlight of the tour, it is physically demanding. If you feel unwell or prefer not to trek, you can choose to remain at a guesthouse in Darchen and wait for the group to return.

faqs.question: How do we get the Tibet Travel Permit?
faqs.answer: We handle all the complex logistics for you! Once you book, we will collect your passport and Chinese visa copies to secure your Tibet Travel Permit through the Tibet Tourism Bureau well in advance of your arrival.

faqs.question: Will I need a VPN in China and Tibet?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you wish to use services like Google, WhatsApp, Facebook, or Instagram, you must download and install a reliable VPN on your devices before arriving in China, as these sites are blocked by the Great Firewall.

faqs.question: What are the accommodations like at Mount Kailash and EBC?
faqs.answer: Accommodations in these highly remote, high-altitude regions are extremely basic. You will stay in simple guesthouses or tented camps with shared, rudimentary toilet facilities and no running hot water. The experience focuses on spirituality and nature rather than luxury.

treks.title: Nepal Luxury Tour Package-7 Days
treks.description: Explore the cultural treasures and natural wonders of Nepal in unparalleled comfort and style. This exclusive 7-day luxury tour is meticulously crafted for those who value privacy, elegance, and efficiency. From 5-star accommodations in the vibrant Kathmandu Valley to boutique lakeside resorts in the serene city of Pokhara, every detail is designed for premium comfort. Skip long, arduous road journeys by taking scenic internal flights that offer incredible aerial views of the Himalayas. You'll explore medieval UNESCO World Heritage sites, glide across the tranquil waters of Phewa Lake, and witness a once-in-a-lifetime sunrise over the snowcapped Annapurna range from the panoramic hilltop of Sarangkot. This journey offers the ultimate blend of deep cultural immersion and luxurious relaxation.
highlights: Relax in absolute comfort at Nepal’s finest 5-star luxury hotels and boutique resorts throughout the journey.
Explore the medieval artistry and spiritual heritage of UNESCO-listed sites in Kathmandu, Patan, and Bhaktapur.
Bypass long road trips with a scenic, time-saving domestic flight between Kathmandu and Pokhara.
Enjoy a peaceful, private boat ride on the serene waters of Phewa Lake, gazing up at Machhapuchhre (Fishtail Mountain).
Discover the natural wonders of Pokhara, including the dramatic Davis Falls and the deep Seti River Gorge.
Wake up to a breathtaking, panoramic Himalayan sunrise over the Annapurna range from the exclusive hilltop of Sarangkot.
Benefit from expert, private guided tours ensuring a highly personalized and insightful cultural experience.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Arrive in Nepal's capital. Enjoy a VIP airport transfer to your luxury hotel in Thamel or your preferred area to relax.

itinerary.title: Explore Kathmandu and Bhaktapur
itinerary.details: Visit the sacred Pashupatinath Temple, the massive Boudhanath Stupa, and the medieval architecture of Bhaktapur Durbar Square.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Sightseeing and Fly to Pokhara (822m)
itinerary.details: Visit Kathmandu Durbar Square, the Kumari Temple, and Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple). Take a scenic 30-minute afternoon flight to Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Discover Pokhara
itinerary.details: Explore Davis Falls, Gupteshwor Cave, the Seti River Gorge, and the International Mountain Museum. End with a peaceful boat ride on Phewa Lake to Barahi Temple.

itinerary.title: Pokhara to Sarangkot (1,600m)
itinerary.details: Take a short, scenic private drive up to the hilltop of Sarangkot. Check into your luxury resort and soak in the tranquil Annapurna mountain vistas.

itinerary.title: Sarangkot Sunrise and Return to Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Wake early for a spectacular sunrise over Fishtail Mountain. Fly back to Kathmandu and spend the afternoon exploring the exquisite artisan heritage of Patan Durbar Square.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy a final luxury breakfast before your private VIP transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for your flight home.

costIncludes: VIP airport pickup and drop-off in premium air-conditioned vehicles.
Twin-share luxury hotel accommodations on a Bed & Breakfast (BB) basis.
Expert, local English-speaking private guide (other languages available upon request).

faqs.question: Is this luxury tour physically demanding?
faqs.answer: Not at all. This tour is graded as 'Easy' and is designed for relaxation and cultural immersion. We bypass arduous overland driving by including a scenic domestic flight to Pokhara. All sightseeing is done at a leisurely pace with private transport, making it perfect for all ages.

faqs.question: Can the itinerary be customized?
faqs.answer: Absolutely! Because this is a private luxury tour, we can tailor the experience to your exact preferences. Whether you want to add a helicopter tour to Everest Base Camp, book exclusive spa treatments, or arrange private dining experiences, our team will make it happen.

faqs.question: What kind of vehicles are used for the transfers?
faqs.answer: We use premium, latest-model air-conditioned SUVs or luxury vans, depending on your group size. You will be chauffeured by professional, courteous drivers ensuring a smooth, safe, and highly comfortable ride throughout your journey.

treks.title: Honey Hunting Festival In Nepal 5 - 10 Days
treks.description: The Honey Hunting in Nepal package is a thrilling cultural immersion designed for adventurers and nature lovers. Far more than a simple hike, this 10-day journey takes you deep into the heart of the Annapurna foothills to witness the Gurung and Magar tribes performing ancient, gravity-defying wild honey harvesting. You will watch skilled hunters risk their lives climbing sheer rock cliffs on fragile, hand-woven bamboo ladders to harvest the rare, reddish 'Mad Honey.' Known for its mild hallucinogenic properties derived from rhododendron nectar, this honey is highly prized for its medicinal benefits. Trekking through the wild, raw beauty of the Lamjung district, you'll pass terraced rice fields, plunging waterfalls, and dense subtropical forests—all against the stunning backdrop of the Annapurna and Manaslu mountain ranges.
highlights: Witness daring local hunters harvest wild honey from sheer, high-altitude cliffs using traditional handmade bamboo ladders.
Immerse yourself in ancient pre-harvest rituals, including prayers and offerings to forest spirits for a safe hunt.
Taste the famous 'Mad Honey', a rare reddish nectar prized for its medicinal benefits and mild hallucinogenic effects.
Experience authentic rural life by staying with local Gurung and Magar families in picturesque villages like Bhujung and Ghalegaun.
Trek through lush subtropical forests, terraced fields, and river valleys adorned with swinging suspension bridges.
Marvel at sweeping, up-close panoramic views of the magnificent Annapurna and Manaslu mountain ranges.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Welcome to Nepal! Transfer to your hotel, attend a brief pre-trek meeting, and enjoy a traditional Nepalese welcome dinner with cultural performances.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Valley Sightseeing Tour
itinerary.details: Acclimatize with a guided tour of four UNESCO World Heritage Sites: Pashupatinath, Boudhanath, Kathmandu Durbar Square, and Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple).

itinerary.title: Drive to Besisahar (760m)
itinerary.details: Leave the valley on a scenic 6-7 hour private Jeep drive along the Prithvi Highway, following the Marshyangdi River to the rustic town of Besisahar.

itinerary.title: Trek to Ghalegaun (2,100m)
itinerary.details: A 7-8 hour trek climbing through forests and small hamlets to Ghalegaun, a model tourism village rich in Gurung culture, with sunset views over Manaslu.

itinerary.title: Trek to Ghanpokhara (2,670m)
itinerary.details: A short, mild 1-2 hour morning hike to the tiny, beautiful village of Ghanpokhara. Spend the day resting, exploring terraced fields, and soaking in the mountain views.

itinerary.title: The Honey-Hunting Ceremony (2,100m)
itinerary.details: The main event! Trek to the cliffs to observe ancient pre-hunt rituals and watch the spectacular, intense honey harvest by local climbers, followed by a fresh honey tasting. Return to Ghalegaun.

itinerary.title: Trek to Pasgaon via Bhujung (1,650m)
itinerary.details: A 6-7 hour hike through rhododendron forests to Bhujung, then a steep climb up to the beautiful ridge-top settlement of Pasgaon.

itinerary.title: Trek to Pakhrikot (1,200m)
itinerary.details: A 5-6 hour trek through dense oak and rhododendron forests, alive with Himalayan birds, followed by a steep descent to the old Gurung village of Pakhrikot.

itinerary.title: Trek to Thumsikot & Drive to Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Walk down to Thumsikot (2 hrs) to conclude the trek, then enjoy a scenic 6-7 hour private Jeep drive back to Kathmandu for a farewell dinner.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy a final breakfast and last-minute souvenir shopping before your transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for your flight home.

treks.additionalInfo: The Honey Hunting Festival is a rare cultural event taking place in the remote mid-elevations of the Annapurna region, predominantly harvested by the Gurung and Magar tribes. The honey's deep red color and unique properties come from Grayanotoxin found in wild Rhododendron nectar, which blooms heavily in Spring. This is a moderate-level trek requiring 5-7 hours of walking daily on rough, mountainous terrain. While you will observe the hunt from a safe distance, there is always a risk of bee stings from the large, aggressive Himalayan cliff bees; please inform us if you have severe allergies. We recommend bringing proper hiking gear, a head net, and insect repellent.

faqs.question: Is it safe to get close to the wild Himalayan bees?
faqs.answer: While the Himalayan cliff bees are large and aggressive, our groups observe the harvest from a safe, designated distance below the cliffs or behind protective netting. However, there is always a slight risk of a stray bee, so we recommend packing a face net and insect repellent. Please inform us beforehand if you have severe bee allergies.

faqs.question: What exactly is 'Mad Honey' and is it safe to eat?
faqs.answer: Mad Honey gets its deep reddish color and unique properties from the grayanotoxin found in wild Rhododendron nectar. When consumed, it provides a very mild hallucinogenic sensation or lightheadedness, along with various traditional medicinal benefits. Tasting it is completely optional and safe when taken in small amounts.

faqs.question: How difficult is the trekking portion of this tour?
faqs.answer: This tour is graded as 'Moderate'. You should expect to walk for 5 to 7 hours daily on rough, steep, and sometimes slippery mountainous terrain. We highly recommend doing some cardiovascular exercises or long hikes a few months prior to arrival to ensure your body is prepared.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation should I expect during the trek?
faqs.answer: This is an off-the-beaten-path cultural immersion. You will stay in traditional Teahouses and homestays with local Gurung and Magar families in villages like Bhujung and Ghalegaun. Facilities are basic but incredibly warm and welcoming, offering an authentic glimpse into Himalayan rural life.

treks.title: Saipal Base Camp Trek 16 Days
treks.description: The Saipal Base Camp Trek is a remarkable and remote 16-day journey that leads you to the base of Saipal Himal (7,031m), a stunning yet unconquered peak in Nepal's far-western region. Unlike the bustling trails of Everest and Annapurna, this trek offers profound solitude, with some days where you might be the only foreigner on the trail. This pristine, off-the-beaten-path adventure takes you through incredibly diverse landscapes, from dense subtropical forests to high-alpine grasslands, deep gorges, and crystal-clear rivers. Along the way, you will immerse yourself in the unique, ancient cultures of the Thakuri and Bhotia communities, whose traditions remain largely untouched by modernity. A true expedition for seasoned trekkers, this physical challenge rewards you with raw natural beauty, panoramic snow-capped peaks, and an unforgettable sense of wilderness.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Marvel at breathtaking, panoramic views of Saipal Himal (7,031m), Api Himal, and other towering peaks of the far-western Himalayas.
Experience absolute solitude on a highly remote, off-the-beaten-path route rarely visited by other tourists.
Immerse yourself in the unique, untouched traditions of the local Thakuri and Bhotia communities.
Trek through incredibly diverse ecosystems, traversing lush pine forests, steep gorges, high-altitude pastures, and glaciers.
Enjoy spectacular scenic domestic flights from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, and up to the remote mountain airstrip of Simikot.
Experience authentic expedition-style trekking with fully catered tented camps set up in pristine wilderness.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Transfer to your hotel, attend a trip briefing, and enjoy a warm Nepalese welcome dinner with cultural dancing.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Sightseeing and Trip Preparation
itinerary.details: Explore 3-4 of Kathmandu's UNESCO World Heritage sites, including Swayambhunath, Pashupatinath, and ancient Durbar Squares.

itinerary.title: Fly to Nepalgunj (150m)
itinerary.details: Take a 1-hour flight to Nepalgunj in south-west Nepal, the main gateway to the remote far-western region.

itinerary.title: Flight to Simikot and Trek to Dharapuri (2,310m)
itinerary.details: Enjoy a scenic 45-minute flight in a tiny aircraft to Simikot. Begin your trek through pine forests and rocky trails to the Karnali River.

itinerary.title: Trek to Kermi (2,670m)
itinerary.details: Walk along the Humla Karnali River, past waterfalls. Visit Lakiyo and Lhundrup Choeling Gompas, and soak in a natural hot spring.

itinerary.title: Trek to Yalbang (3,020m)
itinerary.details: Cross the Salli River and trek through buckwheat fields and pine forests. Visit the Namkh Kyung Dzong monastery, housing statues of Guru Rinpoche.

itinerary.title: Trek to Chala (3,690m)
itinerary.details: Ascend north with beautiful views of the Sumjum and Saipal Himal ranges, finally descending briefly to the remote settlement of Chala.

itinerary.title: Trek to Karang Khola / Labuk Depsa (4,000m)
itinerary.details: Follow the Kalungba River into the beautiful Karang Valley. Catch glimpses of the North Saipal Glacier before camping in a lush forest clearing.

itinerary.title: Trek to Saipal Base Camp (4,250m)
itinerary.details: Carefully navigate steep, icy trails up to the base camp. Be rewarded with majestic, panoramic views of Api, Saipal, Nandadevi, and massive glaciers.

itinerary.title: Rest Day at Base Camp
itinerary.details: Spend the day exploring the base camp area. Hike to nearby vantage points over snow and ice for even more spectacular mountain vistas.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Karang Khola (4,000m)
itinerary.details: Trace your steps back down into the lush pasture lands, enjoying alternative views of the Karang region and Karang Tal.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Yalbang (3,020m)
itinerary.details: An easier descent along isolated trails and the Puiya River. Arrive in Yalbang to further explore the local Thakuri and Bhotia culture.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Dharapuri (2,310m)
itinerary.details: Descend into the lower vegetation and settlement areas, interacting with the indigenous Jhakri communities.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Simikot (2,910m)
itinerary.details: Retrace your final steps to Simikot. Spend the afternoon exploring the town's unique stupas and monasteries.

itinerary.title: Fly back to Kathmandu via Nepalgunj (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Take an early morning flight back to Nepalgunj, then connect to Kathmandu. Celebrate the successful expedition with a farewell dinner.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Enjoy your final morning before our team transfers you to the airport for your journey home.

treks.additionalInfo: The Saipal Base Camp trek is a highly remote, expedition-style journey in Nepal's culturally isolated far-west. You must be prepared for complete self-sufficiency, sleeping in tented camps with no access to standard teahouses, Wi-Fi, or electricity after the first few days. The trail is physically demanding, involving steep climbs, rocky paths, and potentially icy terrain near the base camp. We highly recommend bringing a -20C rated sleeping bag (though we can provide one), sturdy trekking boots, a comprehensive personal medical kit, and a solar charger for your devices. The best time to visit is during Spring (March-May) for blooming rhododendrons, or Autumn (September-November) for crystal-clear mountain views.

faqs.question: Is there electricity and Wi-Fi on the Saipal Base Camp trek?
faqs.answer: As this is one of the most remote areas in Nepal, there are no Wi-Fi or electricity facilities on the trail. You may find a sporadic mobile network until Day 6. We highly recommend bringing a portable solar panel to charge your devices.

faqs.question: What is the accommodation like on this trek?
faqs.answer: Unlike popular regions with developed teahouse networks, this is an expedition-style trek. You will sleep in twin-sharing tented camps for the duration of the trek. Our expert team provides the tents, sleeping bags, and a dedicated cook to prepare all your meals.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Saipal Base Camp trek?
faqs.answer: This trek is considered hard and challenging. It ventures into a remote, unspoiled wilderness with plenty of steep, uphill climbs and rocky, sometimes icy, terrain. A strong level of physical fitness and prior trekking experience is highly recommended.

faqs.question: Are solo trekkers allowed in this region?
faqs.answer: No. Because Saipal is in a highly remote, restricted area, solo trekking is strictly prohibited by the government. You must trek with a registered guide and hold a Restricted Area Permit.

treks.title: Api Base Camp Trek 15 Days
treks.description: The Api Base Camp Trek is a thrilling and adventurous journey into the extreme northwest corner of Nepal, leading to the base of Mount Api (7,132m), one of the highest and least-climbed peaks in the Far-Western region. Protected by the Api Nampa Conservation Area, this untouched region offers far more than just towering mountains. You will trek alongside the beautiful Chameliya River, traversing steep gorges, lush subtropical and alpine forests, and serene glacial lakes. Along this remote and tranquil trail, you will encounter the unique, deeply preserved cultures of the Tharu, Raute, and Bhotiya ethnic communities. For seasoned trekkers seeking an off-the-beaten-path experience away from the bustling crowds, this moderate to challenging expedition offers a rare glimpse into authentic, pure Nepalese wilderness.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Marvel at incredible panoramic views of Mt. Api (7,132m), Mt. Nampa (6,929m), and Mt. Bobaye (6,808m).
Explore the rich biodiversity of the Api Nampa Conservation Area, with potential sightings of snow leopards and Himalayan black bears.
Immerse yourself in the traditional, untouched cultures of the Far-West, including the Raute, Bhotiya, and Tharu communities.
Discover Kalidhunga Lake (4,200m), a stunning, serene glacial lake nestled amidst rugged high-altitude terrain.
Trek alongside the magnificent Chameliya and Mahakali rivers, passing cascading waterfalls and deep gorges.
Enjoy true solitude on an uncrowded, remote trail, offering an authentic experience in Nepal's least developed region.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Transfer to your hotel, attend a trip briefing, and enjoy a warm Nepalese welcome dinner with cultural dancing.

itinerary.title: Fly to Dhangadhi (109m)
itinerary.details: Take a scenic 75-minute flight to Dhangadhi. Enjoy an afternoon cycling trip to Jokhar Lake and the Botanical Garden.

itinerary.title: Drive from Dhangadhi to Gokuleshwar
itinerary.details: Leave the Terai plains on an 8-hour drive through the green hills of Far-Western Nepal, stopping in Dadeldhura. Stay in a basic lodge.

itinerary.title: Drive to Latinath & Trek to Paribagar (1,770m)
itinerary.details: Drive 2 hours to Latinath, the trek's starting point, then hike 1 hour to the beautiful settlement of Paribagar. Sleep in a local homestay.

itinerary.title: Trek to Makarigaad (1,470m)
itinerary.details: Walk for 5 hours through traditional stone villages, ancient terraces, and subalpine forests alongside the Chameliya River.

itinerary.title: Trek to Siti (2,254m)
itinerary.details: Climb up the gorge to Pato, then continue on a gently ascending trail before dropping into the traditional settlement of Siti (8 hours).

itinerary.title: Trek to Domal (2,950m)
itinerary.details: Hike through Khayekot, the last permanent settlement on the route, before reaching Domal, the sacred junction of the Chameliya and Rokap rivers. Camp overnight.

itinerary.title: Trek to Dhaulo Odar (3,548m)
itinerary.details: A 5-hour walk through open alpine pastures, rhododendron forests, and small caves. Camp in an open grassland surrounded by high peaks.

itinerary.title: Trek to Api Base Camp (3,861m) & Return
itinerary.details: Hike up to the base camp plateau for the grandest views of Mt. Api and Nampa. Visit the holy Kalidhunga/Pilkandaha Lake and return to camp.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Siti (2,258m)
itinerary.details: Descend back through Khayekot, taking in the last close views of the towering peaks, and return to the homestay in Siti.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Makarigaad (1,470m)
itinerary.details: Walk along the ridge past forests and sparse agricultural fields, enjoying a delicious, typical Nepali meal prepared by local hosts.

itinerary.title: Trek to Latinath & Drive to Gokuleshwar (822m)
itinerary.details: A pleasant 4-hour downhill hike to Latinath, followed by a scenic 2-hour Jeep ride back to Gokuleshwar.

itinerary.title: Drive to Dhangadhi (109m)
itinerary.details: An early start for the 9-hour drive back through the hills on the Mahakali Highway to the comfort of your tourist-standard hotel in Dhangadhi.

itinerary.title: Fly back to Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Take a scenic morning flight back to the capital. Spend the afternoon resting or strolling the vibrant markets of Thamel.

itinerary.title: Departure Day
itinerary.details: Enjoy your final morning in Nepal before our team transfers you to the airport for your journey home.

treks.additionalInfo: The Api Base Camp trek ventures into one of Nepal's most remote and least-developed regions. You must be prepared for extreme basic conditions, including homestays with no standard amenities and several nights in tented camps. Electricity and Wi-Fi are virtually non-existent; you might find a mobile network only up to Day 6. The trek is rated as 'Hard/Challenging' due to steep, uneven terrain, and altitude, making it suitable only for those with good physical fitness and prior trekking experience. Solo trekking is not allowed in this restricted area. We highly recommend bringing a waterproof duffel bag, a heavy-duty sleeping bag, a portable solar panel, and a comprehensive medical kit.

faqs.question: Is there electricity and Wi-Fi on the Api Base Camp trek?
faqs.answer: Because this is one of the most remote areas in Nepal, there are no Wi-Fi or electricity facilities on the trail. You may find a sporadic mobile network until Day 6. We highly recommend bringing a portable solar panel to charge your devices.

faqs.question: What is the accommodation like on this trek?
faqs.answer: You will experience a mix of very basic local homestays in the lower villages, and expedition-style twin-sharing tented camps as you ascend higher towards the base camp. You must be prepared for a complete lack of modern amenities.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Api Base Camp trek?
faqs.answer: This trek is considered moderate to challenging. It ventures into a remote, unspoiled wilderness with steep ascents, descents, and uneven paths. A strong level of physical fitness and prior trekking experience is highly recommended.

faqs.question: Are solo trekkers allowed in this region?
faqs.answer: No. Because Api is in a highly remote, restricted area, solo trekking is strictly prohibited by the government. You must trek with a registered guide and hold a Restricted Area Permit.

treks.title: Khaptad Trek 11 Days
treks.description: The Khaptad Trek is a highly unique, 11-day journey into the heart of Nepal's remote Far-Western region, exploring the diverse and pristine Khaptad National Park. Named after the revered and mysterious sage 'Khaptad Baba,' who meditated here for over 50 years, this mid-mountain park spans 225 sq km of truly remarkable landscapes. Trekkers will traverse subtropical to temperate forests, medicinal herb-filled meadows, and the stunning rolling grasslands locally known as 'Patans' (around 3,000m). Beyond the spiritual significance of the Khaptad Baba Ashram and Triveni Dham, the area boasts incredible biodiversity, sheltering musk deer, leopards, Himalayan black bears, and over 270 species of birds. This moderate-grade trek offers profound tranquility, a deep connection with nature, and immersive cultural encounters with the local Tharu and Baitadi communities—all far away from the standard tourist crowds.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Explore the breathtaking Khaptad Plateau, famous for its vast, rolling green meadows ('Patans') and serene atmosphere.
Discover immense biodiversity, with opportunities to spot leopards, Himalayan black bears, and over 270 bird species.
Visit the sacred Khaptad Baba Ashram, where the revered spiritual saint meditated for more than 50 years.
Experience spiritual tranquility at Triveni Dham (the confluence of three rivers) and the scenic Khaptad Lake.
Immerse yourself in the unique cultures, traditional farming practices, and vibrant festivals of the local Tharu and Baitadi communities.
Enjoy a truly remote and peaceful trekking experience, far away from the crowded trails of central Nepal.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Transfer to your hotel, attend a trip briefing, and enjoy a warm Nepalese welcome dinner with cultural dancing.

itinerary.title: Fly to Dhangadhi (109m)
itinerary.details: Take a scenic 75-minute flight to Dhangadhi. Enjoy a cycling trip to Jokhar Lake, the Botanical Garden, and the unique Aircraft Museum.

itinerary.title: Drive from Dhangadhi to Silgadhi (1,340m)
itinerary.details: Enjoy an 8-9 hour scenic, and sometimes thrilling, Jeep ride through the steep green hills to the beautiful Silgadhi Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Trek to Jhingrana (2,250m)
itinerary.details: Hike from Silgadhi through Baghlekh, spotting wild red berries and traditional mud houses, before arriving at Jhingrana, the park's entrance (7-8 hours).

itinerary.title: Trek to Khaptad National Park (2,900m)
itinerary.details: Climb through beautiful wildflowers, pine forests, and pasture lands to reach the park headquarters near the army barrack (8-9 hours).

itinerary.title: Explore Khaptad National Park
itinerary.details: Wake early for a stunning sunrise view. Visit the serene Khaptad Baba Ashram and hike to Ghodedawan, the park's largest pasture.

itinerary.title: Hike to Sahasra Linga (3,200m)
itinerary.details: Trek to the highest point of the park to visit the sacred temple of Sahasra Linga, enjoying enthralling panoramic views and potential wildlife encounters.

itinerary.title: Trek to Chainpur (1,296m)
itinerary.details: Descend north through friendly villages to Tamil (7-8 hours), followed by a short Jeep drive to Chainpur for a comfortable hotel stay.

itinerary.title: Drive to Dhangadhi (109m)
itinerary.details: Take a highly scenic 10-hour Jeep ride back to Dhangadhi, stopping for lunch along the way.

itinerary.title: Fly back to Kathmandu (1,400m)
itinerary.details: Take a scenic morning flight back to the capital. Spend the afternoon resting or strolling the vibrant markets of Thamel.

itinerary.title: Departure Day
itinerary.details: Enjoy your final morning in Nepal before our team transfers you to the airport for your journey home.

treks.additionalInfo: The Khaptad Trek is a highly unique journey that blends spiritual pilgrimage with remote wilderness exploration. The Khaptad National Park is relatively undeveloped for mass tourism, meaning accommodations in places like Jhingrana and the park headquarters are very basic teahouses or simple guest houses. The trek is rated as 'Moderate' and requires a basic level of fitness to handle 6-8 hour walking days at elevations up to 3,300m. The best times to visit are Spring (March-May) to see the meadows in full bloom, and Autumn (September-November) for crystal clear skies. Ensure you bring sufficient warm clothing, as temperatures drop significantly on the plateau at night.

faqs.question: Will somebody come to pick me up at the airport upon my arrival?
faqs.answer: Yes! Our airport representative will be waiting to greet you outside the airport terminal holding our company signboard. You will then be transferred directly to your hotel in a private tourist vehicle.

faqs.question: Can I obtain a visa for Nepal upon arrival at the airport?
faqs.answer: Yes, most nationalities can easily obtain a visa on arrival at Tribhuvan International Airport in Kathmandu. You will need a valid passport (with at least 6 months validity), passport-sized photos, and cash (USD/EUR/GBP) for the fee.

faqs.question: What is the accommodation like on the Khaptad Trek?
faqs.answer: Accommodation in Kathmandu, Dhangadhi, and Chainpur will be in comfortable, tourist-standard hotels. However, during the trekking days within and around the National Park, you will stay in very basic, traditional teahouses or simple guest houses.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Khaptad Trek?
faqs.answer: The trek is graded as Moderate. While the maximum altitude is relatively low (3,300m), you will still be walking for 6 to 8 hours on some days over uneven, hilly terrain. A basic level of physical fitness is required.

treks.title: Dhorpatan Dolpo Trek, 30 Days
treks.description: The Dhorpatan Dolpo Trek is a strenuous 30-day expedition that covers numerous high passes, deep jungle ravines, and crosses the main Himalayan chain. It traverses the Dhorpatan Hunting Reserve and Shey Phoksundo National Park, both lying in the rain shadow of the Himalayas in central North-West Nepal. This vast, sparsely populated wilderness hides an incredibly rich array of flora and fauna, making for some of the best, untouched trekking in Nepal. Starting from Beni and culminating in Dolpo (Juphal), this historically significant route follows the migration paths of the Khas people in the late Middle Ages, a trail made famous by Peter Matthiessen's 'The Snow Leopard'. Because it navigates extreme remote areas and high-altitude passes like Numala and Bagala, it is heavily recommended only for highly experienced trekkers seeking profound isolation, virgin Tibetan culture, and raw natural beauty.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Experience breathtaking views of the sparkling Dhaulagiri range (8,167m), Gurja Himal, Churen Himal, and Putha Hiunchuli.
Explore the Dhorpatan Hunting Reserve, Nepal's only hunting reserve, renowned for its diverse wildlife and pristine ecosystems.
Immerse yourself in the vibrant, virgin Tibetan culture of Dolpo, discovering ancient Bon Buddhism practices and remote monasteries.
Marvel at the serene, crystal-clear waters of Phoksundo Lake, the crown jewel of the Shey Phoksundo National Park.
Conquer the grueling but immensely rewarding high-altitude Numala and Bagala passes.
Walk the historical migration route of the Khas people, famously chronicled in Peter Matthiessen's 'The Snow Leopard'.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Dhorpatan Dolpo Trek?
faqs.answer: This is a strenuous, Grade 3 Hard/Challenging trek. It covers 300km over 30 days, crosses high-altitude passes over 5,300m, and navigates extremely remote, rugged terrain. It is highly recommended only for experienced trekkers.

faqs.question: Is this trek suitable for solo travelers?
faqs.answer: Due to the extreme remoteness of the Dhorpatan and Dolpo regions, and the necessity of restricted area permits, solo trekking is not permitted. You must trek with an organized group and a licensed guide.

faqs.question: What is the historical significance of this route?
faqs.answer: This route connects the Karnali basin to the Gandaki River basin and follows the historical migration paths of the Khas people from the late Middle Ages. It is also the route famously described in Peter Matthiessen’s acclaimed book, 'The Snow Leopard'.

treks.title: Kathmandu Chitwan Lumbini Pokhara Tour
treks.description: The 9 Nights 10 Days Nepal Tour Package is the ultimate 'Golden Triangle Plus' experience, perfectly combining Nepal's rich history, profound religion, dramatic mountain scenery, and thrilling wildlife. The journey begins in Kathmandu, the 'City of Temples,' exploring UNESCO World Heritage Sites like Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath, Pashupatinath, and Boudhanath. Next, you will head to the tropical jungles of Chitwan National Park for a 2-night/3-day safari, seeking out the rare one-horned rhinoceros and Royal Bengal tiger via jeep safari and canoe. The spiritual heart of the trip awaits in Lumbini, the sacred birthplace of Lord Buddha, where you'll visit the Mayadevi Temple and international monasteries. Finally, the tour culminates in the breathtaking city of Pokhara—a true paradise on earth. Here, you'll boat on the tranquil Phewa Lake, witness a mesmerizing sunrise over the Annapurna range from Sarangkot, and explore mysterious caves and waterfalls.
highlights: Explore the cultural heart of Nepal with guided tours of Kathmandu's ancient Durbar Squares, Pashupatinath, and Boudhanath Stupa.
Embark on an exhilarating Jeep Safari in Chitwan National Park to spot one-horned rhinos, Royal Bengal tigers, and crocodiles.
Experience a profound spiritual awakening in Lumbini, the sacred birthplace of Siddhartha Gautama (Lord Buddha).
Witness a mesmerizing sunrise over the majestic Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges from Sarangkot Hill.
Enjoy a tranquil boating experience on the serene waters of Phewa Lake in the picturesque city of Pokhara.
The ultimate combination of culture, religion, wildlife, and natural Himalayan beauty in a single 10-day trip.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu & Welcome Dinner
itinerary.details: Transfer to your hotel, attend a trip briefing, and enjoy a warm Nepalese welcome dinner with a cultural dance show.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu UNESCO World Heritage Sightseeing
itinerary.details: Visit iconic sites including Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), Pashupatinath Temple, and Boudhanath Stupa.

itinerary.title: Drive to Chitwan National Park & Tharu Village Tour
itinerary.details: Drive in a private luxury vehicle to Chitwan. In the afternoon, explore the local Tharu ethnic village and enjoy a cultural show at night.

itinerary.title: Full Day Jungle Safari in Chitwan
itinerary.details: Experience an exhilarating jeep safari deep in the jungle. Enjoy bird watching, canoeing, and a visit to the elephant and crocodile breeding centers.

itinerary.title: Drive to Lumbini & Explore the Sacred Garden
itinerary.details: Travel to Lumbini in the southern lowlands. Visit the Mayadevi Temple (the exact birthplace of Buddha), the Ashoka Pillar, and the sacred Pushkarini pond.

itinerary.title: Tour of International Monasteries in Lumbini
itinerary.details: Spend the day exploring the incredible modern Buddhist stupas, Chaityas, and monasteries built by nations from around the world.

itinerary.title: Drive to Pokhara & Evening Boating on Phewa Lake
itinerary.details: Drive through scenic mountain roads to Pokhara. In the evening, relax with a tranquil boat ride on Phewa Lake, enjoying views of the Annapurna range.

itinerary.title: Pokhara City Tour
itinerary.details: Visit mysterious caves like Mahendra Cave and Gupteshwor Mahadev, marvel at the 'Patale Chhaga' (Davis Falls), and explore the International Mountain Museum.

itinerary.title: Early Morning Sarangkot Sunrise & Drive to Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Drive 45 minutes up to Sarangkot Hill for a breathtaking sunrise over the Himalayas. Afterward, drive back to Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Final Departure
itinerary.details: Enjoy your final morning in Nepal before our team transfers you to the airport for your journey home.

treks.additionalInfo: This tour is perfect for new couples, honeymoon trips, and family tours due to its comfortable pace and luxury transportation. It is suitable year-round, including December and throughout the winter. You will be staying in high-quality 3-star hotels with all modern amenities. The drive times between cities can take several hours, but you will be traveling comfortably in a private luxury tourist vehicle.

faqs.question: Is this tour suitable for families and children?
faqs.answer: Absolutely! Graded as 'Easy', this tour utilizes private luxury tourist vehicles and comfortable hotels, making it perfect for families, children, and older adults.

faqs.question: What is the best time of year to do this tour?
faqs.answer: This tour is accessible and highly enjoyable in all seasons. It is particularly pleasant during the autumn, spring, and even throughout the winter months like December.

faqs.question: Are the jungle safaris in Chitwan safe?
faqs.answer: Yes, our jungle activities are extremely safe. You will be accompanied by experienced, state-licensed nature guides during the jeep safari and canoe rides.

faqs.question: Do I need any special permits or vaccinations for this trip?
faqs.answer: No specialized trekking permits are required for this tour. However, standard national park and heritage site entrance fees are required, which are fully included in the package cost.

treks.title: Namobuddha to Panauti Day Hiking 1 Day
treks.description: The Namobuddha to Panauti Day Hike is a magnificent, one-day excursion exploring the sacred and historic sites just southeast of the Kathmandu Valley. Your journey begins at the hilltop monastery of Namobuddha, one of Nepal's most significant Buddhist pilgrimage sites. Adorned with fluttering prayer flags and intricately carved sculptures, the monastery radiates a serene aura where you can witness devoted monks chanting their daily mantras. From this high vantage point, enjoy breathtaking views of the lush landscapes and, on clear days, the distant northern Himalayan massifs. After absorbing the tranquil energy of Namobuddha, you will embark on a highly scenic, three-hour descent through beautiful terraced fields and charming Tamang and Newar settlements. Your hike concludes in the ancient town of Panauti, situated at the confluence of two small rivers. Incredibly preserved despite its proximity to the capital, Panauti offers a deep dive into traditional Newari architecture and culture.
highlights: Visit the sacred Namobuddha Monastery, a major Buddhist pilgrimage site renowned for its serene atmosphere and devoted monks.
Enjoy a pleasant, scenic 3-hour hike traversing beautiful terraced fields and lush forests.
Explore the remarkably preserved ancient Newari town of Panauti, experiencing deeply rooted local art, traditions, and architecture.
Visit the historic 14th-century Indreswor Mahadev Temple, the Radhakrishna Temple, and the local traditional museum.
Observe the traditional, untouched lifestyles of the local Tamang and Newari communities.
Catch splendid panoramic views of the northern Himalayan massifs from the Namobuddha hilltop on a clear day.

itinerary.title: Drive to Namobuddha, Hike to Panauti, Return to Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Start the day with a drive to the sacred hilltop monastery of Namobuddha. Spend time observing the monks and enjoying the panoramic views. Begin the 3-hour scenic descent through terraced fields and small villages towards the ancient town of Panauti. Explore the 14th-century Indreswor Mahadev Temple and the unique Newari architecture of Panauti before driving back to your hotel in Kathmandu.

costIncludes: Private Car with Driver

treks.additionalInfo: This day hike is a fantastic, accessible way to experience Nepal's culture and nature without committing to a multi-day trek. The trail involves some uphill and downhill sections on dirt roads and village paths, but it is entirely manageable for beginners and families. Wear comfortable hiking shoes, a sun hat, and bring a water bottle. No trekking permits are required for this route.

faqs.question: How long does the Namobuddha to Panauti Day Hike take?
faqs.answer: The hiking portion of the trip takes around 3 to 4 hours of walking. The entire excursion, including the drives to and from Kathmandu and sightseeing, takes about 6 to 7 hours depending on your pace.

faqs.question: What is the difficulty level of this hike?
faqs.answer: The hike is considered easy to moderate. The trail is mostly downhill from Namobuddha to Panauti, though there are a few short steep sections. It is perfectly manageable for most hikers, including beginners.

faqs.question: Is it safe to hike Namobuddha to Panauti without a guide?
faqs.answer: While it is physically possible, we highly recommend our professional guide for safety and convenience. The trail can be tricky to navigate, and a guide provides invaluable historical and cultural context to the sites.

faqs.question: What is the best time to do this hike?
faqs.answer: The best time is from October to May when the weather is dry and sunny. It is accessible during the monsoon (June-September), but the trails can become muddy and slippery.

treks.title: Rara Lake Trek 7 Days
treks.description: Rara Lake (also known as Mahendra Daha) is the sparkling gem of the far-western Himalayan range. Situated at a comfortable elevation of 2,990 meters, this short 7-day trek offers an incredible, altitude-sickness-free adventure into pristine isolation. The journey requires two scenic flights from Kathmandu—first to Nepalgunj, then to the remote Talcha Airport. From there, a 2 to 3-hour walk through offbeat terrain leads you to Nepal's largest and deepest lake (167m deep). Set within the Rara National Park, the area boasts incredible biodiversity, including red pandas, Himalayan black bears, and musk deer. The highlight is the mesmerizing turquoise-blue water of the lake, which sparkles like precious gemstones under the sun, alongside the panoramic vistas from Murma Viewpoint (3,630m). Though trekking infrastructure is basic, the utter tranquility and untouched landscapes make it a deeply rewarding experience.
highlights: Discover Rara Lake (Mahendra Daha), Nepal's largest and deepest lake, famous for its sparkling turquoise-blue waters.
Enjoy an altitude-sickness-free trek, with the lake situated at a comfortable elevation of 2,990m.
Take two thrilling domestic flights from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, and up to the remote Talcha Airport.
Explore the diverse wildlife of Rara National Park, home to red pandas, Himalayan black bears, and musk deer.
Hike up to Murma Viewpoint (3,630m) for a heavenly, panoramic view of the lake and surrounding snowbound mountains.
Experience profound peace and pristine, uncrowded trails in the remote Karnali Region.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu & Trip Preparation
itinerary.details: Arrive in Kathmandu. Transfer to your hotel and prepare for the journey ahead.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj
itinerary.details: Take a scenic domestic flight to Nepalgunj in the hot plains of south-western Nepal. Overnight in a hotel.

itinerary.title: Fly to Talcha Airport & Trek to Rara Lake
itinerary.details: Take a thrilling morning flight to the remote Talcha Airport. From there, hike for 2-3 hours through offbeat terrain to reach the stunning Rara Lake.

itinerary.title: Explore Rara Lake & Hike to Murma Viewpoint (3,630m)
itinerary.details: Spend the day exploring the turquoise lake. Ascend to Murma Viewpoint for a breathtaking panoramic view of the lake and mountains.

itinerary.title: Explore Local Villages & Trek back to Talcha
itinerary.details: Visit nearby villages to observe the local lifestyle and culture before trekking back to Talcha.

itinerary.title: Fly Talcha to Nepalgunj to Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Take a flight from Talcha back to Nepalgunj, and connect with a flight back to the capital city of Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Final Departure
itinerary.details: Enjoy your final morning in Kathmandu before transferring to the airport for your journey home.
