treks.additionalInfo: While Rara Lake is stunning, the trekking infrastructure in the Karnali region is basic. You will be staying in simple local teahouses or lodges. We highly recommend bringing ample personal snacks for the journey, as options on the trail are limited. The maximum trekking altitude is very safe at 3,150m (or 3,630m if you hike to Murma Viewpoint), making it accessible for trekkers concerned about altitude sickness.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Rara Lake Trek?
faqs.answer: The trek is graded as 'Easy'. Because the lake is at a relatively low altitude (2,990m) and the walking distances from the Talcha airport are short (2-3 hours), it is perfectly suitable for beginners.

faqs.question: How do we travel to Rara Lake?
faqs.answer: To save time and avoid long, arduous drives, we take two domestic flights: first from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj, and then from Nepalgunj to the remote Talcha Airport. From there, it's a short hike to the lake.

faqs.question: What kind of wildlife might I see in Rara National Park?
faqs.answer: Rara National Park is incredibly biodiverse. Lucky trekkers might spot red pandas, Himalayan black bears, jackals, musk deer, and a massive variety of bird species.

faqs.question: Is there a risk of altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: The risk is extremely low. The lake is situated at 2,990 meters, which is well below the threshold where altitude sickness typically becomes a serious concern. It is a great altitude-sickness-free alternative to higher Himalayan treks.

treks.title: Mohare Danda Trek 8 Days
treks.description: The Mohare Danda Trek is an emerging eco-community trekking route located between the gorges of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountains. It is one of the best alternative trails to expedite the Annapurna Himalayan region in a short amount of time, offering unspoiled natural and cultural gems without the crowds of popular paths like the Annapurna Circuit or Ghorepani Poon Hill. Elevated at an altitude of 3,300m, Mohare Danda provides magnificent panoramic views, especially during sunrise. Crafted by well-known Nepali social entrepreneur Mahabir Pun, this trail focuses on uplifting the living standards of indigenous Magar and Gurung communities through eco-tourism. Trekkers can experience a mesmerizing amalgamation of vibrant culture, traditional lifestyles, and breathtaking natural scenery, making it one of the greatest short-duration, budget, and family-friendly voyages.
highlights: Experience breathtaking, panoramic views of the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri mountain ranges, including Machhapuchhre (Fishtail) and Nilgiri.
Participate in a pioneering eco-community trekking project, supporting sustainable tourism and local homestays.
Immerse yourself in the rich culture and traditional lifestyles of the indigenous Magar and Gurung communities.
Trek through diverse, lush forests of rhododendron, oak, bamboo, and pine, alongside beautiful waterfalls.
Witness the magical sunrise over the Himalayas from the stunning 3,300m vantage point of Mohare Danda.
Visit sacred cultural sites, including the Galeshwor Temple and the Naangi Barahi Temple.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara
itinerary.details: Drive from the capital city of Kathmandu to the stunning lakeside city of Pokhara (822m). The journey takes around 4-5 hours.

itinerary.title: Drive to Galeshwor & Trek to Bans Kharka
itinerary.details: Drive along the Kali Gandaki River to Galeshwor for lunch. Begin an uphill climb, crossing a suspension bridge, to spend the night at Bans Kharka (1,526m).

itinerary.title: Trek to Naangi
itinerary.details: Hike for 5-6 hours passing by beautiful, tiny traditional villages with stunning backdrops of towering mountain ranges. Stay overnight at an eco-friendly lodge in Naangi (2,260m).

itinerary.title: Trek to Mohare Danda
itinerary.details: Trek through lovely forests of oak and rhododendron. Reach the stunning 3,300m vantage point of Mohare Danda for an epic sunset over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges.

itinerary.title: Hike to Deurali via Ghorepani
itinerary.details: Wake up for a mesmerizing sunrise. The trail then leads you through simultaneous steep ups and downs to reach Deurali (3,200m) via Ghorepani.

itinerary.title: Trek to Ghandruk Village
itinerary.details: Descend into stunning woodlands and highly cultivated lands to reach Ghandruk (2,012m), a supreme vantage point providing extraordinary views of Annapurna South and Machhapuchhare.

itinerary.title: Trek to Nayapul & Drive to Pokhara
itinerary.details: Descend to Nayapul (1,070m) through stone-paved trails and terrace farms. Drive back to Pokhara for a relaxing evening by the lake.

itinerary.title: Drive back to Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Drive back to Kathmandu via a private vehicle. Enjoy a stop at the holy shrine of Manakamana Temple via cable car before returning to your hotel.

treks.additionalInfo: The Mohare Danda Trek is an excellent, affordable, family-friendly classic tea house trekking experience. Because it is a community eco-tourism project, your participation directly helps improve the livelihoods of villagers and aids conservation efforts in the region. The trails are locally trodden, well established, and comparatively easy, making it an incredible alternative to the more heavily trafficked routes.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Mohare Danda Trek?
faqs.answer: Graded as 'Moderate', it is highly suitable for beginners and families who possess a reasonable level of physical fitness. The maximum altitude is 3,300m, keeping the risk of acute mountain sickness very low.

faqs.question: What makes this trek eco-friendly?
faqs.answer: The trek is part of a community-managed eco-tourism project initiated by Mahabir Pun. You stay in community lodges and homestays, which means your spending directly supports the local economy and conservation efforts.

faqs.question: Do I need any special permits?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) permit and a TIMS card. Both of these are fully included in the price of your package.

treks.title: Ghorepani Poon Hill Trekking with Hot Springs-5 Days
treks.description: The Ghorepani Poon Hill Trek with Hot Springs is a quick, easy, and highly accessible 5-day adventure into the foothills of the revered Annapurna range. This family-friendly journey is the perfect introduction for beginners looking to experience the Himalayas without the worry of severe high-altitude sickness. The trek takes you up the famous stone steps of Ulleri, winding through lush forests of oak and vibrant rhododendron (especially spectacular when blooming in spring), and passing through traditional Gurung and Magar villages like Ghandruk. The absolute pinnacle of the trip is the early morning hike to Poon Hill (3,210m), which offers an unparalleled, golden sunrise over a stunning panorama of snow-capped giants, including Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), Annapurna South, and Dhaulagiri. To top off the adventure, the trek concludes with a deeply relaxing soak in the naturally heated geothermal waters of the Jhinu Danda Hot Springs, soothing your tired muscles before heading back to Pokhara.
highlights: Witness an iconic, golden sunrise over the Himalayas from the famous Poon Hill viewpoint (3,210m).
Soak your tired muscles and relax in the naturally heated geothermal waters of the Jhinu Danda Hot Springs.
Trek through vibrant, lush forests of oak and beautiful rhododendron that burst into color during the spring.
Immerse yourself in the rich culture and renowned warm hospitality of the traditional Gurung and Magar communities.
Ascend the famous, steep stone stairs of Ulleri village, a challenging but highly memorable part of the trail.
Enjoy a short, highly accessible trek that is perfectly suited for beginners, families, and children.

itinerary.title: Drive from Pokhara to Nayapul and hike to Ulleri (1970m)
itinerary.details: Drive for 1.5 hours to Nayapul. From there, follow the Modi River through several villages before ascending the famous stone steps to Ulleri (7 hrs).

itinerary.title: Trek to Ghorepani from Ulleri (2860m)
itinerary.details: Wake up to majestic views of the Annapurna ranges. Trek for 5 hours across lush rhododendron forests to reach Ghorepani.

itinerary.title: Hike to Poon Hill Viewpoint (3210m) & Trek to Tadapani (2,600m)
itinerary.details: Wake up early for a 1-hour hike to Poon Hill to witness an astonishing sunrise. Afterward, trek 6-7 hours through beautiful forests to Tadapani.

itinerary.title: Trek to Jhinu Hot Spring Via Chhomrong (1780m)
itinerary.details: Descend for 5-6 hours through the beautiful Gurung village of Ghandruk and Chhomrong. Arrive at Jhinu Danda and spend a couple of hours soaking in the natural hot springs.

itinerary.title: Short walk from Jhinu Danda & Drive to Pokhara (822m)
itinerary.details: After breakfast, enjoy a short walk to catch a private jeep. Drive for 3 hours back to the lakeside city of Pokhara to conclude the trip.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Poon Hill Trek?
faqs.answer: This trek is considered Easy to Moderate. It is an excellent choice for beginners and families as the trails are well-maintained and the maximum altitude is relatively low.

faqs.question: When is the best time to do this trek?
faqs.answer: While accessible year-round, Spring (March to May) is highly recommended as the dense rhododendron forests are in full, vibrant bloom.

faqs.question: Is there a risk of altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: The risk is minimal. The highest point you will sleep is 2,860m at Ghorepani. You only briefly reach 3,210m at the Poon Hill viewpoint for the sunrise.

treks.title: Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek -19 Days
treks.description: The Kanchenjunga Circuit Trek is an untouched, hidden treasure in the far eastern Himalayas of Nepal bordering Sikkim, India. This remote and highly adventurous 19-day expedition takes you around the third-highest mountain in the world, Mt. Kanchenjunga (8,586m). Because the region is heavily protected and requires special restricted area permits, the trails remain uncrowded, pristine, and incredibly tranquil. The demanding route crosses lush subtropical jungles, high alpine meadows, and the stunning Yalung Glacier, ultimately leading to both the North (Pangpema) and South (Oktang) base camps. Along this magical journey, you will immerse yourself in the rich, traditional cultures of the Sherpa, Limbu, and Rai communities. If luck is on your side, you may spot rare wildlife like the elusive snow leopard, red panda, and Himalayan black bear. This Grade 3 trek is significantly more difficult than popular routes like the Annapurna or Manaslu Circuits, making it a perfect match for experienced trekkers seeking raw, unparalleled wilderness.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Gaze upon the majestic Mt. Kanchenjunga (8,586m), the third-tallest mountain in the world, alongside peaks like Mt. Jannu and Tent Peak.
Reach both the spectacular Pangpema (North) and Oktang (South) base camps for profound panoramic views.
Trek through an exclusive, highly restricted area of Nepal, guaranteeing uncrowded and pristine wilderness trails.
Traverse incredibly diverse landscapes, ranging from subtropical jungles and rhododendron forests to vast glacial zones.
Immerse yourself in the authentic Tibetan Buddhist culture of traditional Sherpa, Limbu, and Rai ethnic villages.
Encounter rare and endangered wildlife in the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area, including red pandas and snow leopards.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Our airport representative will transfer you to your hotel. Rest and explore Thamel in the evening.

itinerary.title: Trek Permit Preparation Day
itinerary.details: Meet the team manager to submit your original passport for the restrictive permit preparation. Optional sightseeing tour in the afternoon.

itinerary.title: Fly to Bhadrapur & Drive to Taplejung (1820m)
itinerary.details: Take a 45-minute domestic flight to Bhadrapur, then hop in a local jeep for a scenic 7-9 hour drive through the tea cultivations of Kanyam to Taplejung.

itinerary.title: Drive to Sekathum (1650m)
itinerary.details: To save time, take a jeep through Mitlung, Chirwa, and Lelep to Sekathum. Your National Park and Restricted Area permits will be checked along the way.

itinerary.title: Trek to Amjilosa (2498m)
itinerary.details: Begin your trek ascending alongside the Ghunsa Khola, crossing numerous bridges and verdant forests before reaching Amjilosa.

itinerary.title: Trek to Gyabla (2725m)
itinerary.details: Hike through dense forests devoid of human settlement. Keep an eye out for red pandas and enjoy magnificent waterfalls before reaching Gyabla.

itinerary.title: Trek to Ghunsa (3415m)
itinerary.details: Trek through lush woodlands packed with flora and fauna to reach the Tibetan-influenced village of Ghunsa.

itinerary.title: Trek to Khambachen (4145m)
itinerary.details: Ascend through pine forests with chances to spot blue sheep and snow leopards. Enjoy spectacular views of Mt. Jannu before arriving in Khambachen.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization and Rest Day
itinerary.details: Rest in Khambachen. Take a short hike to nearby glaciers, lakes, and viewpoints to help your body adjust to the extreme altitude.

itinerary.title: Trek to Lhonak (4792m)
itinerary.details: Navigate the challenging junction of the Lhonak and Kanchenjunga glaciers, passing the Ramdang Monastery to reach the tiny settlement of Lhonak.

itinerary.title: Hike to Kanchenjunga North Base Camp (Pang Pema, 5143m)
itinerary.details: Hike along the moraines to Pang Pema, the Kanchenjunga North Base Camp, to witness the breathtaking towering peaks. Return to Lhonak.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Ghunsa (3415m)
itinerary.details: Retrace your steps past the stone huts, rock-falling zones, and soaring peaks to return to Ghunsa.

itinerary.title: Trek to Sele Le Base Camp (4240m)
itinerary.details: Trek through dense forests to the isolated human settlement of Sele Le. Snow leopard sightings are possible here.

itinerary.title: Trek to Tseram via High Passes (3868m)
itinerary.details: Cross several high-altitude passes including Sinion La (4440m) and Mirgin La (4480m) for panoramic views of Everest, Makalu, and Kanchenjunga.

itinerary.title: Hike to Oktang (South Base Camp Viewpoint, 4740m)
itinerary.details: Hike along the Yalung glacier to Oktang to enjoy stunning close-up views of the three summits of Mt. Kanchenjunga. Return to Tseram.

itinerary.title: Trek to Tortong (2980m)
itinerary.details: Enjoy a tranquil downhill descent through vibrant rhododendron forests to reach Tortong.

itinerary.title: Trek to Yamphudin (1692m)
itinerary.details: Descend steeply to the Amji Khola and pass through Lamite Bhanjyang before arriving at Yamphudin, where your permits will be checked again.

itinerary.title: Drive to Bhadrapur
itinerary.details: Conclude your trekking and take a long, scenic drive back to the plains of Bhadrapur.

itinerary.title: Fly to Kathmandu & Final Departure
itinerary.details: Take a morning flight back to Kathmandu. Transfer to the airport for your journey home.

It demands prior trekking experience and excellent physical fitness due to the extreme altitudes (up to 5,143m) and the rugged, remote terrain. faqs.question: Why is this a restricted area?
faqs.answer: The Kanchenjunga region is heavily protected to preserve its pristine environment, unique wildlife, and indigenous cultures, as well as due to its sensitive border with India/Sikkim.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Kanchenjunga Circuit?
faqs.answer: It is very challenging. The 19-day duration, extreme remoteness, and multiple days above 4,000m make it suitable only for experienced, highly fit trekkers.

faqs.question: Can I trek to Kanchenjunga solo?
faqs.answer: No, the Nepalese government strictly prohibits solo trekking in the Kanchenjunga Restricted Area. You must trek with a registered guide and hold a special restricted area permit.

treks.title: Everest Base Camp via Jiri 26 Days
treks.description: The Everest Base Camp and Gokyo Lakes Trek via Jiri is a spectacular, budget-friendly 26-day alternative for adventurers who wish to explore the Khumbu region without taking the nerve-wracking flight to Lukla. Beginning with a scenic drive to the lower Solu region (Bhandara), this classic overland route combines the traditional EBC trek with the stunning Gokyo Lakes and the challenging Cho La Pass (5,420m). As you ascend through dense forests and picturesque Sherpa villages, you will cross thrilling suspension bridges and visit ancient monasteries, completely immersing yourself in the local culture. The trek rewards you with the breathtaking turquoise Gokyo Lakes (the highest freshwater lakes in the world), the majestic Ngozumpa Glacier, and an epic sunrise from Kala Patthar (5,545m). Without the stress of a mountain flight, this adventurous journey offers an authentic, profound, and deeply satisfying exploration of the lap of Mt. Everest (8,848m) alongside towering giants like Lhotse, Makalu, and Cho Oyu.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Skip the flight to Lukla and enjoy a classic, overland trek starting from the lower Solu region (Jiri/Bhandara).
Conquer the legendary Everest Base Camp (5,364m) and witness the world's highest peak up close.
Climb Kala Patthar (5,545m) for unparalleled, golden sunrise views over Mt. Everest and the Khumbu glacier.
Explore the vibrant, turquoise glacial waters of the sacred Gokyo Lakes and the massive Ngozumpa Glacier.
Test your endurance by crossing the challenging, high-altitude Cho La Pass (5,420m).
Immerse yourself in authentic Sherpa culture, visiting bustling Namche Bazaar and the majestic Tengboche Monastery.

itinerary.title: Arrive at Tribhuvan International Airport (TIA) (1400m)
itinerary.details: Land at the international airport in Kathmandu. Our team will welcome you and drive you to the hotel for a welcome dinner.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Bamti Bhandara by Bus (1520m)
itinerary.details: After a scrumptious breakfast, begin a scenic, 7-8 hour drive towards the lower Solu region of Bhandara.

itinerary.title: Trek Bhandara to Kinja (1630m)
itinerary.details: Begin trekking on a downhill path that leads to the Likhu Khola. Kinja is situated right on the bank of the river.

itinerary.title: Trek Kinja to Lamjura La (3530m)
itinerary.details: Ascend through farmhouses and lush rhododendron forests to Lamjura La, offering a breathtaking view of Pikey Peak.

itinerary.title: Trek Lamjura-la to Junbeshi (2700m)
itinerary.details: Descend through a forested path to Taktor, and continue trekking towards the beautiful Sherpa village of Junbesi.

itinerary.title: Trek Junbesi to Nunthala (2330m) via Taksindu Pass
itinerary.details: Catch your first glimpse of Mt. Everest today! Cross the Taksindu La pass and descend through dense forests to reach Nunthala.

itinerary.title: Trek Nunthala to Bupsa (2360m)
itinerary.details: Pass by Khari Khola, cross a suspension bridge, and continue walking up to Bupsa, situated on a scenic hilltop.

itinerary.title: Trek Bupsa to Chauri Kharka/Phakding (2660m)
itinerary.details: Gradually trek towards Chauri Kharka or Phakding village, joining the busy, main Khumbu trekking trail just below Lukla.

itinerary.title: Trek to Namche Bazaar (3440m)
itinerary.details: Walk through dense forests and cross suspension bridges before a steep, 1.5-hour ascent to Namche Bazaar, the Sherpa capital.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day in Namche Bazaar (3440m)
itinerary.details: Rest day! Hike up to the Everest View Hotel for stunning panoramas, then explore the shops, cafes, and museums in Namche.

itinerary.title: Trek Namche to Dhole (4110m)
itinerary.details: Follow the gorgeous trail to Mong La Pass (3,972m), descend to the Dudh Koshi River, and trek through green pastures to Dhole.

itinerary.title: Trek Dhole to Machhermo (4470m)
itinerary.details: Walk uphill following a steep route through Lhabarma and Luza, enjoying the refreshing scent of scrub junipers and fabulous views.

itinerary.title: Trek Machhermo to Gokyo (4790m)
itinerary.details: Walk along the terminal moraine of the Ngozumpa glacier. Pass the first and second lakes to reach the picturesque Gokyo village.

itinerary.title: Excursion day to Fifth Gokyo Lake
itinerary.details: Hike to the stunning fifth Gokyo Lake, surrounded by towering snow-capped mountains. Return to the village to relax.

itinerary.title: Trek Gokyo to Dragnak (4750m)
itinerary.details: Wake up early and hike to Gokyo Ri (5,357m) for a breathtaking sunrise. Afterward, begin trekking downhill toward Thangna/Dragnak.

itinerary.title: Trek Thangnak to Dzongla (4830m) via Cho La pass (5368m)
itinerary.details: Get ready for a difficult day. Ascend the steep, slippery Cho La Pass, crossing a glacier, before descending to Dzongla.

itinerary.title: Trek Dzongla to Gorak Shep (5170m)
itinerary.details: Continue walking alongside the Khumbu glacier on a smooth path to Lobuche, then ascend further to Gorak Shep.

itinerary.title: Excursion to Everest Base Camp (5364m) & Return to Gorakshep
itinerary.details: Walk along the lateral moraine to reach the legendary Everest Base Camp! Take plenty of pictures before returning to Gorakshep.

itinerary.title: Sunrise at Kala Patthar (5545m) & Trek to Pheriche (4240m)
itinerary.details: Trek early in the freezing cold to Kala Patthar for the ultimate, unobstructed sunrise view of Mt. Everest. Descend to Pheriche.

itinerary.title: Trek Pheriche to Namche bazaar (3438m)
itinerary.details: Descend through dense rhododendron forests, passing by the majestic Tengboche Monastery, before arriving back in Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Trek Namche Bazar to Monjo (2835m)
itinerary.details: Descend steeply to Jorsale and Monjo. Walk through lush forests and cross lovely streams, leaving the high mountains behind.

itinerary.title: Trek Monjo to Paiya (2730m)
itinerary.details: Begin trekking off the main Lukla trail, heading south through dense forests, terraced fields, and small settlement areas to Paiya.

itinerary.title: Trek Paiya to Nunthala (2330m)
itinerary.details: Enjoy the scenery and the daily lifestyle of the locals as you trek through farming fields back towards Nunthala.

itinerary.title: Trek Nunthala to Salleri (2390m)
itinerary.details: Ascend past fluttering prayer flags to Taksindo, then continue through lush pine forests and hilly gorges to reach Salleri.

itinerary.title: Drive Salleri to Kathmandu by private jeep (1400m)
itinerary.details: Embark on a long 10-12 hour drive along the BP highway, enjoying the views of the Sunkoshi river valley before arriving in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Fly back home
itinerary.details: The 26-day epic adventure ends here. We will drop you at the airport in time for your international departure.

treks.additionalInfo: The Everest Base Camp via Jiri is a classic, overland alternative to the standard EBC trek that avoids the stressful and weather-dependent mountain flight to Lukla. It also offers significantly more time for acclimatization and a chance to experience the less crowded, authentic lower Solu region. This is a Grade 3 Hard/Challenging trek covering 400km over 26 days. Excellent physical stamina and prior trekking experience are highly recommended.

faqs.question: Why choose the Jiri route instead of flying to Lukla?
faqs.answer: The Jiri route is a classic, overland alternative that completely avoids the nerve-wracking and highly weather-dependent mountain flight to Lukla. It also offers more time for acclimatization and a chance to experience the less crowded, authentic lower Solu region.

faqs.question: How difficult is this 26-day trek?
faqs.answer: Graded as Hard/Challenging, this trek covers roughly 400km over 26 days, crosses the high-altitude Cho La Pass (5,420m), and reaches Kala Patthar (5,545m). Excellent physical stamina and prior trekking experience are required.

faqs.question: Is altitude sickness a major concern?
faqs.answer: While altitude is always a risk above 3,000m, the overland approach from Jiri provides significantly more days for your body to gradually acclimatize compared to flying directly into Lukla, dramatically reducing the overall risk.

treks.title: Great Himalaya Trail-Mugu to Humla Region-30 Days
treks.image: /images/Great Himalaya Trail-Kanchenjunga to Makalu Region- 53 Days.jpg
treks.description: The Great Himalaya Trail – Section 6 (Mugu-Humla Region) is a remarkable 30-day expedition traversing the most remote, pristine, and rugged landscapes in northwestern Nepal. Serving as an extension to the Jumla to Rara trek, this 'off the beaten track' journey offers an authentic immersion into the Hidden Himalayas. As you venture through the Karnali gorge, steep mountain passes, and stunning high-altitude valleys, you will witness cultures and ancient Tibetan Buddhist lifestyles that remain entirely untouched by modern changes. Highlights include circling the magnificent Rara Lake (Nepal's largest lake), walking the historic Maoist pilgrimage route, and meeting the friendly indigenous villagers of the Limi Valley who depend heavily on trans-Himalayan salt trade. Featuring 400-1000 year-old monasteries, sprawling pine forests, and breathtaking views of the Saipal and Nalakankar ranges, this incredibly challenging trek provides a true sense of exploration that many believe resembles the mythical Shangri-La.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Embark on an epic, off-the-beaten-track exploratory journey on the Great Himalaya Trail with a genuine sense of adventure.
Witness authentic, untouched cultures that have remained preserved for centuries in the remote Karnali and Humla regions.
Explore the magnificent Rara Lake (Nepal's largest lake), ringed with gorgeous pine, spruce, and juniper forests.
Immerse yourself in rich Tibetan Buddhist heritage, visiting ancient monasteries that date back 400 to 1,000 years.
Traverse incredibly challenging high-altitude terrain, demanding deep physical endurance but rewarding you with unmatched pristine wilderness.
Spot rare high-altitude biodiversity, including possibilities of seeing the elusive snow leopard or valuable Yarsagumba.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu & Transfer to Hotel (1400m)
itinerary.details: Our airport representative will pick you up from the airport and transfer you to a 4-star hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Permit Procedure & Fly to Nepalgunj (150m)
itinerary.details: Morning is spent preparing the necessary restricted area permits. In the afternoon, fly down to the hot plains of Nepalgunj.

itinerary.title: Fly from Nepalgunj to Jumla (2370m)
itinerary.details: Take a scenic mountain flight to Jumla, the starting point of our expedition. Overnight at a tented camp.

itinerary.title: Trek Jumla to Danphe Langa (3130m)
itinerary.details: Begin the Great Himalaya Trail with a 6-hour trek ascending towards Danphe Langa.

itinerary.title: Trek Danphe Langa to Chautha (2770m)
itinerary.details: Trek for 6 hours through remote terrain, moving steeply up and down gorges towards Chautha.

itinerary.title: Trek Chautha to Dhotu (2380m)
itinerary.details: A slightly shorter 5-hour trek, continuing through the rugged province of Humla.

itinerary.title: Trek Dhotu to Rara Lake (3040m)
itinerary.details: Trek for 4 hours to reach the magnificent Rara Lake, Nepal's largest freshwater lake, ringed by pine and spruce forests.

itinerary.title: Exploring Rara Lake
itinerary.details: Spend the day exploring the stunning beauty of Rara National Park. Enjoy the vibrant rhododendrons and the reflection of snow-capped peaks on the water.

itinerary.title: Trek Rara Lake to Luma Village (2110m)
itinerary.details: Leave the lake behind and trek for 6 hours through remote villages where life has remained unchanged for centuries.

itinerary.title: Trek Luma Village to Changkheli (3600m)
itinerary.details: A challenging 6-hour trek gaining significant altitude to reach Changkheli.

itinerary.title: Trek Changkheli to Dharma Village (2550m)
itinerary.details: Descend sharply over 7 hours to the Dharma Village, interacting with locals who depend on the Tibetan salt trade.

itinerary.title: Trek Dharma Village to Melcham (2800m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours through alpine meadows and difficult farming terrain.

itinerary.title: Trek Melcham to Pomkha (2800m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours traversing the ups and downs of the Hidden Himalayas.

itinerary.title: Trek Pomkha to Ghatte (2600m)
itinerary.details: Another challenging 7-hour day navigating the remote Karnali region.

itinerary.title: Trek Ghatte to Simikot (2950m)
itinerary.details: Trek 8 hours to reach Simikot, the administrative center of Humla, deeply connected to ancient trade routes.

itinerary.title: Trek Simikot to Hepka (3500m)
itinerary.details: Ascend for 6 hours away from Simikot into increasingly high-altitude terrain.

itinerary.title: Trek Hepka to Sechi Lagna (4540m)
itinerary.details: A tough 7-hour day pushing well above 4,000m to the high pass of Sechi Lagna.

itinerary.title: Trek Sechi Lagna to Dharamshala (4800m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours to our highest sleeping point of the expedition. The air is thin, and the views are breathtaking.

itinerary.title: Trek Dharamshala to Tankchhe (4200m)
itinerary.details: An 8-hour trek descending slightly into the pristine Limi Valley.

itinerary.title: Trek Tankchhe to Halji (3720m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours to Halji, home to incredible Tibetan Buddhist cultural heritage and ancient monasteries.

itinerary.title: Trek Halji to Manepeme (3992m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours further through the stunning, stark landscapes of upper Humla.

itinerary.title: Trek Manepeme to Hilsa (3600m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours to Hilsa, an important border town situated directly on the Tibetan frontier.

itinerary.title: Trek Hilsa to Shivshiv (4340m)
itinerary.details: Ascend again for 6 hours, experiencing a profound blend of Hindu, Buddhist, and Shamanic cultures.

itinerary.title: Trek Shivshiv to Muchu (3130m)
itinerary.details: A 7-hour trek descending sharply through rugged mountain environments.

itinerary.title: Trek Muchu to Kermi (2790m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours through pine-forested Karnali gorges with views of the Saipal range.

itinerary.title: Trek Kermi to Dharapori (2610m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours, inching closer to the completion of our immense journey.

itinerary.title: Trek Dharapori to Simikot (2950m)
itinerary.details: The final 5 hours of trekking! Return to Simikot and enjoy the comfort of a tea house.

itinerary.title: Fly Simikot to Nepalgunj & Fly to Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Take morning flights from Simikot to Nepalgunj, and then onward to Kathmandu. Transfer to your hotel to rest.

itinerary.title: Free day in Kathmandu
itinerary.details: A well-deserved free day in the capital to recover, shop for souvenirs, or explore the city.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: The monumental 30-day expedition concludes. We will transfer you to the airport for your flight home.

treks.additionalInfo: This section of the Great Himalaya Trail is an extreme, exploratory journey through Nepal's Wild West. Due to the complete lack of tourist infrastructure, this expedition relies entirely on full-service camping (tents, cooks, and porters). This is a Grade 3 Hard/Challenging trek requiring excellent physical endurance to manage 30 days of consecutive hiking and altitudes reaching up to 4,820m.

faqs.question: Why is this trek mostly camping (tented)?
faqs.answer: The Mugu to Humla region is incredibly remote and sees very few tourists. Because tea house infrastructure is practically non-existent in these high-altitude sections, full camping logistics (tents, chefs, porters) are required to complete the journey safely.

faqs.question: How hard is the Great Himalaya Trail?
faqs.answer: Section 6 of the GHT is graded as Hard/Challenging. You will be trekking 6-8 hours daily over 30 days, traversing difficult, rugged terrain, and sleeping at high altitudes in a tent. Excellent physical endurance is completely mandatory.

faqs.question: Are special permits required?
faqs.answer: Yes. Humla and Mugu contain highly restricted areas near the Tibetan border that require special trekking permits, which are all handled and included by our team.

treks.title: Great Himalaya Trail-Dolpo to Mugu Region 34 Days
treks.description: The Great Himalaya Trail – Section 5 (Dolpo to Mugu Region) is an immensely challenging and rewarding 34-day trek through Nepal's most tranquil, remote, and culturally preserved terrain. Starting from the medieval town of Kagbeni in Mustang, the journey traverses high mountain passes like Sangda-La and Nangda-La (5,360m), leading deep into the 'Hidden Himalayas.' You will encounter the striking, barren landscapes of the Dolpo rain shadow, explore the mesmerizing crystal-clear turquoise waters of Phoksundo Lake (in Shey Phoksundo National Park), and visit the mythic 800-year-old Shey Gompa near Crystal Mountain. Along this extraordinary wilderness route, you'll experience the ancient Bon-Buddhist culture of the Dolpo-pa people and trek through high-altitude villages like Dho Tarap that remain entirely isolated in winter. Expect rugged, untamed beauty, pure wilderness camping, and an unparalleled adventure spanning 460km.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Immerse yourself in the unique Bon-Buddhist culture of the Dolpo-pa people, exploring ancient villages isolated by the harsh winter.
Witness the breathtaking, crystal-clear turquoise waters of Phoksundo Lake, the crown jewel of Shey Phoksundo National Park.
Visit the 800-year-old Shey Gompa and explore the mythology surrounding the sacred Crystal Mountain.
Conquer extreme high-altitude mountain passes, including the formidable Sangda-La (5,195m) and Nangda-La (5,360m).
Experience pure, untamed wilderness camping in some of the most remote, unexplored regions of far-western Nepal.
Trek through the striking, barren landscapes of Dolpo's rain shadow and keep an eye out for the elusive snow leopard.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu & Transfer to Hotel (1400m)
itinerary.details: Our airport representative will pick you up from the airport and transfer you to a 4-star hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Permit Procedure & Fly to Pokhara (822m)
itinerary.details: Morning is spent preparing the necessary restricted area permits. In the afternoon, take a short flight to the lakeside city of Pokhara.

itinerary.title: Fly to Jomsom (2720m) & Trek to Kagbeni (2800m)
itinerary.details: Take a stunning 25-minute mountain flight to Jomsom, then trek for 3-4 hours to the medieval, apple-orchard town of Kagbeni.

itinerary.title: Trek Kagbeni to Dangarjong (3290m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours away from the main Annapurna Circuit into the remote, restricted region. Overnight at a tented camp.

itinerary.title: Trek Dangarjong to Sangda Village (3700m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours deeper into the wilderness, ascending steadily towards the high passes.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day in Sangda Village
itinerary.details: Rest day to help your body adapt to the altitude before tackling the demanding passes ahead.

itinerary.title: Trek Sangda Village to Sangda Phedi (4190m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours to the base of the formidable Sangda-La pass.

itinerary.title: Trek to Molum Sumna (4860m) via Sangda-La Pass (5195m)
itinerary.details: An exhausting 8-hour day crossing the brutal Sangda-La pass. Enjoy spectacular views before descending into Dolpo.

itinerary.title: Trek Molum Sumna to Naljyang Sumna (4600m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours through the starkly beautiful, arid landscapes of Dolpo's rain shadow.

itinerary.title: Trek Naljyang Sumna to Chharka Bhot (4110m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours to the ancient, fortified village of Chharka Bhot, seemingly frozen in time.

itinerary.title: Rest day in Chharka Bhot
itinerary.details: A well-deserved rest day to explore the village, observe traditional practices, and recover your strength.

itinerary.title: Trek to Rapka (4535m) via Chharka Bhanjyang (5027m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6-7 hours, conquering another 5,000m+ pass to reach Rapka.

itinerary.title: Trek Rapka to Tinje Gaon (4150m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7-8 hours traversing the remote highlands to the secluded village of Tinje Gaon.

itinerary.title: Trek Tinje Gaon to Shimen Gaon (3870m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours passing through small settlements deeply rooted in Bon-Buddhist traditions.

itinerary.title: Trek Shimen Gaon to Nisal Gaon (3750m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours, encountering traditional wooden dolls (dokpas) believed to ward off evil spirits.

itinerary.title: Trek Nisal Gaon to Saldang (3770m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours to reach Saldang, a major village in the region with profound Tibetan influences.

itinerary.title: Trek Saldang to Namgung (4430m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours ascending out of the Saldang valley towards Namgung.

itinerary.title: Trek Namgung to Shey Gompa (4160m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours to arrive at the mythic 800-year-old Shey Gompa, located near the sacred Crystal Mountain.

itinerary.title: Trek Shey Gompa to Nangda-La Phedi (4600m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours to position yourself for another major pass crossing.

itinerary.title: Trek to Phoksundo Khola (4316m) via Nangda-La Pass (5360m)
itinerary.details: Cross the highest pass of the trek (5,360m) during this grueling 5-6 hour day, descending toward the Phoksundo River.

itinerary.title: Trek Phoksundo Khola to Phoksundo Lake (3733m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours to reach the crown jewel of the region: the crystal-clear, mesmerizing Phoksundo Lake.

itinerary.title: Exploring Phoksundo Lake
itinerary.details: Spend the day exploring the surreal turquoise waters, surrounding hills, and nearby ancient monasteries.

itinerary.title: Trek Phoksundo Lake to Pungmo (3600m)
itinerary.details: Leave the lake behind and trek for 5 hours toward Pungmo.

itinerary.title: Trek Pungmo to Lasa (4060m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours, gaining altitude once again in preparation for the final major pass.

itinerary.title: Trek to Kagmara Phedi (4000m) via Kagmara La Pass (5115m)
itinerary.details: Cross the Kagmara La Pass (5,115m) over a 7-hour trek, rewarding yourself with panoramic views.

itinerary.title: Trek Kagmara Phedi to Hurikot (3010m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours, descending sharply into greener, more hospitable terrain.

itinerary.title: Trek Hurikot to Nauli Ghot (3670m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours through lush landscapes toward Nauli Ghot.

itinerary.title: Trek Nauli Ghot to Kudi Gaon (2810m)
itinerary.details: Descend further over 7 hours, leaving the extreme altitudes behind.

itinerary.title: Trek Kudi Gaon to Dochal (2630m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours through picturesque villages.

itinerary.title: Trek Dochal to Jumla (2370m)
itinerary.details: The final 5 hours of trekking! Arrive in Jumla to conclude this monumental overland journey.

itinerary.title: Fly Jumla to Nepalgunj (50m)
itinerary.details: Take a morning flight from Jumla down to the hot plains of Nepalgunj.

itinerary.title: Fly Nepalgunj to Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Fly back to Kathmandu and transfer to your hotel to finally rest in comfort.

itinerary.title: Free day in Kathmandu
itinerary.details: A much-needed free day in the capital to recover, shop, or reflect on your epic journey.

itinerary.title: Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: The 34-day expedition concludes. We will transfer you to the airport for your flight home.

faqs.question: Why is this trek a mix of camping and tea houses?
faqs.answer: The Dolpo to Mugu region traverses extremely isolated terrain lacking modern tourist infrastructure. Tented camping is necessary for the vast majority of the route, with a few basic tea houses available in larger settlements.

faqs.question: How strenuous is this trek?
faqs.answer: This section of the GHT is graded as Strenuous (Grade 4). You will cross multiple passes over 5,000m, sleep at high altitudes in tents, and trek for 34 consecutive days. It requires superb physical endurance and previous high-altitude experience.

faqs.question: Are special permits needed?
faqs.answer: Yes. Upper Dolpo and Mugu are highly restricted regions requiring special permits to preserve their delicate cultures and environments. Our team arranges all necessary documentation for your journey.

treks.title: Great Himalaya Trail-Annapurna to Mustang Region 33Days
treks.image: /images/Great Himalaya Trail-Kanchenjunga to Makalu Region- 53 Days.jpg
treks.description: The Great Himalaya Trail – Section 4 (Annapurna to Mustang Region) is a remarkable 33-day journey that seamlessly connects the lush, verdant valleys of the Annapurna region with the arid, high-altitude deserts of Upper Mustang. Starting from Jagat in the Marsyangdi Valley, this trail ventures deep into the remote Nar-Phu Valley, crosses the formidable, snowy Teri-La Pass (5,595m), and descends into the restricted Kingdom of Lo (Upper Mustang). The geographical shift is stunning—from dense rhododendron forests and green Gurung villages to the barren, wind-swept Tibetan plateau. Trekkers will explore ancient walled cities like Lo Manthang, discover mystical cliff-carved sky caves, and visit centuries-old Tibetan Buddhist monasteries. This breathtaking and highly challenging trek concludes by trekking down the mighty Kali Gandaki valley, ending at Jomsom before flying out to Pokhara.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Experience a profound geographical shift, trekking from the lush, green forests of Annapurna into the dry, arid deserts of Upper Mustang.
Explore the ancient walled city of Lo Manthang, the historic capital of the secluded Kingdom of Lo.
Conquer the formidable, snow-covered Teri-La Pass (5,595m) that bridges the Nar-Phu valley with Upper Mustang.
Discover the mystical 'Sky Caves' carved high into the sheer cliff walls of the Mustang region.
Immerse yourself in deeply preserved Tibetan Plateau culture, exploring 400 to 1000-year-old Buddhist monasteries.
Enjoy world-class, panoramic views of Himalayan giants like Annapurna I, Dhaulagiri, and Machhapuchhre (Fishtail).

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu & Transfer to Hotel (1400m)

itinerary.title: Trek Dharapani to Koto (2600m)

itinerary.title: Trek Koto to Meta (3560m)

itinerary.title: Trek Meta to Kyang (3820m)

itinerary.title: Trek Kyang to Phu Gaon (4000m)

itinerary.title: Trek Phu Gaon to Nar Gaon (4110m)

itinerary.title: Exploring Nar Gaon

itinerary.title: Trek Nar Gaon to Yak Kharka (4600m)

itinerary.title: Trek Yak Kharka to Labse Khola (4800m)

itinerary.title: Trek Labse Khola to Teri-La Phedi (5000m)

itinerary.title: Hike to Luri Gompa (4000m)

itinerary.title: Trek Luri Gompa to Lo-Manthang (3840m)

itinerary.title: Exploring Lo-Manthang

itinerary.title: Exploring Chhoser Village and Caves

itinerary.title: Trek Lo-Manthang to Tsarang (3560m)

itinerary.title: Trek Tsarang to Ghiling (3570m)

itinerary.title: Trek Ghiling to Samar (3660m)

itinerary.title: Trek Samar to Chhuksang (2990m)

itinerary.title: Trek Chhuksang to Muktinath (3800m)

itinerary.title: Trek Muktinath to Jomsom (2720m)

treks.additionalInfo: This incredible section of the Great Himalaya Trail seamlessly links the lush Annapurna region with the high-altitude desert of Upper Mustang. Because the route traverses the extremely remote, high-altitude Teri-La Pass (5,595m) to bridge these regions, you will experience several days of pure wilderness camping before returning to tea houses. This is a Grade 3 Hard/Challenging trek requiring excellent physical endurance.

faqs.question: Why do we need a mix of camping and tea houses?
faqs.answer: While tea houses are widely available in the lower Annapurna and main Mustang routes, the remote crossing from the Nar-Phu valley to Mustang via the Teri-La Pass is complete wilderness and requires full-service tented camping for several days.

faqs.question: Is Upper Mustang like Tibet?
faqs.answer: Yes, Upper Mustang is often called 'Little Tibet.' It shares a border with Tibet, and its deeply preserved Buddhist culture, arid landscape, and ancient architecture closely mirror the Tibetan Plateau.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Teri-La Pass?
faqs.answer: The Teri-La Pass (5,595m) is extremely challenging and often heavily snow-bound. It requires significant physical endurance, mental toughness, and proper acclimatization to cross safely.

treks.title: Great Himalaya Trail-Langtang to Manaslu Region-50 Days
treks.image: /images/Great Himalaya Trail-Kanchenjunga to Makalu Region- 53 Days.jpg
treks.description: The Great Himalaya Trail – Section 3 (Langtang to Manaslu Region) is an epic 50-day expedition that combines the remote wilderness of Langtang and Ganesh Himal with the rich Tibetan Buddhist culture of the Tsum Valley and Manaslu. This colossal 600km journey starts just outside Kathmandu, taking you past the sacred five lakes of Panch Pokhari before navigating the incredibly challenging, snow-bound Tilman's Pass (5,320m). Trekkers will explore the pristine 'Hidden Treasures' of Langtang National Park, crossing from lush rhododendron forests to sweeping alpine meadows, with up-close views of Dorje Lakpa and Langtang Lirung. The journey then transitions into the sacred Tsum Valley, a hidden 'Beyul' featuring ancient monasteries like Mu Gompa and Milarepa's Cave. The expedition culminates with the formidable Larkya-La Pass (5,160m) in the Manaslu region, offering unparalleled, close-up views of Mt. Manaslu (the world's eighth-highest peak) and a profound immersion into unspoiled Himalayan life.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Conquer the legendary Great Himalaya Trail, embarking on a massive 50-day, 600km trek traversing Langtang, Ganesh Himal, and Manaslu.
Navigate the extreme, snow-bound Tilman's Pass (5,320m) and the spectacular Larkya-La Pass (5,160m).
Discover the hidden 'Beyul' of Tsum Valley, exploring ancient spiritual sites like Mu Gompa and Milarepa's Cave.
Experience pure, untamed wilderness camping in the remote Jugal Himal, home to the elusive red panda and blue sheep.
Witness breathtaking, up-close views of Mt. Manaslu (8,163m), Ganesh Himal, and the Langtang Lirung.
Immerse yourself in authentic Tamang, Gurung, and Tibetan Buddhist cultures in highly isolated mountain communities.

itinerary.title: Trek to Moraine Camp (4500m) via Tilman’s Pass (5320m)
itinerary.details: An exhausting 9-hour day crossing the snowy, technical Tilman’s Pass. This is a true alpine adventure.

itinerary.title: Trek Moraine Camp to Langshisa Kharka (4080m)

itinerary.title: Trek Langshisa Kharka to Kyanjin Gompa (3730m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours to Kyanjin Gompa, finally reaching tea house accommodations.

itinerary.title: Trek Sherpa Gaon to Briddim (2230m)

itinerary.title: Trek Briddim to Timure (1762m)

itinerary.title: Trek Timure to Nagthaligyang (3165m)

itinerary.title: Trek Tatopani to Gatlang Village (2238m)

itinerary.title: Trek Somdang to Pangsang Kharka (3600m)

itinerary.title: Trek Sertung to Lapagaon (1810m)

treks.additionalInfo: The Langtang to Manaslu section of the Great Himalaya Trail is an extreme, monumental 50-day expedition. Covering 600km, the route demands incredible mental stamina and physical endurance to navigate massive elevation changes, technical snowy passes (Tilman's and Larkya-La), and long stretches of isolated wilderness camping. This is a Grade 3 Hard/Challenging trek designed for highly experienced adventurers.

faqs.question: How difficult is a 50-day trek?
faqs.answer: This 50-day expedition is graded as Hard/Challenging. Trekking for nearly two months requires tremendous mental stamina and superb physical endurance. You will cross multiple 5,000m+ passes and cover 600km of rugged terrain.

faqs.question: Do we sleep in tents or tea houses?
faqs.answer: This massive section uses a combination of both. In the highly remote Jugal Himal and Tilman's Pass areas, we rely entirely on full-service tented camping. In Langtang, Tsum Valley, and Manaslu, we use available tea houses.

faqs.question: Are permits difficult to get?
faqs.answer: The trek requires multiple restricted area permits for Manaslu and Tsum Valley, as well as National Park fees for Langtang. Our team will handle all the complex permit logistics for you in Kathmandu.

treks.title: Great Himalaya Trail-Everest to Rolwaling Region-40 Days
treks.image: /images/Great Himalaya Trail-Kanchenjunga to Makalu Region- 53 Days.jpg
treks.description: The Great Himalaya Trail – Section 2 (Everest to Rolwaling Region) is a profound 40-day expedition that connects the legendary Khumbu (Everest) region with the remote, 'hidden valley' of Rolwaling. This highly demanding alpine journey requires crossing three formidable, technical mountain passes: Zatrwa La (4,610m), Amphu Labtsa (5,845m), and the treacherous Tashi Labsta Pass (5,755m). Trekkers will summit Mera Peak (6,470m), explore the iconic Everest Base Camp (5,364m), cross the stunning Cho-La and Renjo-La passes, and witness the mesmerizing turquoise Gokyo Lakes. Beyond Everest, the trail descends into the secluded Rolwaling valley past Tsho Rolpa, Nepal’s largest glacial lake. This trek is an unparalleled blend of world-class mountaineering, pure wilderness camping, and deep immersion into the Sherpa culture and Buddhist heritage of some of the most spectacular, untouched mountains on earth.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Conquer an epic 40-day, 500km traverse combining the famous Everest Region with the remote, untouched Rolwaling valley.
Summit Mera Peak (6,470m) and navigate extreme, technical high passes including Amphu Labtsa (5,845m) and Tashi Labsta (5,755m).
Explore the iconic Everest Base Camp (5,364m) and witness legendary sunrise views from Kala Patthar (5,550m).
Traverse the massive Ngozumpa Glacier to the stunning, turquoise Gokyo Lakes, crossing the Cho-La (5,420m) and Renjo-La (5,360m) passes.
Camp beside Tsho Rolpa, Nepal's largest glacial lake, surrounded by the towering peaks of the Rolwaling Himal.
Immerse yourself deeply in the rich Sherpa cultural heritage and ancient Buddhist lifestyles of high-altitude villages like Beding and Na.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Our airport representative will pick you up from the airport and transfer you to a 4-star hotel in Kathmandu.

itinerary.title: Free day in Kathmandu
itinerary.details: A free day to prepare, arrange gear, and obtain necessary climbing permits for the epic expedition.

itinerary.title: Fly to Lukla (2800m)
itinerary.details: Take a thrilling mountain flight to Lukla, the gateway to the Everest region. Stay overnight at a lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek Lukla to Chutanga (3000m)
itinerary.details: Begin trekking east away from the main Everest trail, heading toward the Hinku valley. Walk 6 hours.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization at Chutanga
itinerary.details: An essential rest day to acclimatize before crossing the first major pass.

itinerary.title: Trek to Thulikharka (4200m) via Zatrwa La Pass (4610m)
itinerary.details: Cross the Zatrwa La Pass over a challenging 8-hour trek, descending into the lush Hinku valley.

itinerary.title: Trek Thulikharka to Kothe (3550m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours descending through dense rhododendron and pine forests.

itinerary.title: Trek Kothe to Thangnak (4350m)

itinerary.title: Trek Thangnak to Khare (5000m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours to Khare, the base for Mera Peak climbing.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization day at Khare
itinerary.details: Rest, practice climbing techniques, and prepare gear for the upcoming summit push.

itinerary.title: Trek Khare to Mera Base Camp (5350m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours ascending the glacier to establish base camp. Transition to tented camping.

itinerary.title: Trek Base Camp to Mera High Camp (5800m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours to High Camp. The air is extremely thin, and views of Everest, Makalu, and Cho Oyu are astounding.

itinerary.title: Summit Mera Peak (6470m) & Return to Kongma Dingma (5200m)
itinerary.details: Start very early for a grueling 9-hour summit push. Stand atop Mera Peak (6,470m) before descending to Kongma Dingma.

itinerary.title: Trek Kongma Dingma to Seti Pokhari (4900m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours deeper into the remote wilderness.

itinerary.title: Extra day for rest and acclimatization
itinerary.details: A much-needed rest day after the summit push.

itinerary.title: Trek Seti Pokhari to Amphu Labtsa Base Camp (5527m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours to the base of the treacherous Amphu Labtsa pass.

itinerary.title: Cross Amphu Labtsa Pass (5845m) to Chhukung (4730m)
itinerary.details: An epic, highly technical 8-hour day crossing Amphu Labtsa using ropes and crampons. Descend into the main Khumbu valley.

itinerary.title: Hike to Chhukung Ri (5550m)
itinerary.details: A 7-hour round-trip hike to the summit of Chhukung Ri for phenomenal views of Lhotse and Ama Dablam.

itinerary.title: Trek Chhukung to Lobuche (4910m) via Kongma La Pass (5535m)
itinerary.details: Cross the first of the 'Three Passes' over a 9-hour trek, descending to the bustling Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Trek Lobuche to Gorak Shep (5140m)
itinerary.details: A short 4-hour trek to the highest tea house settlement in the world.

itinerary.title: Explore Everest Base Camp (5364m)
itinerary.details: A 3-hour round trip to the legendary Everest Base Camp, surrounded by the Khumbu Icefall.

itinerary.title: Hike Kala Patthar (5550m) & Trek to Dzongla (4830m)
itinerary.details: Hike Kala Patthar early for an iconic Everest sunrise, then trek 7 hours down to Dzongla.

itinerary.title: Trek Dzongla to Thangnak (4700m) via Cho-La Pass (5420m)
itinerary.details: Cross the icy Cho-La pass over a 6-hour trek.

itinerary.title: Trek Thangnak to Gokyo (4790m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours across the Ngozumpa Glacier to the stunning turquoise waters of Gokyo.

itinerary.title: Hike to Gokyo Ri (5360m)
itinerary.details: A 6-hour round-trip hike for arguably the best panoramic viewpoint in the entire Everest region.

itinerary.title: Trek Gokyo to Lumde (4368m) via Renjo-La Pass (5360m)
itinerary.details: Cross the final Khumbu pass over 5 hours, descending toward the Tibetan trade route.

itinerary.title: Trek Lumde to Thame (3820m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours to the historic, culturally rich Sherpa village of Thame.

itinerary.title: Trek Thame to Thyangbo (4230m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours, moving away from Everest and toward the Rolwaling valley.

itinerary.title: Trek Thyangbo to Ngole (5130m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours, returning to true wilderness and tented camping.

itinerary.title: Trek Ngole to Tashi Labtsa Camp (5665m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours to the high camp of the fearsome Tashi Labtsa pass.

itinerary.title: Trek to Glacier Camp (4735m) via Tashi Labtsa Pass (5755m)
itinerary.details: A dangerous and exhausting 7-hour crossing of Tashi Labtsa (5,755m), dropping into the Rolwaling valley.

itinerary.title: Trek Glacier Camp to Tsho Rolpa Lake (4540m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours to the shores of Nepal's largest glacial lake, Tsho Rolpa.

itinerary.title: Trek Tsho Rolpa Lake to Na (4180m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours to Na, the highest summer settlement in Rolwaling. Return to tea houses.

itinerary.title: Trek Na to Beding (3470m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours to Beding, a traditional Sherpa village hidden deep in the valley.

itinerary.title: Exploration day at Beding
itinerary.details: Rest and explore the local monasteries and rich cultural heritage of this isolated community.

itinerary.title: Trek Beding to Daldung La (3976m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours traversing the valley walls.

itinerary.title: Trek Daldung La to Simigaon (2036m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours descending sharply out of the alpine environment into lush, green hills.

itinerary.title: Trek Simigaon to Gonggar & Drive to Kathmandu (1400m)

treks.additionalInfo: The Everest to Rolwaling section of the Great Himalaya Trail is arguably the most technically demanding portion of the entire GHT High Route. Graded as Grade 4 Strenuous, it involves summiting Mera Peak (6,470m) and crossing two highly technical, mountaineering-level passes (Amphu Labtsa at 5,845m and Tashi Labsta at 5,755m). Crampons, ice axes, fixed ropes, and previous mountaineering experience are absolutely required. You must also have specialized insurance covering high-altitude peak climbing.

faqs.question: How difficult are the mountain passes?
faqs.answer: Extremely difficult. Passes like Amphu Labtsa (5,845m) and Tashi Labsta (5,755m) are highly technical, requiring mountaineering equipment like crampons, ice axes, and fixed ropes. You must have prior mountaineering experience.

faqs.question: Do I need special insurance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because this trek includes peak climbing (Mera Peak) and technical passes above 5,500m, your travel insurance must explicitly cover high-altitude mountaineering and emergency helicopter evacuation.

faqs.question: Are tea houses available the whole time?
faqs.answer: No. While the Everest region is well-supplied with tea houses, the crossings over Amphu Labtsa and Tashi Labsta into the Rolwaling Valley require full-service wilderness tented camping for several days.

treks.title: Great Himalaya Trail-Kanchenjunga to Makalu Region- 53 Days
treks.description: The Great Himalaya Trail – Section 1 (Kanchenjunga to Makalu Region) is a staggering 53-day, 1,050km expedition through the extreme eastern edge of Nepal. Serving as the monumental start of the Great Himalaya Trail, this route takes adventurers through the pristine, off-the-beaten-path wilderness of the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area and Makalu Barun National Park. You will explore ecological zones ranging from subtropical valleys along the sparkling Tamur River to isolated glacial wilderness. Highlights include breathtaking, close-up views of Mt. Kanchenjunga (the world’s 3rd highest peak) and Mt. Makalu (the 5th highest), as well as a crossing of the formidable Lumba Sumba Pass (5,177m). Along the way, immerse yourself in the rich, traditional cultures of the Sherpa, Rai, Limbu, and Tibeto-Mongoloid communities that inhabit these remote, shrouded valleys. Expect a true, rugged wilderness experience with abundant wildlife, including the possibility of spotting red pandas, blue sheep, and snow leopards.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Embark on an epic 53-day, 1,050km trek marking the first section of the legendary Great Himalaya Trail.
Witness breathtaking, close-up views of Mt. Kanchenjunga (3rd highest) and Mt. Makalu (5th highest).
Traverse the formidable Lumba Sumba Pass (5,177m), a highly challenging and remote high-altitude crossing.
Explore the untouched Barun Valley and Kanchenjunga Conservation Area, rich in diverse flora and rare fauna.
Immerse yourself deeply in the traditional lifestyles of the Rai, Limbu, and high-altitude Sherpa communities.
Experience true wilderness, transitioning from subtropical valleys to remote, glaciated alpine environments.

faqs.question: How difficult is a 53-day, 1,050km trek?
faqs.answer: This expedition is graded as Hard/Challenging. Covering 1,050km over 53 days requires supreme mental stamina, immense physical endurance, and the ability to thrive in extremely remote, high-altitude conditions.

faqs.question: Are there tea houses on this route?
faqs.answer: Yes, but only in certain sections. The trek utilizes tea houses where available, but significant portions—especially around the Lumba Sumba Pass—require full-service wilderness tented camping.

faqs.question: Is it possible to see snow leopards?
faqs.answer: While sightings are incredibly rare, the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area and Makalu Barun National Park are home to snow leopards, red pandas, and blue sheep, making this a prime route for wildlife tracking.

treks.title: Lumba Sumba Pass Trek 21 Days
treks.description: The Lumba Sumba Pass Trek is one of Nepal’s best-kept secrets, an off-the-beaten-path 21-day expedition that explores the remote Kanchenjunga and Makalu regions. Following a section of the legendary Great Himalayan Trail (GHT), this fully supported wilderness camping trek connects the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area with the Makalu Barun National Park. Trekkers will transition from sub-tropical forests to pristine alpine zones, culminating in the thrilling crossing of the Lumba Sumba Pass (5,177m). Expect zero tourist infrastructure and unparalleled solitude as you navigate rugged trails, isolated Tibetan-influenced villages like Olangchung Gola, and deep river gorges. The journey rewards adventurers with magnificent, unobstructed views of Mt. Kanchenjunga (8,586m) and Mt. Makalu (8,481m), alongside incredible biodiversity including red pandas and snow leopards.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Discover one of Nepal's best-kept secrets on a 21-day wilderness camping trek connecting the Kanchenjunga and Makalu regions.
Conquer the challenging Lumba Sumba Pass (5,177m), traversing the remote Great Himalayan Trail.
Enjoy spectacular, unobstructed panoramas of the world's 3rd highest (Kanchenjunga) and 5th highest (Makalu) peaks.
Explore highly isolated traditional villages, including the ancient Tibetan settlement of Olangchung Gola.
Trek through the untouched wilderness of the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area, a sanctuary for snow leopards and red pandas.
Experience true solitude on a rugged, off-the-beaten-path route with zero modern tourist infrastructure.

faqs.question: Can a beginner do the Lumba Sumba Pass Trek?
faqs.answer: No. This trek is extremely demanding, remote, and involves crossing a 5,177m pass with no tourist infrastructure. It is only recommended for fit, experienced trekkers.

faqs.question: What is the accommodation like?
faqs.answer: The Lumba Sumba Pass is primarily a camping trek. Our team will provide sturdy alpine sleeping tents, along with a dining tent, toilet tent, and an expert kitchen crew who will prepare all your meals.

faqs.question: Are there alternative routes to extend the trek?
faqs.answer: Yes! Because this trail touches both regions, you can easily extend the trek to the Kanchenjunga Base Camp (an additional 6 days) or the Makalu Base Camp (an additional 12 days).

treks.title: Kanchenjunga South Base Camp Trek 14 Days
treks.description: Kanchenjunga South Base Camp Trek is an extreme wilderness and off-the-beaten-path trek in Nepal that immerses you in the teeming flora and fauna of the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area. While the full Kanchenjunga circuit usually takes over three weeks, this specially designed 14-day itinerary leads you directly to the south base camp of Mount Kanchenjunga at 4,730 meters. Untouched and unbothered by crowds, this route is perfect for travelers with limited time who still want to experience the daring adventure of the eastern Himalayas. The trail offers otherworldly landscapes, isolated mountain lakes, cascading waterfalls, and picturesque villages inhabited by Rais, Limbus, and Sherpas. You will be rewarded with breathtaking views of the world’s third-highest peak, Kanchenjunga (8,586m), along with Mt. Jannu, Makalu, and Kabru. Expect a demanding yet spiritually rejuvenating journey through silent forests and ancient gompas.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Reach the South Base Camp of Mt. Kanchenjunga (4,730m) on a specially designed, fast-paced 14-day itinerary.
Witness breathtaking, unobstructed views of the world's 3rd highest peak, Kanchenjunga (8,586m), alongside Mt. Jannu and Makalu.
Explore the untouched wilderness of the Kanchenjunga Conservation Area, home to exotic snow leopards and red pandas.
Hike to the magnificent Yalung Glacier (4,580m) for up-close encounters with dramatic alpine terrain.
Immerse yourself in the magical Buddhist and Hindu cultures of the Rai, Limbu, and high-altitude Sherpa communities.
Enjoy unparalleled solitude and tranquility on an off-the-beaten-path route far away from crowded tourist trails.

treks.additionalInfo: The Kanchenjunga South Base Camp trek is an off-the-beaten-path journey that demands strong fitness and previous trekking experience. Although the altitude gain is gradual, the trails are highly isolated with scarce facilities. You must be prepared for a digital detox and a true wilderness experience.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Kanchenjunga south base camp trek?
faqs.answer: It is one of the most challenging treks in Nepal. The route is off-the-beaten-path, isolated, and has scarce facilities. You need to be physically fit and have strong mental endurance.

faqs.question: Do I need a special permit for this trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Kanchenjunga region is a restricted area. You need a Kanchenjunga Conservation Area Project (KCAP) permit and a restricted area entry permit. We arrange all of this for you.

faqs.question: Can a beginner do the Kanchenjunga south base camp trek?
faqs.answer: No, this trek is not ideal for beginner trekkers. It demands previous high-altitude trekking experience and strong physical fitness to withstand the rugged terrain.

faqs.question: Are there tea shops on the route?
faqs.answer: Yes, there are limited tea houses, but prices for snacks and bottled water are very high due to the extreme remoteness. It is best to bring your own favorite snacks and water purification tablets.

treks.title: Annapurna Circuit via Kang La and Nar 17 Days
treks.image: /images/Annapurna Circuit via Kang La and Nar 17 Days.jpg
treks.description: The Annapurna Circuit via Kang La and Nar Phu Valley is a spectacular 17-day journey that blends the classic Annapurna Circuit with an exploration of one of Nepal's most isolated, restricted areas. This adventurous trek diverges from the main trail to venture deep into the Nar Phu Valley, an ancient Tibetan-influenced region characterized by stone houses, centuries-old monasteries, and a stark, high-altitude desert environment. The trek features two massive crossings: the dramatic Kang La Pass (5,320m) offering panoramic views of Annapurna II and Tilicho Peak, followed by the iconic Thorong La Pass (5,416m). Descending into the arid Kali Gandaki Gorge (the world's deepest gorge), you will visit the sacred Hindu and Buddhist pilgrimage site of Muktinath before concluding the trek in Jomsom. This Grade 3 trek offers a challenging yet deeply rewarding mix of raw wilderness, challenging passes, and profound cultural immersion.
highlights: Explore the hidden, restricted Nar Phu Valley, offering an authentic glimpse into ancient Tibetan culture and traditions.
Conquer two massive high-altitude passes: the dramatic Kang La Pass (5,320m) and the iconic Thorong La Pass (5,416m).
Witness breathtaking panoramas of the Annapurna, Dhaulagiri, and Manaslu mountain ranges.
Visit the sacred Muktinath Temple, a revered pilgrimage site for both Hindus and Buddhists featuring 108 eternal water spouts.
Trek through the world's deepest gorge, the Kali Gandaki, and search for ancient fossilized ammonites (Shaligrams).
Experience extreme diverse landscapes, transitioning from lush subtropical forests to high-altitude Tibetan plateaus.

itinerary.title: Arrival to Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Welcome to Kathmandu. We will pick you up from the airport and assist with your hotel check-in. Enjoy a welcome dinner.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Valley Sightseeing & Trek Preparation
itinerary.details: Guided tours of UNESCO World Heritage Sites (Swayambhunath, Kathmandu Durbar Square, Boudhanath, Pashupatinath) while we finalize your restricted area permits.

itinerary.title: Drive by Jeep to Dharapani (1860m)
itinerary.details: A scenic 9-hour jeep drive covering 225km through the hills from Kathmandu to Dharapani.

itinerary.title: Trek Dharapani to Koto (2600m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours through pine and oak forests, enjoying views of Annapurna II and Manaslu before arriving at Koto.

itinerary.title: Trek Koto to Meta (3560m)
itinerary.details: Leave the main Annapurna trail and trek 6 hours into the restricted Nar Phu valley, reaching the Tibetan Buddhist community of Meta.

itinerary.title: Trek Meta to Phu Village (4080m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours past ruins and forts into the ancient, restricted Phu Village, famous for its unique blue sheep and Tibetan culture.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day in Phu Village
itinerary.details: Rest and acclimatize. Explore the Tashi Lhakhang Monastery and the traditional stone architecture of the village.

itinerary.title: Trek Phu Village to Nar Phedi (3490m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours reversing the route slightly to reach Nar Phedi, home to an ancient monastery.

itinerary.title: Trek Nar Phedi to Nar Village (4150m)
itinerary.details: A short 3-hour trek to Nar Village. Prepare for the upcoming Kang La pass crossing.

itinerary.title: Trek Nar Village to Ngawal (3660m) via Kang La Pass (5320m)
itinerary.details: A massive 9-hour day. Ascend and cross the spectacular Kang La Pass with views of Gangapurna and Tilicho, then descend to Ngawal.

itinerary.title: Trek Ngawal to Manang (3540m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours rejoining the main Annapurna Circuit trail, passing Braga Monastery before reaching the bustling town of Manang.

itinerary.title: Trek Manang to Yak Kharka (4050m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4 hours ascending steadily into the alpine environment of Yak Kharka.

itinerary.title: Trek Yak Kharka to Thorong High Camp (4925m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours up to the base of the mighty Thorong La, preparing for tomorrow's massive crossing.

itinerary.title: Trek to Muktinath (3760m) via Thorong La (5416m), Drive to Jomsom (2720m)
itinerary.details: Cross the iconic Thorong La Pass (5,416m). Descend steeply to the holy site of Muktinath, then take a jeep to Jomsom. 9 hours total.

itinerary.title: Flight Jomsom to Pokhara (822m)
itinerary.details: Take a scenic 30-minute early morning flight through the Kali Gandaki gorge to the lakeside city of Pokhara. Relax by Phewa Lake.

itinerary.title: Drive Pokhara to Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: A 7-hour tourist bus ride back to Kathmandu. Celebrate the completion of the trek with a farewell dinner.

itinerary.title: Final Departure
itinerary.details: Your incredible 17-day adventure concludes. Transfer to the airport 3 hours before your flight.

treks.additionalInfo: The Annapurna Circuit via Kang La and Nar Phu Valley is an incredibly challenging Grade 3 trek. It crosses two high-altitude passes over 5,300m in quick succession. Trekkers must be physically robust, emotionally motivated, and well-acclimatized to undertake this dual-pass expedition. Travel insurance covering high-altitude evacuation is mandatory.

faqs.question: Do I need a special permit for the Nar Phu Valley?
faqs.answer: Yes. Nar Phu is a restricted area in Nepal. You are required to have a special restricted area permit issued through a registered trekking agency, and you must trek with a licensed guide.

faqs.question: How difficult is it to cross two passes?
faqs.answer: Crossing both Kang La (5,320m) and Thorong La (5,416m) on the same trek makes this a Grade 3 Hard/Challenging itinerary. It requires excellent physical fitness, stamina, and proper acclimatization.

faqs.question: Is this a camping trek?
faqs.answer: No, this route utilizes tea houses and local homestays for the duration of the trek, offering simple Nepali cuisine and basic accommodations.

treks.title: Darjeeling-Sikkim-Ilam Tour 6 Days
treks.description: Witness the beauty of northeast India and eastern Nepal with a perfectly blended multi-country tour. This 6-day journey connects the scenic tea gardens of Kanyam in Ilam (Nepal) with the magnificent hill resorts of Sikkim and Darjeeling (India). Discover the breathtaking vistas of rolling hills, manicured tea plantations, and the majestic Kanchenjunga mountain range. Explore Gangtok, the capital of Sikkim, known for its vibrant monasteries, mystic rituals, and high-altitude lakes like Tsomgo. Journey on to Darjeeling to witness the iconic sunrise over Tiger Hill, visit the UNESCO World Heritage Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (Toy Train), and explore historic zoological parks and peace pagodas. This is a luxurious, moderate-grade tour that combines nature, culture, and spectacular Himalayan panoramas across two beautiful countries.
highlights: Explore the vast, scenic tea gardens of Kanyam in Ilam, Nepal, known as the Queen of Eastern Nepal.
Witness breathtaking sunrise panoramas over the Kanchenjunga range from Darjeeling's famous Tiger Hill.
Visit Gangtok, the vibrant capital of Sikkim, nestled in the Himalayas with rich Tibetan Buddhist culture.
Take an excursion to the stunning high-altitude Tsomgo Lake (3,753m), home to migratory birds and Brahminy Ducks.
Experience the iconic Darjeeling Himalayan Railway and visit historic sites like the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute.
Enjoy a luxurious multi-country adventure with premium hotel accommodations and private tourist vehicles.

itinerary.title: Flight Kathmandu to Bhadrapur & Transfer to Kanyam (1810m)
itinerary.details: Take an early morning flight to Bhadrapur, then drive to the beautiful tea estates of Kanyam. Enjoy a sightseeing tour of the tea gardens. Overnight at a hotel in Kanyam.

itinerary.title: Transfer to Gangtok (1650m)
itinerary.details: Drive from Ilam to the Kakarvitta/Panitanki border. After border formalities, transfer to Gangtok, the mystic capital of Sikkim. Check in and overnight in Gangtok.

itinerary.title: Excursion to Tsomgo Lake (3753m)
itinerary.details: Take a 2-hour drive to the stunning oval-shaped Tsomgo Lake. Enjoy the high-altitude scenery before returning to Gangtok to explore MG Road in the evening.

itinerary.title: Gangtok Sightseeing & Transfer to Darjeeling (2042m)
itinerary.details: Visit local Gangtok sights including the Flower Show, Dro-Dul Chorten, and Bakthang Falls. Later, drive to the charming hill station of Darjeeling.

itinerary.title: Darjeeling Local Sightseeing
itinerary.details: Early morning (4 AM) visit to Tiger Hill for sunrise over Kanchenjunga. After breakfast, visit the Himalayan Mountaineering Institute, Zoo, Peace Pagoda, and Tea Gardens.

itinerary.title: Drive to Panitanki/Bhadrapur & Fly to Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Check out and drive back to the Nepal border at Panitanki, continue to Bhadrapur airport, and take a scenic flight back to Kathmandu to conclude the tour.
