treks.additionalInfo: This multi-country tour is perfect for families, couples, and those looking for a luxurious cultural getaway. Please ensure you have the necessary documentation, including a valid Indian visa if required for your nationality, before booking this trip.

faqs.question: Do I need a visa for India?
faqs.answer: If you are not a citizen of Nepal or India, you will need a valid Indian visa to cross the border at Panitanki and visit Sikkim/Darjeeling. Please arrange this prior to the trip.

faqs.question: What happens if Tsomgo Lake is closed due to bad weather?
faqs.answer: In case of bad weather conditions or landslides where Tsomgo Lake is closed, our team will provide an alternate local sightseeing excursion in Gangtok.

faqs.question: Are the meals included?
faqs.answer: Yes, the package includes Breakfast, Lunch, and Dinner provided at the respective hotels during your stay.

treks.title: Incredible Himalaya Tour to Tibet, Nepal & Bhutan 15 Days
treks.description: Take an incredible 15-day multi-country journey across the Himalayas, connecting Tibet, Nepal, and Bhutan. This spectacular overland tour begins on the 'Roof of the World' in Lhasa, exploring iconic Tibetan Buddhist sites such as the Potala Palace and Jokhang Temple. You will traverse the vast Tibetan Plateau, viewing the stunning Yamdrok Lake and Karola Glacier, before reaching the towering North Face of Mount Everest at Everest Base Camp (5,200m). From there, cross the Gyirong border into the legendary Kathmandu Valley in Nepal to explore ancient UNESCO World Heritage cities. Finally, fly into the mystical Kingdom of Bhutan to discover the secrets of 'Gross National Happiness,' visiting Paro, Thimphu, and Punakha, and hiking to the breathtaking Tiger's Nest Monastery. This is the ultimate Himalayan cultural and natural expedition.
highlights: Explore the iconic Potala Palace and Jokhang Temple in Lhasa, the spiritual heart of Tibet.
Stand beneath the towering North Face of Mount Everest at Everest Base Camp (5,200m).
Witness breathtaking alpine scenery including the turquoise Yamdrok Lake and the Karola Glacier.
Discover the ancient UNESCO World Heritage Sites of the Kathmandu Valley, including Patan and Bhaktapur.
Hike to Bhutan's legendary Tiger's Nest Monastery, perched on a cliff 900m above the Paro Valley.
Experience the unique culture and 'Gross National Happiness' philosophy in Thimphu and Punakha, Bhutan.

itinerary.title: Lhasa Arrival (3650m) | Pick-up Service
itinerary.details: Welcome to Lhasa, the capital of the Tibet Autonomous Region! Transfer to your hotel to acclimatize to the extreme altitude.

itinerary.title: Lhasa City Tour | Jokhang Temple, Sera Monastery
itinerary.details: Explore the Jokhang Temple and Barkhor Street, then witness the famous monks' debating session at Sera Monastery.

itinerary.title: Lhasa City Tour | Potala Palace, Drepung Monastery
itinerary.details: Visit the iconic Potala Palace, the highest palace in the world, followed by a tour of the Drepung Monastery.

itinerary.title: Lhasa to Shigatse (3850m) | Yamdrok Lake, Karola Glacier
itinerary.details: Drive across the Kampala Pass to view the stunning Yamdrok Lake and hike near the Karola Glacier before reaching Shigatse.

itinerary.title: Shigatse to EBC (5200m) | Rongpuk Monastery
itinerary.details: Visit Tashilunpo Monastery, then drive over Gyawu La Pass to reach Everest Base Camp and the highest monastery in the world, Rongpuk.

itinerary.title: EBC to Old Tingri (4300m) | Sunrise at Mount Everest
itinerary.details: Witness the magical sunrise over the North Face of Mt. Everest, then drive to Old Tingri and visit the Qomolangma Guandi Temple.

itinerary.title: Old Tingri to Gyirong Town (2800m)
itinerary.details: Drive towards the China-Nepal border along the scenic Friendship Highway, with views of Mt. Shishapangma (8027m).

itinerary.title: Across the Border | Gyirong Port to Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Cross the border into Nepal via Rashuwaghadi and take a long, rugged drive into the legendary Kathmandu Valley.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Valley & Bhaktapur Tour
itinerary.details: Visit Kathmandu Durbar Square, Swayambhunath (Monkey Temple), and the ancient pottery city of Bhaktapur.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu Valley & Patan Tour
itinerary.details: Explore Patan Durbar Square, the sacred Pashupatinath Temple, and the massive Boudhanath Stupa.

itinerary.title: Flight Kathmandu to Paro & Transfer to Thimphu
itinerary.details: Fly into Bhutan. Visit the Iron Chain Bridge and the massive Buddha Dordenma Statue before arriving in Thimphu.

itinerary.title: Thimphu to Punakha (1200m)
itinerary.details: Explore Thimphu's cultural sites including Trashichho Dzong, then drive across Dochula Pass to the warmer Punakha valley.

itinerary.title: Punakha to Paro (2200m)
itinerary.details: Visit the beautiful Punakha Dzong and the Chimi Lhakhang (Fertility Temple) before driving back to Paro.

itinerary.title: Paro | Hike to Tiger's Nest Monastery
itinerary.details: A highlight of the trip: a 5-hour round trip hike to the iconic Taktsang Goemba (Tiger's Nest), clinging to a sheer cliff.

itinerary.title: Paro Departure
itinerary.details: Your incredible 15-day multi-country Himalayan adventure concludes. Transfer to Paro International Airport.

treks.additionalInfo: This overland journey crosses extremely high altitudes in Tibet (up to 5,200m at EBC). You must be prepared for altitude acclimatization, basic conditions in remote areas, and long driving days across international borders.

faqs.question: Do I need special permits for this tour?
faqs.answer: Yes, you need Tibet Entry Permits, Alien Travel Permits, a Nepal Visa, and a Bhutan Visa. Our team will handle the complex permit process for Tibet and Bhutan on your behalf.

faqs.question: Will I experience altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: The tour reaches extremely high altitudes in Tibet, maxing out at EBC (5,200m). We provide oxygen in the vehicles and schedule the itinerary to help you acclimatize gradually. However, you should consult your doctor before joining.

faqs.question: Are flights between Kathmandu and Paro included?
faqs.answer: No, international airfares, including the flight from Kathmandu to Paro, are excluded from the base price and must be booked separately.

treks.title: Manaslu Circuit + Tsum Valley Trek 18 Days
treks.description: The Manaslu and Tsum Valley Trek is an 18-day teahouse trip that takes trekkers close to the world’s eighth-highest peak, Mt. Manaslu (8,163m), through the mysterious, hidden valley of Tsum. Tsum Valley, an ancient pilgrimage destination, adds to the allure with its traditional Buddhist and Tibetan culture, undisturbed by modernity. You will discover Tibetan Buddhism’s ancient traditions, rotating prayer wheels, deep-throated Tibetan horns, and a mystical paradise of Buddhist temples and nunneries. The trail journeys through terraced fields, lush pine and rhododendron forests, deep gorges of the Budhi Gandaki river, and stark alpine environments. Combining the secluded Tsum Valley with the classic Manaslu Circuit, this challenging Grade 3 trek culminates with the dramatic crossing of the high-altitude Larkya La Pass (5,160m). This route is less crowded, offering raw natural beauty and a spiritual atmosphere.
highlights: Trek around Mt. Manaslu (8,163m), the world's eighth-highest peak, on a less-crowded, pristine trail.
Explore the secret, hidden Tsum Valley, renowned for its ancient Tibetan Buddhist culture and undisturbed way of life.
Visit ancient monasteries such as Mu Gompa, Rachen Gompa, and the sacred Milarepa Piren Phu Cave (pigeon cave).
Cross the dramatic Larkya La Pass (5,160m) offering breathtaking views of Himlung Himal, Cheo Himal, and Annapurna II.
Experience a unique cultural blend of Tibetan Nupri and Gurung inhabitants along an ancient trading route to Tibet.
Follow the majestic Budhi Gandaki River through diverse landscapes from subtropical jungles to high-altitude alpine meadows.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu Airport (1400m)
itinerary.details: Our representative will greet you at the airport and transfer you to your hotel. Later, we will hold a trip briefing.

itinerary.title: Private Jeep Kathmandu to Machha Khola (890m)
itinerary.details: A scenic 9-hour drive via Arughat and Soti Khola to the start of the trek at Machha Khola.

itinerary.title: Trek Machha Khola to Jagat (1340m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6-7 hours crossing suspension bridges, passing hot springs at Tatopani, and entering the Manaslu Conservation Area at Jagat.

itinerary.title: Trek Jagat to Lokpa (2240m)

itinerary.title: Trek Lokpa to Chumling (2386m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours through deep pine and rhododendron forests, arriving at Chumling with views of Ganesh Himal.

itinerary.title: Trek Chumling to Rachen Gompa (3240m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours to Chhokang Paro, a traditional town, before arriving at the nunnery of Rachen Gompa.

itinerary.title: Trek Rachen Gompa to Nile (3361m) & Mu Gumpa (3700m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours up to Mu Gumpa, the highest point in Tsum Valley, before returning to Nile for the night.

itinerary.title: Trek Nile to Chumling (2386m)
itinerary.details: Descend 6 hours retracing your steps along the Siyar River back to Chumling.

itinerary.title: Trek Chumling to Deng (1860m)
itinerary.details: Trek 8 hours out of the Tsum Valley, rejoining the main Manaslu circuit trail and walking along the Budhi Gandaki to Deng.

itinerary.title: Trek Deng to Namrung (2630m)
itinerary.details: Ascend 8 hours into Upper Nuri, where the Tibetan influence becomes prominent. Arrive at Namrung village.

itinerary.title: Trek Namrung to Lho (3180m)
itinerary.details: Trek to Lho village, dominated by a large Gompa and offering spectacular views of Mt. Manaslu.

itinerary.title: Trek Lho to Samagaon (3520m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours to the large village of Samagaon, the gateway to Manaslu Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day at Samagaun (3520m)
itinerary.details: Rest and acclimatize. Take an optional day hike to Birendra Lake, Pungen Monastery, or Manaslu Base Camp (4800m).

itinerary.title: Trek Samagaon to Samdo (3860m)
itinerary.details: A short 7-hour trek to Samdo, the highest village in the valley, just 4km from the Tibetan border.

itinerary.title: Trek Samdo to Larkya Phedi / Dharmasala (4480m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours up to the base of the pass, resting at the stone guest house of Dharmasala to prepare for tomorrow.

itinerary.title: Trek Larkya Phedi to Bimthang (3720m) via Larkya La Pass (5160m)
itinerary.details: A massive 9-hour day crossing the dramatic Larkya La Pass (5,160m) before descending steeply into Bimthang.

itinerary.title: Trek Bimthang to Tiliche (2560m)
itinerary.details: Descend 8 hours through rhododendron forests and high grazing pastures to the village of Tiliche.

itinerary.title: Drive Tiliche to Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Take a private jeep for a 9-hour drive back to Kathmandu. Celebrate the trek's completion with a farewell dinner.

treks.additionalInfo: The Manaslu Circuit combined with the Tsum Valley is a strenuous, high-altitude Grade 3 trek. It demands excellent physical conditioning. You will trek through remote regions with basic tea house amenities and cross a massive pass over 5,100m.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Manaslu Tsum Valley Trek?
faqs.answer: This is a Grade 3 Hard/Challenging trek. You will be trekking 6-7 hours daily over steep and rocky terrain, reaching elevations over 5,100m. It requires excellent physical fitness and stamina.

faqs.question: Do I need travel insurance?
faqs.answer: Yes, comprehensive travel insurance is mandatory. It must cover high-altitude medical issues and emergency helicopter evacuation up to 6,000m.

faqs.question: Are the trails crowded?
faqs.answer: Compared to the Annapurna or Everest regions, the Manaslu Circuit and Tsum Valley routes are much less crowded, offering a more peaceful and authentic wilderness experience.

treks.title: Manaslu Circuit Trek 14 Days
treks.description: Manaslu Circuit Trek is categorized as one of the ultimate adventure treks in Nepal, combining the high Himalayas with rich cultural heritage and biological diversity. Located east of the Annapurna range, Mount Manaslu (8,163m) is the eighth-highest peak in the world. This strenuous 14-day trek ascends through the deep gorge of the Budhi Gandaki River, offering numerous waterfalls and diverse landscapes, culminating in the crossing of the formidable snow-clad Larkya La Pass (5,106m). From lush subtropical greenery to spectacular high-altitude glacial landscapes, the trek is visually stunning. Along the way, you will cross an interesting mix of authentic Hindu and Tibetan-style Buddhist villages. Compared to other established routes, this circuit remains relatively less crowded, offering a tranquil and pristine Himalayan experience.
highlights: Trek around Mount Manaslu (8,163m), the eighth-highest peak in the world, on a tranquil, less-crowded trail.
Cross the formidable snow-clad Larkya La Pass (5,106m) for panoramic views of Himlung Himal, Cheo Himal, and Annapurna II.
Experience authentic cultural immersion in remote, Tibetan-influenced Buddhist villages.
Discover diverse landscapes from subtropical jungles and terraced fields to high-altitude alpine meadows and glacial moraines.
Explore the Manaslu Conservation Area, home to unique wildlife like Himalayan marmots, blue sheep, and snow leopards.
Take an acclimatization side trip to the stunning turquoise waters of Birendra Lake or Manaslu Base Camp (4,800m).

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Our representative will greet you at the airport and transfer you to your hotel. Later, we will hold a trip briefing.

itinerary.title: Permit Preparation & Trek Briefing
itinerary.details: We finalize your Restricted Area Permits while you relax or explore Kathmandu. Pre-trip meeting with your guide.

itinerary.title: Drive Kathmandu to Machha Khola (890m)
itinerary.details: Take a scenic 8-hour private jeep ride along the winding roads via Arughat to start your trek at Machha Khola.

itinerary.title: Trek Machha Khola to Jagat (1340m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours along the Budhi Gandaki River, crossing suspension bridges and passing hot springs before entering the Conservation Area at Jagat.

itinerary.title: Trek Jagat to Deng (1860m)
itinerary.details: Ascend 7 hours through lush forests and traditional villages, crossing the Budhi Gandaki River multiple times.

itinerary.title: Trek Deng to Namrung (2630m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours ascending steeply through forests and gompas, noticing a shift towards Tibetan Buddhist culture as you reach Namrung.

itinerary.title: Trek Namrung to Lho (3180m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours past barley fields and beautiful chortens, arriving in Lho village with your first major views of Manaslu.

itinerary.title: Trek Lho to Samagaon (3520m)
itinerary.details: A short 5-hour trek to the large Tibetan settlement of Samagaon, offering close-up views of Mt. Manaslu.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day at Samagaun (3520m)
itinerary.details: Rest and acclimatize. Optional day hikes to the turquoise Birendra Lake, Pungen Monastery, or up to Manaslu Base Camp (4800m).

itinerary.title: Trek Samagaon to Samdo (3860m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours ascending the valley to Samdo, the highest village on the trek, located near the Tibetan border.

itinerary.title: Trek Samdo to Larkya Phedi / Dharamshala (4480m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours up to the base of the pass. Rest early at the stone guest house of Dharamshala to prepare for tomorrow's crossing.

itinerary.title: Trek Larkya Phedi to Bimthang (3720m) via Larkya La Pass (5106m)
itinerary.details: The climax of the trek. An 8-9 hour day crossing the dramatic snow-covered Larkya La Pass, followed by a steep descent into Bimthang.

itinerary.title: Trek Bimthang to Tiliche (2560m)
itinerary.details: Descend 6 hours through high grazing pastures and beautiful rhododendron forests to the village of Tiliche.

itinerary.title: Drive Tiliche to Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Take a private jeep back to Kathmandu via Besisahar. Celebrate the completion of the circuit with a farewell dinner.

3 nights’ accommodation in Kathmandu on BB base (before start the trek).
Professional English-speaking trekking guide (salary, meals, lodging, insurance covered).
Private Jeep to Machha Khola.

Private Jeep to Besishar from Tilche, and Private Jeep to Kathmandu from Besishar.
Tourist service charge, VAT, tax.

Farewell dinner in Kathmandu on the return day.
costExcludes: International airfare, Nepal Entry Visa fees and Insurance.
Beverages, alcoholic drinks, mineral water, boiled water, hot shower, extra meals, upgraded accommodation during the tour.
Lunch, dinner, extra night accommodation in Kathmandu.
Tips for Guide and Porter.
treks.additionalInfo: The Manaslu Circuit is a strenuous Grade 3 trek that ventures into restricted areas. A high level of physical fitness, cardiovascular endurance, and prior trekking experience is highly recommended to safely cross the 5,106m Larkya La Pass.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Manaslu Circuit Trek?
faqs.answer: This is a Grade 3 Hard/Challenging trek. It involves 6-7 hours of daily hiking over steep, rocky terrain and reaching altitudes over 5,100m. It requires a high level of physical fitness and mental preparation.

faqs.question: What permits are required for this trek?
faqs.answer: You will need a TIMS card, a permit to enter the Manaslu Conservation Area, and a special Restricted Area Permit. Our team will prepare these for you in Kathmandu.

faqs.question: Do I need a guide for this trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Manaslu region is a restricted area, and trekking independently is prohibited. You must trek with a licensed guide and be in a group of at least two trekkers.

treks.title: Tsum Valley Trek 11 Days
treks.description: If you are looking for a different trek in the Nepal Himalayas, why not take a trip through the remote and secluded Tsum Valley? It has been open to trekkers for less than 20 years, so it is not as accessible or well-known as classic treks in other parts of the country. This 11-day trek introduces us to Tibetan lifestyles and culture with the many gompas and monasteries we pass through. As we trek through the Manaslu Conservation Area, not only do we meet Buddhist monks and yak herders, but we also run the possibility of meeting rare wildlife like Red Pandas, Snow Leopards, and Blue Sheep. The trails are mainly at elevations over 3,000m, and the views of mountains like Mt Manaslu (8,163m), Ganesh Himal, and Himalchuli are unique. This is a journey through a hidden gem known for its stunning Himalayan views, vibrant Tibetan Buddhist culture, and peaceful atmosphere.
highlights: Explore the remote Tsum Valley, a hidden gem opened to outside trekkers only since 2008.
Visit ancient sacred monasteries like Mu Gompa and Rachen Gompa, rich in spiritual significance.
Discover the Milarepa Cave, where the famous 11th-century Buddhist scholar and yogi meditated.
Enjoy panoramic views of majestic peaks including Mt. Manaslu, Ganesh Himal, and Himalchuli.
Experience a region deeply rooted in Tibetan culture, observing traditions like the Shagya (non-violence) tradition.
Trek through the Manaslu Conservation Area, offering chances to spot elusive wildlife like Snow Leopards and Red Pandas.

itinerary.title: Kathmandu to Maccha Khola (930m) by Private Jeep
itinerary.details: Leave Kathmandu early for a scenic 8-hour drive. We travel along the Trishuli River to Arughat before a bumpy ride to Maccha Khola.

itinerary.title: Trek Maccha Khola to Jagat (1340m)
itinerary.details: A 5-hour trek crossing high suspension bridges over the Budhi Gandaki River, passing lush forests and Gurung villages.

itinerary.title: Trek Jagat to Lokpa (2240m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours through Philim. We diverge from the main Manaslu circuit trail and enter the gateway to the Tsum Valley at Lokpa.

itinerary.title: Trek Lokpa to Chumling (2386m)
itinerary.details: A steep climb through pine and rhododendron forests to the Tibetan-style, stone-paved village of Chumling.

itinerary.title: Trek Chumling to Chekampar (Chokhangparo) (3031m)
itinerary.details: Enter the Upper Tsum Valley, a region deeply influenced by Tibetan culture, with amazing views of Ganesh Himal.

itinerary.title: Trek Chekampar to Nile (3361m)
itinerary.details: A 4-hour spiritual trek visiting Milarepa's Cave and Rachen Gompa before arriving at the last settlement, Nile.

itinerary.title: Day Trip to Mu Gompa (3700m)
itinerary.details: A 5-hour round trip hike to Mu Gompa, the largest and most important monastery in the valley, adorned with stunning murals.

itinerary.title: Trek Nile / Mu Gompa to Chumling (2386m)
itinerary.details: Descend 6 hours through the valley, enjoying the changing vegetation as we return to the greener Lower Tsum Valley.

itinerary.title: Trek Chumling to Philim (1570m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours passing Samba Falls and winding through terraced fields back to the main trail at Philim.

itinerary.title: Trek Philim to Maccha Khola (930m)
itinerary.details: A final 5-hour descent along the Budhi Gandaki River, spending our last night on the trail at Maccha Khola.

itinerary.title: Drive Maccha Khola to Kathmandu (1300m)
itinerary.details: A 9-hour private jeep ride back to the comforts of Kathmandu to celebrate the completion of the trek.

Lunch and Dinner in Kathmandu.

Tips for staff (expected after trek) and expenses due to itinerary changes.
treks.additionalInfo: The Tsum Valley is a sacred region that follows the Shagya Tradition (non-violence). In respect of this century-old tradition, killing animals is prohibited, and only vegetarian meals will be provided at the tea houses.

faqs.question: Is the Tsum Valley a restricted area?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Tsum Valley is a restricted area. A special trekking permit is required and must be obtained through registered trekking agencies.

faqs.question: What is the Shagya Tradition of Tsum Valley?
faqs.answer: It is a century-old tradition of non-violence prohibiting the killing of any living animal. The valley was officially declared a non-violence area in 2008, and only vegetarian meals are served in tea houses.

faqs.question: Can we trek the Tsum Valley independently?
faqs.answer: No, independent trekking is not allowed. You must trek with an organized group through a registered trekking agency.

treks.title: Annapurna Circuit Trek with Tilicho Lake 16 Days
treks.description: The Annapurna Circuit with Tilicho Lake Trek is a popular Himalayan trek offering stunning mountain views, diverse landscapes, and deep cultural experiences. This is one of the most rewarding treks in the Annapurna region that lets you experience Himalayan flora and fauna, holy temples, stunning waterfalls, and varied climate zones. The journey starts with a drive from Kathmandu to Jagat. Along the route, you will pass Tibetan-style settlements and witness magnificent views of Mt. Annapurna, Thorung Peak, Nilgiri, Chulu, Tukuche Peak, Dhaulagiri, and Lamjung Himal. A major highlight is taking a detour to the pristine, turquoise waters of Tilicho Lake (4,920m), often called 'The Great Ice Lake,' surrounded by majestic peaks. The ultimate challenge is crossing the Thorong La Pass (5,416m), before descending to the sacred Muktinath Temple. You will also relax in the natural hot springs of Tatopani and catch a glorious sunrise over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri massifs from the famous Poon Hill viewpoint.
highlights: Cross the formidable Thorong La Pass (5,416m), one of the highest trekking passes in the world.
Take a side trip to the stunning turquoise waters of Tilicho Lake (4,920m), one of the highest lakes in the world.
Witness spectacular sunrise views over the Annapurna and Dhaulagiri ranges from the famous Poon Hill viewpoint.
Discover diverse landscapes, from subtropical forests and terraced farms to high-altitude alpine deserts.
Visit the sacred Muktinath Temple, featuring 108 stone faucets and an eternal flame, revered by Hindus and Buddhists.
Relax your muscles in the natural hot springs at Tatopani and admire the amazing Narchyang waterfall.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Jagat (1300m) by Private Jeep
itinerary.details: Early morning 10-hour drive from Kathmandu to Jagat (175km). Pass beautiful villages, fast-flowing rivers, and green hills.

itinerary.title: Trek from Jagat to Dharapani (1860m)
itinerary.details: A 5-hour trek through barley, rice, and potato fields, passing several waterfalls at Tal Village before reaching Dharapani.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dharapani to Chame (2610m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours through pine and fir forests to Chame, the district headquarters, with remarkable views of Annapurna II.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chame to Upper Pisang (3300m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours through a steep valley to view the massive Paungda Danda Rock Face, then descend to Pisang.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pisang to Manang (3540m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours on the upper trails via Geru for outstanding views. Visit the Barge Monastery, the largest in Manang.

itinerary.title: Rest and Acclimatization day at Manang (3540m)
itinerary.details: Acclimatize in Manang. Take a short hike to Gangapurna Lake or Ice Lake, and visit the Himalayan Rescue Association.

itinerary.title: Trek from Manang to Siri Kharka (4060m)
itinerary.details: A 5-hour trek taking the upper route through coniferous forests and the Tibetan settlement of Khangsar to Siri Kharka.

itinerary.title: Trek from Siri Kharka to Tilicho Base Camp (4150m)
itinerary.details: A 5-hour trek through landslide-prone areas, offering impressive rock formations and views of Tilicho Peak.

itinerary.title: Visit Tilicho Lake (4920m) & Trek back to Siri Kharka (4060m)
itinerary.details: A massive 8-hour day. Ascend steeply to the breathtaking Tilicho Lake (The Great Ice Lake), then retrace back to Siri Kharka.

itinerary.title: Trek from Siri Kharka via Yak Kharka to Ledar (4250m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours descending past the uninhabited Khangsar Village to Yak Kharka and Ledar. Watch out for blue sheep!

itinerary.title: Trek from Ledar to Thorong High Camp (4925m)
itinerary.details: A steep 5-hour uphill climb to Thorong High Camp, the last hamlet before the mighty Thorong La Pass.

itinerary.title: Trek to Muktinath (3760m) via Thorong La Pass (5416m)
itinerary.details: The climax! A 9-hour day starting at 3 AM to cross Thorong La Pass (5,416m), before a steep descent to the holy Muktinath Temple.

itinerary.title: Drive Muktinath to Tatopani (1200m) via Jomsom
itinerary.details: Take a rough 6-hour local jeep ride through the world's deepest gorges to Tatopani. Relax in the natural hot springs.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tatopani to Ghorepani (2860m)
itinerary.details: Trek 9 hours ascending through lush rhododendron and magnolia forests to the ridge-top village of Ghorepani.

itinerary.title: Poon Hill (3210m) Sunrise, Trek to Birethanti, Drive to Pokhara
itinerary.details: Early morning hike to Poon Hill for a spectacular sunrise. Trek down to Birethanti and take a jeep to Pokhara (822m).

itinerary.title: Drive from Pokhara to Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: A 7-hour private jeep ride back to Kathmandu. Celebrate the completion of your epic journey with a farewell dinner.

treks.additionalInfo: The Annapurna Circuit with Tilicho Lake is a physically demanding Grade 3 trek. The luggage limit per trekker is 9kg (sharing one porter per two trekkers). You must pack efficiently using a 60-liter duffle bag. Warm layers (-15°C sleeping bag) are essential for high altitudes.

faqs.question: What makes this trek different from the standard Annapurna Circuit?
faqs.answer: The primary difference is the inclusion of Tilicho Lake. The standard circuit bypasses this detour. Adding Tilicho Lake offers a more challenging route, dramatic scenery, and additional altitude, making the experience more adventurous.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Annapurna Circuit with Tilicho Lake?
faqs.answer: This is a Grade 3 Hard/Challenging trek. It involves 4-7 hours of hiking daily over varied terrain at high altitudes, including the formidable Thorong La Pass (5,416m). Cardiovascular fitness and stamina are essential.

faqs.question: Are hot showers and Wi-Fi available?
faqs.answer: Yes, electricity and Wi-Fi are available in most teahouses, though they usually come at a small extra cost, especially at higher altitudes. Hot showers are also available but may incur an additional fee.

treks.title: Nar Phu Valley Trek 8 Days
treks.description: The Nar Phu Valley, located in the trans-Himalayan region of Nepal, is a remote and less-traveled trekking destination known for its pristine beauty and Tibetan cultural influence. It’s often referred to as 'Little Tibet' due to its unique landscape and the presence of Khampa (Tibetan refugee) communities. Embark on an unforgettable journey through the mystical Nar Phu Valley Trek, a hidden gem in the Annapurna region of Nepal. This 8-day adventure begins in Kathmandu, where you will drive to Koto to kickstart your trekking expedition. From Koto, the trail leads you through quaint villages and rugged terrain as you make your way to Meta, Phu Gaon, and the enchanting Nar Valley. Immerse yourself in the rich culture and traditions of the Tamang and Tibetan communities as you explore remote villages adorned with ancient monasteries and vibrant prayer flags. The trek culminates by crossing the high Kang-La Pass (5,306m) before descending to Humde and driving back to Kathmandu.
highlights: Discover Annapurna's most isolated, unexplored areas in Nepal.
Immerse yourself in the rich culture and traditions of the Tamang and Tibetan communities.
Explore the ancient monasteries, traditional houses, and vibrant prayer flags of Phu Gaon and Nar Valley.
Marvel at breathtaking views of snow-capped peaks, deep gorges, and lush alpine meadows.
Cross the challenging Kang-La Pass (5,306m) offering unparalleled views of the Himalayan peaks.
Experience a unique, off-the-beaten-path trek in the portion of the Tibetan plateau that touches Nepal.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Koto (2700m)
itinerary.details: An 8-9 hour scenic drive from Kathmandu to Koto, offering breathtaking views of the Nepalese countryside as you ascend.

itinerary.title: Trek from Koto to Meta (3560m)
itinerary.details: A 7-hour trek through lush forests and charming villages, gaining altitude with panoramic views of the surrounding valleys.

itinerary.title: Trek from Meta to Phu Gaon (4080m)
itinerary.details: A 6-hour trek into the remote heart of the region. Traverse rugged terrain and rocky paths to reach the picturesque village of Phu Gaon.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization and exploration of Phu Gaon (4250m)
itinerary.details: Spend the day exploring the enchanting village, engaging with friendly locals, and visiting ancient monasteries to acclimatize.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phu Gaon to Nar (4110m)
itinerary.details: A challenging 7-hour trek crossing pristine landscapes to reach Nar, greeted by stunning mountain views and unique cultural heritage.

itinerary.title: Trek Nar to Nawal (3675m) via Kang-La Pass (5306m)
itinerary.details: A demanding 8-hour day crossing the high Kang-La Pass (5,306m) for unparalleled Himalayan views before descending to Nawal.

itinerary.title: Trek to Humde & Drive to Besisahar (820m)
itinerary.details: A short hike to Humde where you will catch a 5-hour drive down to the lower valleys at Besisahar.

itinerary.title: Drive from Besisahar to Kathmandu (1350m)
itinerary.details: A 5-hour scenic drive back to Kathmandu to conclude your incredible Nar Phu Valley adventure.

Government-licensed, English-speaking trekking guide and strong porters (1 porter per 2 people).

Gratuities to guides and staff (recommended).

treks.additionalInfo: The Nar Phu Valley Trek is an off-the-beaten-path adventure that explores highly restricted areas of Nepal, known as 'Little Tibet'. It requires good physical stamina for long ascents and high pass crossings.

faqs.question: Do I need a special permit for the Nar Phu Valley?
faqs.answer: Yes, the Nar Phu Valley is a restricted area. You will need a Nar Phu Valley Special Permit, an Annapurna Conservation Area Permit (ACAP), and a TIMS card.

faqs.question: How difficult is the Nar Phu Valley Trek?
faqs.answer: This is a Grade 3 Hard/Challenging trek. It involves steep ascents, rugged terrain, and crossing the high Kang-La Pass (5,306m). Good physical fitness is required.

faqs.question: Are there teahouses in the Nar Phu Valley?
faqs.answer: Yes, the route has developed to support teahouse trekking, offering basic lodging and meals, allowing you to travel without heavy camping gear.

treks.title: Upper Dolpo Trek traverse 5 Mountain Passes 30 Days
treks.description: Upper Dolpo, situated in the mid-western part of the country between the Dhaulagiri mountain range and the Tibetan plateau is one of the most thrilling and challenging treks to the remote and isolated areas of Nepal. The Upper Dolpo Trek traverse 5 mountain passes is a journey to pure Tibetan region that takes through the undiscovered route in the mountain territory from the foothills of the massive Himalayas to several high passes and remote villages, connecting the desserts of Upper Dolpo with the beautiful Kali Gandaki valley in Mustang. The 30-day amazing journey to Upper Dolpo begins with an amazing scenic flight to Juphal via Nepalgunj. You come across the beautiful Shey Phoksundo Lake (the deepest lake of Nepal), the remote village of Ringmo, and sacred Shey Gompa. Throughout the journey, you pass a series of high passes including Nagdalo La (5350m), Sela La (5095m), Shimen La (4375m), Mola La (5030m), Niwas La (5120m), and Jungben La (5550m). Dolpo is considered the last reserve of pure Tibetan culture left in the world where people still practice the pre-Buddhist Bon Po religion. Traversing across Jungben La (5550m), the trail reaches the Valley of Kali Gandaki River, taking you to Jomsom in Mustang.

quickFacts.bestSeason: Feb to May - Sept to Nov

highlights: Discover Shey Phoksundo National Park and Shey Phoksundo Lake, Nepal's deepest lake surrounded by high hills.
Immerse in Bon Buddhist Culture in Ringmo Village and ancient Shey Gompa.
Traverse 5 major mountain passes including Nagdalo La (5,350m) and the formidable Jungben La Pass (5,550m).
Experience breathtaking views of the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna Mountain Ranges and the unique Crystal Mountain.
Encounter a diverse ecosystem featuring blue sheep, Himalayan black bears, and the elusive snow leopard.
Trek the backdrop of the Oscar-nominated film 'Himalayas' through one of Nepal's most restricted and remote regions.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Welcome to Nepal! Transfer to your 3-star hotel and stroll around the nearby marketplace.

itinerary.title: Guided Sightseeing Tour in Kathmandu Valley
itinerary.details: Explore world heritage sites: Pashupatinath, Boudhanath, Swayambhunath, and Kathmandu Durbar Square. Pre-trip discussion.

itinerary.title: Fly from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj (150m)
itinerary.details: Take a 55-minute domestic flight to Nepalgunj. Experience a change in topography and prepare for the trek.

itinerary.title: Fly to Juphal (2490m) and trek to Dunai (2140m)
itinerary.details: A scenic 35-minute flight to Juphal, followed by a 4-hour trek down to the Thuli Bheri River to Dunai.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dunai to Chhepka (2675m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours entering Shey Phoksundo National Park, walking through pine, cypress, and bamboo forests to Chhepka.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chhepka to Amchi Hospital (3110m)
itinerary.details: Follow the Phoksundo Khola upstream on a narrow path high up in the valley for 5 hours.

itinerary.title: Trek from Amchi Hospital to Ringmo Gaon (3725m)
itinerary.details: Ascend through birch forests to Ringmo village, an attractive settlement with flat-roofed stone houses near Phoksundo Lake.

itinerary.title: Explore Ringmo Gaon and Phoksundo Lake
itinerary.details: Rest day to explore the tranquil, deep blue Phoksundo Lake and the ancient Bon culture of Ringmo village.

itinerary.title: Trek to Chabluk Phu (Dharmasala) (3625m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours following the riverbed of Phoksundo Khola, enjoying views of Kanjirowa Himal (6612m).

itinerary.title: Trek to Nagdalo La Base Camp (4625m)
itinerary.details: Make a steep climb on a cliff above Tuk Kyaksa Khola to reach the Snowfields Camp at the base of Kang La.

itinerary.title: Trek to Shey Gompa (4375m) traverse Nagdalo La (5350m)
itinerary.details: A 7-hour energetic ascent over Ngadalo La (5350m), descending to the 11th-century Shey Gompa below Crystal Mountain.

itinerary.title: Explore Shey Gompa and Tsakang Gompa
itinerary.details: Rest and explore the ancient Gompa renowned for its giant copper and gold-plated statue of a seated Sakyamuni Buddha.

itinerary.title: Trek to Namgung (4430m) traverse Sela La Pass (5095m)
itinerary.details: A 9-hour day crossing Sela La, enjoying sights of the northern Tibetan plateau, descending to the meadows of Namgung.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namgung to Saldang (3980m)
itinerary.details: A 4-hour trek to Saldang, a wealthy, historically significant village situated on an ancient trade route to Tibet.

itinerary.title: Trek from Saldang to Khomagaon (4100m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours across a vast landscape of sand dunes and bare hills, passing white-washed villages and long Mani walls.

itinerary.title: Trek to Shimen (3850m) traverse Shimen La Pass (4375m)
itinerary.details: Cross Shimen La and climb down along arid terrain to the Panjyan Khola to reach Shimen Gompa.

itinerary.title: Trek from Shimen to Tinje (4110m)
itinerary.details: Move downhill along off-road trails above the gorge, visiting ancient Pu Gompa before arriving at Tinje.

itinerary.title: Explore Tinje village
itinerary.details: Explore the main village in this extensive valley, visiting two Gompas, an old fortress, and traditional artists.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tinje to Rapka (4535m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours alongside the Panjyan Khola, crossing several bridges to reach the Rapka campsite.

itinerary.title: Trek to Chharka Bhot (4110m) traverse Mola La Pass (5030m)
itinerary.details: An 8-hour day climbing Mola La Pass (5030m) before descending to the Chharka Village on the Tulsi Khola.

itinerary.title: Explore Chharka Bhot
itinerary.details: Rest and explore the village's two gompas, Buddhist and Bönpo, representing the dual religious nature of Dolpo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chharka Bhot to Norbulung (4750m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours, ascending an uneven trail to a big meadow, getting views of the Dhaulagiri massif.

itinerary.title: Trek from Norbulung to Molum Sumdo (4860m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours ascending slowly to a yak pasture, Molum Sumdo, for great views of Dhaulagiri II.

itinerary.title: Trek to Ghalden Ghuldun (4247m) traverse Niwas La (5120m) & Jungben La (5550m)
itinerary.details: A massive 9-hour day crossing two high passes, including the highest point of the trek (5550m), before descending to Santa.

itinerary.title: Trek from Ghalden Ghuldun to Santa Village (3777m)
itinerary.details: Leave Dolpo behind and enter the Annapurna Conservation Area, navigating steep gorges to reach Santa.

itinerary.title: Trek from Santa Village to Phalyak (3175m)
itinerary.details: An 8-hour day crossing Bhima Lojun La (4460m) and descending steeply through forests to the Mustangi village of Phalyak.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phalyak to Jomsom (2724m)
itinerary.details: A short 4-hour walk through the Kali Gandaki riverbed to the windy town of Jomsom to celebrate.

itinerary.title: Fly from Jomsom to Pokhara
itinerary.details: A stunning 25-minute scenic flight out of the mountains to the lakeside city of Pokhara. Rest in a 3-star hotel.

itinerary.title: Buffer Day & Fly back to Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Contingency day for flights. Afternoon flight back to Kathmandu. Relax and enjoy the city.

itinerary.title: Final Departure from Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Transfer to the airport 3 hours before your scheduled flight. Farewell from Nepal!

faqs.question: How difficult is the Upper Dolpo Trek?
faqs.answer: The Upper Dolpo Trek is considered a challenging Grade 3 trek due to its high altitude (reaching 5,550m), remote location, and demanding terrain traversing 5 major mountain passes. It requires excellent physical fitness and prior trekking experience.

faqs.question: Is it possible to obtain a permit for the Upper Dolpo Trek?
faqs.answer: Yes, but Upper Dolpo is a highly restricted area. Special permits must be arranged through a registered trekking company and issued by the Nepalese government.

faqs.question: What is the accommodation like?
faqs.answer: Accommodation is primarily in twin-sharing tented camps, as the infrastructure in this remote region is very basic. Our crew sets up dining tents, kitchen tents, and sleeping tents, providing a rugged yet fully supported adventure.

treks.title: Lower Dolpo Trek 18 Days
treks.description: Lower Dolpo Trek is one of the most exciting and challenging treks situated in the western hills of Nepal, which allows the trekkers to experience the real adventures of trekking on an off-the-beaten path, composed of steep sloppy hills. Lower Dolpo Trek is packed with amazing gifts of nature, including Shey Phoksundo Lake and also boasts of the pre-Buddhism Bon Po culture. The 18-day Lower Dolpo Trek begins with a flight from Kathmandu to Juphal via Nepalgunj. You trek through semi-desert region combined with densely forested paths filled with pine, rhododendrons, bamboo, and juniper trees. You also enter the beautiful Shey Phoksundo National Park, inhabited by endangered animals like the snow leopard, Himalayan musk deer, and blue sheep. The trekkers also traverse through two high passes: Numa La Pass (5310m) and Baga La Pass (5170m), which offer extraordinary views of Mt. Dhaulagiri (8167m). Another highlight of the trek includes the pristine turquoise Phoksundo Lake, split between rocks that rise 2000m into the clear mountain skies. The Dolpo region is populated by Tibetan and Magar people who still practice the pre-Buddhist Bon Po religion.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Traverse untouched landscapes and remote villages in Nepal's western Himalayas for a sense of isolation and tranquility.
Interact with the Dolpo-pa people and explore ancient monasteries practicing the pre-Buddhist Bon religion.
Spot endangered wildlife such as snow leopards and blue sheep in Shey Phoksundo National Park.
Cross challenging high passes like Numa La (5,310m) and Baga La (5,170m) for panoramic views of Mt. Dhaulagiri.
Visit the majestic turquoise waters of Phoksundo Lake, Nepal's deepest alpine freshwater lake.
Enjoy scenic domestic flights from Kathmandu to Nepalgunj and on to the remote Juphal airstrip.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu (1400m)

itinerary.title: Permit procedure and fly to Nepalgunj (150m)
itinerary.details: Process necessary permits in Kathmandu before taking a scenic flight to Nepalgunj, an important business center near the Indian border.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tarakot to Laina Odar (3375m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours following the Tarap Khola. Relish views of Putha Hiunchuli and the Churen Himal Range before a steep ascend to Laina Odar.

itinerary.title: Trek from Laina Odar to Toltol (3523m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours through the deep gorge of the Tarap River on paths carved from steep slopes to reach the winter settlement of Toltol.

itinerary.title: Trek from Toltol to Dho Tarap (3950m)
itinerary.details: Trek 7 hours moving out of the tree line into forested paths of wild rose and juniper to Dho Tarap, an ancient Tibetan trading point.

itinerary.title: Excursion around Dho Tarap
itinerary.details: Acclimatization day. Explore monasteries, learn about the Bon-Po and Nyigmapa religions, and observe the unique homespun clothing.

itinerary.title: Trek to Numa La Base Camp (4350m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours uphill past the traditional village of Tokyu, continuing through rugged trails to the base of Numa La.

itinerary.title: Trek to Danighar (4510m) via Numa La Pass (5310m)
itinerary.details: A difficult 8-hour day climbing to the top of Numa La (5,310m) for extraordinary views of Mt. Dhaulagiri before descending to Danighar.

itinerary.title: Trek to Temche/Yak Kharka (4110m) via Baga La Pass (5170m)
itinerary.details: A 6-hour steep ascent over Baga La (5,170m) passing sacred Chortens, descending into a deep ravine to reach Temche.

itinerary.title: Trek from Yak Kharka to Shey Phoksundo Lake (3600m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours ascending to the famous Bon settlement of Ringmo and arriving at the stunning turquoise waters of Phoksundo Lake.

itinerary.title: Explore around Shey Phoksundo Lake
itinerary.details: Rest day to explore the deepest lake in Nepal and the 900-year-old Tshowa Bon Monastery near Ringmo.

itinerary.title: Trek from Shey Phoksundo Lake to Chhepka (2678m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours gradually descending through beautiful pine and birch forests back towards Chhepka.

itinerary.title: Trek from Chhepka to Juphal (2475m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours passing the national park check post and walking through fields of barley and wheat to return to Juphal.

itinerary.title: Fly from Juphal to Nepalgunj & return to Kathmandu
itinerary.details: Catch an early morning flight from Juphal to Nepalgunj, followed by a connecting flight back to Kathmandu. Rest at your hotel.

itinerary.title: Buffer day in Kathmandu
itinerary.details: A contingency day for potential flight delays or cancellations due to bad weather in the mountains.

itinerary.details: Transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for your final departure.

faqs.question: How difficult is Lower Dolpo Trekking?
faqs.answer: This trek comprises several ups and downs and two high passes over 5000 meters which is physically demanding. So, this trek is listed as among the difficult treks in Nepal.

faqs.question: What is Dolpa famous for?
faqs.answer: Trekking into Dolpa presents an exposure to the high and remote Himalayan valleys, resembling the Tibetan highlands. The main highlight includes Shey Phoksundo National Park and Shey Phoksundo Lake.

faqs.question: What is the age limit for trekking?
faqs.answer: While there is no age restriction, the recommended minimum age for children is around ten, and up to 50+ years for older people, provided they are in good physical condition.

treks.title: Mardi Himal Peak Climbing 12 Days
treks.description: Mardi Himal Climb is one of the most beautiful, short, easy trekking peaks in Nepal. It remains beneath the Machhapuchhre edge in the Annapurna range. Mardi Himal (5,587 m), is one of the lowest trekking peaks in Nepal. It is ideal for mountaineers who want to gain some mountain climbing experience before taking on 8000m mountains. The climbers of this peak do not require any previous mountaineering experience. The climbers can observe snow-capped mountains, including Annapurna I-III, Gangapurna, Mt. Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre, Fang Peak, Him Chuli, and Singu Chuli from the summit. The Mardi Himal region is a virgin landscape in Nepal that has yet to be explored. This unique peak climbing also includes a trekking adventure in the Himalayan foothills. Trekkers need to trek for around two weeks to arrive at the base of Mardi Himal, allowing them to explore the Thakali, Gurung, and Magar communities' culture, tradition, and lifestyle. The trails are covered in Buddhist prayer flags, chortens, and mani walls. Mardi Himal peak climbing is a strenuous trek and climb in Nepal, reaching a maximum elevation of 5,587 meters. The main climbing route ascends the East face over snow terrain, passing a col at 5,200 meters.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Climb Mardi Himal (5,587m), a less-explored peak offering a solitary and peaceful climbing experience.
Enjoy panoramic views of the Annapurna range, including a close-up of the rugged southwest face of Machhapuchhre.
Trek through dense rhododendron forests, alpine meadows, and remote, rugged high-altitude terrain.
Experience a low altitude summit climb ideal for beginners seeking to gain mountaineering experience.
Interact with local communities and experience the unique culture of the Gurung and Magar people in villages like Siding.
Observe diverse wildlife, including the national bird of Nepal, the Danphe (Pheasant).

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu Airport and Hotel transfer (1400m)
itinerary.details: Welcome to Nepal! Transfer to your hotel. Meet the team, get a trip briefing, and enjoy a warm welcome dinner.

itinerary.title: Drive from Kathmandu to Pokhara (820m)
itinerary.details: Take a scenic 5-6 hour drive (200km) to Pokhara, enjoying views of green hills and winding rivers along the way.

itinerary.title: Drive to Phedi & Trek to Pothana (1890m)
itinerary.details: Drive 1 hour to Phedi. Start your 3-4 hour trek passing through Dhampus with stunning Annapurna views to reach Pothana.

itinerary.title: Trek from Pothana to Forest Camp (2500m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours along green forested trails, gaining altitude while enjoying the breezy atmosphere and diverse wildlife.

itinerary.title: Trek from Forest Camp to High Camp (3550m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours through adventurous trails passing green forests to reach High Camp. Experience the local tea house lifestyle.

itinerary.title: Trek from High Camp to Mardi Himal Base Camp (4500m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours through the foothills of the mountain. Acclimatize and prepare for the summit at Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Summit Mardi Himal (5587m) and back to Base Camp (4500m)
itinerary.details: The critical 7-hour summit day! Cross some technical sections on the East face to reach the top for breathtaking views of Machhapuchhre.

itinerary.title: Trek from Base Camp to Lo Camp (3000m)
itinerary.details: After clearing the camp, descend 4-5 hours to Lo Camp, enjoying the changing vegetation and different mountain perspectives.

itinerary.title: Trek from Lo Camp to Siding Village (1700m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours down to the beautiful village of Siding. Observe ancient architecture and interact with the friendly locals.

itinerary.title: Drive from Siding village to Pokhara (822m)
itinerary.details: Take a 3-hour private jeep ride from Siding back to Pokhara. Relax by the lake and explore the vibrant nightlife.

itinerary.title: Flight back from Pokhara to Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Catch a quick 35-minute scenic flight back to Kathmandu. Transfer to your hotel for rest and last-minute shopping.

itinerary.details: Transfer to Tribhuvan International Airport for your flight home, bringing your Mardi Himal adventure to a close.

faqs.question: How tall is the Mardi Himal?
faqs.answer: The Mardi Himal has an elevation of 5587m above sea level.

faqs.question: The best time for the Mardi Himal Peak Climbing in Nepal?
faqs.answer: Spring (April - May) and Autumn (October - November) are ideal for the Mardi Himal climbing adventure. There are moderate temperatures and stable weather conditions in the region.

faqs.question: How difficult Is Mardi Himal Peak Climbing?
faqs.answer: Mardi Himal is a low elevation trekking peak at just 5587 m. Hence, you can complete this climb even though you have not trekked on any high altitude conditions before. With proper packing and preparation, you can climb Mardi Himal with ease. However, finding the route towards the summit and couloirs on the East Face col pose some challenges.

faqs.question: Do you need any previous peak climbing experience to climb Mardi Himal in Nepal?
faqs.answer: Mardi Himal peak climbing does not require any previous experience in mountain climbing. Hence, it is ideal for beginners to take this peak climbing adventure. However, they must go through a proper training regime with climbing equipment and gear.

faqs.question: How to tackle altitude sickness?
faqs.answer: Acclimatization is a must while trekking and climbing in high altitude conditions. A slow and steady trek at a gentle pace is crucial. You should never climb more than 600m in a single trekking day. Hydrate regularly and do not drink alcohol.

faqs.question: Are guides and a porter essential for this Mardi peak climb?
faqs.answer: A local professional guide will help you with navigation and provide motivation. Porters help you carry your luggage and keep your equipment safe. You will have an excellent adventure with a local guide.

faqs.question: Where will you stay along the trek?
faqs.answer: Trekkers will stay in local tea houses along trails that provide basic facilities of meals and accommodations. There are twin beds, sheets, mattresses, pillows, and a blanket in these teahouses' rooms.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance needed for the trip?
faqs.answer: Proper travel insurance is essential, and it must cover medical emergencies, physical injuries, evacuation, flight delays, accidents, and must cover above 4000m in high altitudes.

faqs.question: Is oxygen required during the Mardi Himal climb?
faqs.answer: An oxygen cylinder is not required during the Mardi Himal peak climbing as it is a low altitude climb. However, you should acclimatize well to tackle altitude sickness.

faqs.question: What are the emergency protocols during the climb?
faqs.answer: Our team members have experience in first aid. Besides that, Helicopter evacuation is also available in case of emergencies.

treks.title: Pisang Peak Climbing 15 Days
treks.description: Pisang Peak (6,091 meters/19,984 feet), also known as Jong Ri, lies between Annapurna I and Manaslu in the Manang district. In the year 1955, a German Expedition team first climbed the Pisang Peak successfully. Pisang Peak thereafter came to limelight and has become a popular trekking peak in the Annapurna region. The trekking offers a captivating journey through diverse landscapes, cultural sites, and vast biodiversity. Likewise, climbing and summiting the peak is a thrilling and triumphant moment. Pisang Peak is straightforward, with quick climbing experience. Though Pisang Peak is characterized as an easy climbing Peak in the Himalayas, a fair enough fitness level with sound health conditions is required for a successful adventure. Summiting Pisang Peak offers close-range panoramic views of stunning mountain peaks, including Annapurna, Chulu Range, Manaslu, Himlung, Tilicho Peak, Damodar, etc. The 15-day Pisang Peak Climbing itinerary offers a fascinating and adventurous journey in the Himalayas with a harmonious balance of the trek and climb.

quickFacts.bestSeason: Feb to May - Sept to Nov

highlights: Adventurous climb of the 6,000-meter class peak with panoramic views of the Annapurna and Manaslu ranges.
Cross the high mountain Thorong La Pass (5,416 meters) offering incredible panoramic views.
Experience technical climbing using ropes, ice axes, and crampons on the final ascent to the summit.
Traverse the enchanting landscapes of bamboo and rhododendron forests and cross the pristine Marsyangdi River.
Explore the wonderful Annapurna Circuit and the pristine Manang and Mustang regions.
Visit and explore the religious pilgrimage site of the Hindus and Buddhists, the holy Muktinath Temple.

itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours uphill, gaining deep insights into Tibetan-style culture as you make your way to Chame, the headquarters of Manang.

itinerary.title: Trek From Chame to Upper Pisang (3700m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours into an alpine environment. See terraced farmlands and Tibetan-style houses as Pisang Peak and the Annapurna range come into view.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day At Upper Pisang
itinerary.details: Rest and explore Upper Pisang. Take short hikes to acclimatize, check your climbing equipment, and marvel at the mountain views.

itinerary.title: Trek from Upper Pisang to Pisang Peak Base Camp (4380m)
itinerary.details: Trek 3-4 hours ascending through alpine terrains and rocky paths to reach the base camp, where you'll stay overnight in tents.

itinerary.title: Trek to Pisang Peak High Camp (5400m)
itinerary.details: Trek 3-4 hours on narrow, rocky, and potentially snowy trails to High Camp. Acclimatize and prepare for the summit push.

itinerary.title: Summit Pisang Peak (6091m) and Back to Base Camp (4380m)
itinerary.details: The 7-9 hour summit day! Navigate steep technical sections with fixed ropes to reach the summit. Celebrate the triumph and descend to Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek From Pisang Peak Base Camp to Manang Valley (3450m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours descending to connect back with the Annapurna Circuit trail and walking alongside the riverbeds to Manang.

itinerary.title: Trek From Manang to Yak Kharka (4110m)
itinerary.details: Trek 3-4 hours ascending steep uphills towards the high-altitude grazing pastures of Yak Kharka.

itinerary.title: Trek From Yak Kharka to Thorong Phedi (4600m)
itinerary.details: Trek 3-4 hours on rugged rocky paths, entering high alpine terrains at the foot of the challenging Thorong La Pass.

itinerary.title: Cross Thorong La (5416m) and Trek to Muktinath (3710m)
itinerary.details: An epic 8-10 hour day. Start early to conquer the pass, then enjoy a long descent to the holy pilgrimage site of Muktinath.

itinerary.title: Drive From Muktinath to Tatopani (1190m)
itinerary.details: Drive 6-7 hours descending rapidly from the arid landscapes to the sub-tropical environment of Tatopani. Relax in the natural hot springs.

itinerary.title: Drive From Tatopani to Pokhara (822m)
itinerary.details: Drive 5-6 hours along the Kali Gandaki Gorge to reach the lakeside city of Pokhara, culminating your adventurous journey.

faqs.question: What kinds of gear and clothing do I need?
faqs.answer: Good hiking and mountaineering boots. Gloves, down jacket, rain gear, fleece. You will need sock liners, wool socks. Make sure you have trainers for camps. Wicking layers are great.

faqs.question: What is the best season for peak climbing in Nepal?
faqs.answer: March to May, September to November is the best season for peak climbing in Nepal.

faqs.question: What equipment does company provide and can we rent some?
faqs.answer: You can hire or buy personal equipment needed for peak climbing. Normal gear like Sleeping bags and down jackets will be provided by the company.

treks.title: Tent or Tharpu Peak Climbing 18 Days
treks.description: Tent Peak climbing is one of the most popular peak climbing destinations in the Annapurna region of Nepal. It stands at the height of 5663 meters and within the Annapurna sanctuary. The Tent peak is also popular to the name Tharpu Chuli. The trail to Tent Peak climbing goes through the large rhododendron forest, rugged landscapes, terrace farmings, and local settlements. The route passes through some of the attractive villages of Brahmin, Chhetri, Gurung, and Magar. Lying to the south of Annapurna Base Camp, Tent Peak is a relatively small and easy trekking peak in Nepal. Reaching the top of the summit offers trekkers with some of the breathtaking views of Mount Annapurna, Hiunchuli, Machhapuchhre, Dhaulagiri, and several other peaks. The 18 days Tent Peak climbing package provides you with proper acclimatization.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Breathtaking views of the Annapurna Sanctuary and surrounding peaks including Annapurna I, Machhapuchhre (Fishtail), and Hiunchuli.
Ascend to the summit of Tent Peak (Tharpu Chuli) at 5,663m for an astounding 360-degree panorama of the Annapurna massif.
Trek through diverse landscapes, including lush rhododendron forests, terraced farmland, and traditional Gurung villages.
Enjoy the natural hot springs of Jhinu Danda after a rewarding climbing experience.
Combine the famous Annapurna Base Camp (ABC) trek with a relatively accessible, non-technical peak climb.
Experience climbing on snow and ice slopes using mountaineering gear like crampons and ice axes.

itinerary.title: Trek to Chhumrong (2170m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours crossing the Kimrong Khola and walking over ridges to reach Chhumrong, the gateway to the sanctuary.

itinerary.title: Trek to Dovan (2500m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6-7 hours descending to the Chhomrong Khola, then climbing up to Sinuwa before walking through bamboo forests to Dovan.

itinerary.title: Trek to Deurali (3250m)
itinerary.details: Trek 3-4 hours alongside the Modi Khola, passing Himalaya Hotel and Hinku Cave. A short day to help with acclimatization.

itinerary.title: Trek to Annapurna Base Camp (4130m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours passing avalanche areas to Machhapuchhre Base Camp, then a gradual climb beside the moraine to Annapurna Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Excursion around Annapurna Base Camp Lodge
itinerary.details: Acclimatization day. Enjoy the panoramic views and receive basic climbing techniques and training from our experts.

itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours descending to the glacier region, crossing an icy trail, and ascending the moraine to the Tent Peak Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek to Tent Peak High Camp (4900m)
itinerary.details: Trek 3-4 hours making a steep uphill climb. Enjoy magnificent views of Hiunchuli, Annapurna, and Machhapuchhre from High Camp.

itinerary.title: Tharpuchuli (Tent Peak) Summit (5663m) and return to High Camp
itinerary.details: Trek 7-8 hours. Start early, climb the steep slopes using fixed ropes, and reach the summit for incredible 360-degree views! Descend back to High Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Machhapuchhre Base Camp (3700m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours descending through Annapurna Base Camp and continuing down to Machhapuchhre Base Camp.

itinerary.title: Trek to Dovan Lodge (2500m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours descending back past Deurali, Hinku Cave, and the Himalaya Hotel to reach Dovan.

itinerary.title: Trek down to Jhinu / hot spring (1760m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours passing Bamboo and Sinuwa, descending to Chhomrong Khola, and arriving at Jhinu to relax in the natural hot springs.

faqs.question: Can I get an arrival visa in Nepal?
faqs.answer: Yes, one can get a visa at the Nepalese Embassy or consulate or at the airport upon arrival.

faqs.question: What kind of accommodation can we get on Annapurna Base Camp Trek?
faqs.answer: The accommodation is in native teahouses/guesthouses. At base camp and high camp for climbing, accommodation is in tented camps on a twin-share basis.

faqs.question: What is the elevation of Annapurna Base Camp?
faqs.answer: Annapurna Base Camp is at an elevation of 4,130 meters / 13,550 feet.

treks.title: Yala Peak Climbing 13 Days
treks.description: Yala Peak Climb (5,500m) is an exciting and easy climb located near the Nepal-Tibet border of Nepal. Langtang National Park is nearby and is popular for the Gosainkunda and Helambu treks. Yala Peak is one of Nepal’s less technical trekking peaks, making it suitable for those with some trekking experience. However, good physical fitness is necessary. You do not need any previous mountaineering experience to climb this 5,500m peak. Our 13-day Yala Peak Climbing program starts with a seven-hour drive from Kathmandu. We’ll stop at Kyanjing Gompa (3,800m) for acclimatization before heading to Yala Base Camp. After successfully summiting Yala Peak, you can either return directly to Dhunche or trek via Gosainkund Pass to Helambu. The geology around Yala Peak is characterized by diverse terrain from plush rhododendron forests to high-altitude meadows connected by rocky paths. Yala Peak is home to various animals, including the snow leopard and red panda.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

highlights: Enjoy one of Nepal’s peaceful treks in the magnificent Langtang Valley, despite being closer to Kathmandu.
Experience the stunning mountain ranges of the Langtang region, including Langtang Lirung and Ganesh Himal.
Experience a relatively low-altitude Himalayan climbing adventure on Yala Peak without prior mountaineering experience.
Immerse yourself in the unique culture and traditions of the Langtang people, encountering friendly Tamang and Sherpa communities.
Visit the historic Kyanjin Gompa monastery and explore the local cheese factory.
Navigate through Langtang National Park, housing varied wildlife like red pandas and snow leopards.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu and transfer to the hotel (1355m)
itinerary.details: Welcome to the Himalayas! Transfer to your hotel via a private vehicle, followed by a trip briefing and welcome dinner with cultural dance.

itinerary.details: Drive 7 hours north along the riverbanks to Syabrubesi, the starting point of the trek. Spend the night at a local lodge.

itinerary.title: Trek to Lama Hotel (2400m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours passing through bamboo forests and the Landslide area, following the bank of the Langtang river up to Lama Hotel.

itinerary.title: Trek to Langtang Village (3330m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours deeper into the Himalayas. Pass the army check post at Ghoratabela and walk through small settlements to reach Langtang Village.

itinerary.title: Trek to Kyanjin Gompa (3870m)
itinerary.details: Trek 3-4 hours on a relatively easy day to reach Kyanjin Gompa, the last settlement in the valley. Visit the famous local cheese factory.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization Day
itinerary.details: Spend the day exploring around Kyanjin Gompa and optionally hike to Tsergo-Ri (4985m) for majestic views to help with acclimatization.

itinerary.title: Trek to Yala Peak Base Camp (5033m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours to reach Yala Base Camp. Enjoy stunning views of peaks like Naya Kanga, Tsergo Ri, and Ganchenpo from your tented camp.

itinerary.title: Summit Yala Peak (5500m) and back to Kyanjin Gompa (3870m)
itinerary.details: Trek 8 hours. Start early to conquer the summit of Yala Peak, enjoying fascinating views of Tibetan mountains. Descend all the way back to Kyanjin Gompa.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Lama Hotel (2400m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours retracing your steps through the villages and forests, enjoying alternative perspectives of the valley.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Syabrubesi (1550m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5 hours mostly downhill through dense forests of rhododendron, oak, and pine trees back to Syabrubesi.

itinerary.title: Drive back to Kathmandu (1355m)
itinerary.details: Drive 5-6 hours back to Kathmandu enjoying the terraced farming and green highlands. Farewell dinner in the evening to celebrate the summit.

itinerary.details: Enjoy a guided sightseeing tour of the Kathmandu Valley, visiting Swayambhunath, Pashupatinath, Boudhanath, and Kathmandu Durbar Square.

itinerary.details: Our representative will drop you off at the international airport for your flight home. Safe travels!

treks.additionalInfo: Yala Peak is a fantastic introductory climb in the Himalayas. Ya' in Yala comes from 'Yalmo' meaning Yeti, and 'la' means peak. Legend has it that many yetis inhabited the area!

faqs.question: How high is the Yala Peak summit?
faqs.answer: Yala Peak’s summit reaches an elevation of approximately 5,500 meters (18,044 feet) above sea level.

faqs.question: Do you need trekking gear like a harness or crampons during the Yala Peak summit?
faqs.answer: While Yala Peak is considered a non-technical climb, it often requires the use of trekking gear such as crampons, especially depending on the season and snow conditions.

faqs.question: How long does it take to climb Yala Peak?
faqs.answer: The overall Yala Peak expedition typically takes 10 to 14 days. The climb from the base camp to the summit generally takes 7 to 8 hours.

treks.title: LOBUCHE PEAK (6119M) + EBC TREK 17 Days
treks.description: Lobuche Peak climbing, particularly Lobuche East Peak, offers a unique adventure in Nepal's Everest region, blending trekking and mountaineering. It's known for stunning views, a challenging climb, and cultural immersion in the Sherpa region. The peak itself, at 6,119 meters (20,075 feet), rewards climbers with panoramic vistas of Everest, Lhotse, and other iconic Himalayan peaks. Lobuche Peak is a well-known trekking peak of Nepal located in the Khumbu region. Consisting of two faces; Lobuche East (6,119m) and Lobuche West (6,145m), the Lobuche peak lies just above the Lobuche village and Khumbu Glacier. Lobuche East Peak climbing is the best plan for beginners to tick the very first peak climb of their life. This not too difficult trekking peak offers a beautiful but learnable climbing experience.
highlights: Reach the summit of Lobuche East Peak which stands at 6,119m and eyeshot the breathtaking Himalayan panorama from the top.
Heavenly views of Mt Everest, Mt Lhotse, Mt Makalu, Mt Nuptse, Mt Amadablam, Mt Pumori, and several more peaks.
Trek over the trail of the most popular Everest Base Camp Trek until Lobuche.
Explore the uniquely established Sherpa settlements and their culture amid prayer flags, gompas, and Monasteries.
The trek to the base camp of the highest peak in the world, Mt. Everest, and Kala Patthar, the best viewpoint of Mt. Everest.
The short and exciting Mountain Flight to and from the Lukla Airport.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Kathmandu Airport and Hotel transfer (1400m)
itinerary.details: Welcome to Nepal! Enjoy a quick and hassle-free hotel transfer, followed by a warm welcome dinner with the expedition team.

itinerary.title: Arrangement Day
itinerary.details: Preparation day. Attend a trip briefing, meet your trekking and climbing guides, and check your gear for the expedition.

itinerary.title: Fly to Lukla (2860m) and trek to Phakding (2610m)
itinerary.details: Take a scenic 40-minute mountain flight to Lukla. Meet your porters and trek 4 hours alongside the Dudh Koshi River to Phakding.

itinerary.title: Trek from Phakding to Namche Bazaar (3446m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours crossing suspension bridges and entering Sagarmatha National Park. Make the final ascent to Namche Bazaar, the hub of the Khumbu.

itinerary.title: Acclimatization in Namche Bazaar
itinerary.details: Rest day to acclimatize. Hike to the Everest View Hotel for stunning views of Everest, Lhotse, and Ama Dablam.

itinerary.title: Trek from Namche Bazaar to Tengboche (3800m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours enjoying beautiful mountain views. Ascend to Tengboche to visit the largest and most famous monastery in the Everest region.

itinerary.title: Trek from Tengboche to Dingboche (4347m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours walking through lush forests and crossing the Imja Khola to reach the scenic village of Dingboche.

itinerary.title: Rest and Explore Dingboche (4410m), Hike to Nagarjun Peak
itinerary.details: Acclimatization day. Hike 2-3 hours up Nagarjun Peak (4900m) for magnificent views, following the 'climb high, sleep low' principle.

itinerary.title: Trek from Dingboche to Lobuche (4940m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours moving through rough and steep trails past the memorial stupas at Thukla, walking along the Khumbu Glacier to Lobuche.

itinerary.title: Trek to Gorakshep and Everest Base Camp (5364m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6-7 hours. Reach Gorakshep, leave your bags, and hike along the Khumbu Glacier to the iconic Everest Base Camp! Return to Gorakshep.

itinerary.title: Hike to Kalapatthar (5644m) and Trek to Lobuche (4940m)
itinerary.details: Trek 6-7 hours. Start early to hike Kala Patthar for the best sunrise view of Mount Everest. Descend back to Lobuche for the night.

itinerary.title: Trek to Lobuche High Camp (5300m)
itinerary.details: Trek 3-4 hours on steep, rough trails to reach High Camp. Rest in tents and undergo a climbing skills and gear usage session with your guide.

itinerary.title: Summit Day (6119m) Lobuche East and Trek Down to Pheriche (4371m)
itinerary.details: Trek 8-10 hours. Ascend the steep, icy southern ridge using fixed ropes and crampons. Reach the summit for an incredible panorama! Descend safely to Pheriche.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Namche (3446m)
itinerary.details: Trek 5-6 hours making the long but beautiful descent back to the comforts and lively atmosphere of Namche Bazaar.

itinerary.title: Trek back to Lukla (2800m)
itinerary.details: Trek 4-5 hours retracing your steps along the Dudh Koshi River and exiting the National Park to arrive back in Lukla.

itinerary.title: Fly back to Kathmandu (1400m)
itinerary.details: Take the 40-minute scenic morning flight back to Kathmandu. Transfer to your hotel to celebrate the successful expedition!

itinerary.title: Final Departure
itinerary.details: Departure day. Our team will drop you off at the international airport according to your flight schedule.

faqs.question: Will I get charging and internet facilities on the peak climbing journey?
faqs.answer: Yes, but until the Lobuche village only. From Lobuche, there are no teahouses further and you have to spend overnights in tented camps.

faqs.question: What are the permits required for the Lobuche climb?
faqs.answer: You have to get a peak climbing permit which is issued by the Nepal Mountaineering Association, along with Sagarmatha National Park entry permit.

faqs.question: How hard is Lobuche Peak Climbing?
faqs.answer: Lobuche peak is one of the difficult trekking peaks in Nepal. There is one technical section while ascending the summit where a climber has to ascend 45 degrees steeped snowy trail. Prior mountaineering training is recommended.

treks.title: Singu Chuli Peak Climbing 20 Days
treks.description: A slightly more difficult climb than the neighboring Tharpu Chuli peak climb, but with all the thrills and excitement you would expect climbing through ice and snow at this altitude. Singu Chuli Peak (6,501m) is also known as Fluted Peak and is located within the Annapurna Conservation Area, a place rich in a unique flora, fauna and the effervescent smiles of the local Gurung people and their rich Tibetan Buddhist faith. The views are amazing, especially with the south face of Annapurna as a backdrop. The trek begins at Birethanti and passes through the villages of Ghandruk, Chomrong and Ghorepani before arriving at Machapuchare (Fishtail) Base Camp. From here you have some absolutely fantastic in-your-face panoramic views of some of the world’s highest mountains.

quickFacts.bestSeason: March to May / Sept to Nov

Trek to Annapurna Base Camp, offering stunning views of towering peaks and glaciers in a serene spiritual atmosphere.
Technical ascent of Singu Chuli, requiring experience in ice and rock climbing and specialized equipment.
Summit views providing panoramas of the Annapurna massif, including Annapurna I and Machhapuchhre.
Cultural immersion in traditional Gurung and Tibetan Buddhist villages.
Combine the climb with the ascent of Tharpu Chuli (Tent Peak).

faqs.question: How difficult is Singu Chuli Peak Climbing?
faqs.answer: Singu Chuli Peak Climbing is considered a challenging endeavor, requiring technical mountaineering skills and previous high-altitude climbing experience. The steep slopes, ice sections, and exposed ridges make it a demanding climb.

faqs.question: Do I need prior climbing experience to attempt Singu Chuli Peak?
faqs.answer: Yes, Singu Chuli Peak is considered a challenging climb and requires previous mountaineering experience. It is recommended for experienced climbers with good physical fitness and technical skills.

faqs.question: What permits do I need for Singu Chuli Peak Climbing?
faqs.answer: You will need to obtain both a Trekking Permit from the Annapurna Conservation Area Project (ACAP) and a Climbing Permit from the Nepal Mountaineering Association (NMA).

treks.title: Langtang Trek 8 Days
treks.description: This is one of the most popular trekking areas in Nepal. The Langtang National Park encompasses beautiful landscapes, meadows, and old monasteries. This trek will pleasantly surprise you as you walk past the forests savoring the stunning views of mountains, valleys, and glaciers. The Chortens, mani walls, and monasteries reflect the influence of the Buddhist religion in this peaceful region. The trek begins with a drive along the Trishuli River to Syabrubesi, an ancient trading route between Nepal and Tibet. As you walk past numerous forests, you might spot local wildlife like musk deers, Himalayan monal, tahrs, wild dogs, serows, or even snow leopards. Experience a hearty welcome from the local Tamang communities and witness majestic views of Langtang Lirung and the surrounding glaciers from Kyanjin Ri or Tserko Ri viewpoints.
highlights: Scenic private Jeep drive from Kathmandu to Syabrubesi.
Visit Langtang village and the ancient Kyanjin Gompa Monastery.
Panoramic mountain views from Kyanjin Ri (4,773m) and Tserko Ri (5,450m).
Snow-capped mountains, waterfalls, amazing Lirung and Kimshung glaciers, and several suspension bridges.
Lush green forests, meadows, and potential wildlife sightings (red panda, snow leopard, musk deer, bear, langur).
Encounter rich Tamang culture, heavily influenced by Tibetan Buddhism.

itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours passing through fertile jungles and rural settlements rich in bamboo and birch groves alongside the Langtang River to Lama Hotel.

itinerary.details: Trek 3-4 hours on an easier, shorter day to help acclimatize. Walk past yak pastures, mani walls, and arrive at the ancient monastery of Kyanjin Gompa.

itinerary.details: Acclimatize and explore! Visit the monastery, the local cheese factory, and hike up to Kyanjin Ri (4773m) or Tserko Ri (5450m) for incredible panoramic glacier views.

itinerary.details: Trek 6 hours retracing your steps downhill through the dense river valley forests, stopping for lunch at Ghoda Tabela, and sleeping at Lama Hotel.

itinerary.details: Take an early morning private Jeep drive (7-9 hours) back to Kathmandu, enjoying the terraced farmlands and river valleys one last time.
